nodes.label: annotate-source Skill
nodes.rationale: The platform's canonical data-model step: @annotate(concept, grain, roles, links) on each dlt resource drives staging generation, PII policy, monitors, metric candidates and graph edges. validate_annotations enforces concrete concepts, legal topology edges, money_amount/currency_code pairing, exactly one key column. Independent rewrite against dlt Core's public API; structure follows the vendored dlt-hub/dlthub-ai-workbench.

nodes.label: create-filesystem-pipeline Skill
nodes.rationale: Profile before scaffolding (never guess the schema); explicit file_glob; reader transformer per format; incremental on modification_date for accumulating landing zones; cloud credentials only via secrets_update_fragment.

nodes.label: create-sql-pipeline Skill
nodes.rationale: Explicit decisions required: list tables (never everything), monotonic incremental cursor (without it every run is a full copy), merge+primary_key for mutable tables vs append for immutable events, full_with_precision reflection when types matter, backfills through pf plan backfill.

nodes.label: find-source Skill
nodes.rationale: No hosted connector catalogue in dlt Core, so a three-tier ladder: verified sources (dlt init), OpenAPI-generated rest_api (dlt-init-openapi), hand-rolled rest_api. Always annotate, commit the connector back to the registry, never inline credentials. After first load, pf semantic scan induces an ontology proposal; the scan proposes, a human decides.

nodes.label: After the first load: propose the ontology
nodes.norm_label: after the first load: propose the ontology

nodes.label: steward-ontology Skill
nodes.rationale: Induction proposes vocabulary; the human steward makes the four judgements induction cannot: synonym detection (minting a synonym silently splits every downstream metric), business verb naming, PII confirmation (never pre-accepted at any confidence; a missing tag fails loudly which is the safer failure), and specialisation via parent. Approved terms go to the group's extension.yaml only; another company never inherits a word that means nothing to them.

nodes.label: The four judgements induction cannot make
nodes.norm_label: the four judgements induction cannot make

nodes.label: Things that should make you reject
nodes.norm_label: things that should make you reject

nodes.label: optimize-performance Skill
nodes.rationale: Diagnose before tuning via get_local_pipeline_state and load timings; symptom-to-lever table (parallelized extract, buffer/file rotation for memory, parquet loader format, load workers). Full reload every run usually means missing incremental. Never raise concurrency past the project's DuckDB writer pool.

nodes.label: setup-data-quality Skill
nodes.rationale: Two layers catch different failures: deterministic schema contracts at load time (DEFAULT_CONTRACT evolves tables/columns but freezes data_type; STRICT_CONTRACT for mature sources) and statistical monitors after load, generated from ontology roles by monitors_for, never hand-written. dbt tests catch nulls and duplicates; monitors catch the failure that costs money.

nodes.label: install-duckdb Skill
nodes.rationale: One pinned extension set (httpfs, json, spatial, excel) auto-loaded in Warehouse.connect. Adding an extension is a platform change affecting every company -- propose it, never apply from a project session; community extensions need explicit security review.

nodes.label: read-file Skill
nodes.rationale: Profile a data file before scaffolding a pipeline -- guessing a schema is how a filesystem source ends up all-VARCHAR. The profile (columns, types, null rates, keys, timestamps, money columns) feeds the pipeline scaffold and becomes the annotation roles.

nodes.label: read-memories Skill
nodes.rationale: Memories are scoped per-project on purpose: session logs stay inside the project so recovering context can never leak a sister's business logic. Prefer the context card and knowledge graph over log archaeology; reach for memories when the question is 'why was it done this way', which the graph cannot answer. Promotion into group or platform rules is a reviewed human step.

nodes.label: build-dashboard Skill
nodes.rationale: Start from the metric, never the chart; pick the chart form by the data's job; compose to the standard page anatomy; colour by job from the theme only. Non-negotiables: no dual-axis charts, selective labelling, one question per page. Adapted from the vendored evidence-bi upstream skill pack.

nodes.label: dashboard-loop Skill
nodes.rationale: Iterative draft-score-critique-fix loop that terminates because most of the quality bar is mechanically checkable by pf report audit; judgement questions are asked once per pass, not re-litigated. A pass that changes nothing is the signal to stop, not to look harder; rejected options are recorded in decisions/ so the next pass does not re-litigate them.

nodes.label: Exit conditions — stop when all hold
nodes.norm_label: exit conditions — stop when all hold

nodes.label: forge-ui Skill
nodes.rationale: Control plane is a Vite+React SPA served by the same FastAPI process as /api -- no second server, no SSR. Read the vendored Forge skill pack's props before writing a component: wss3-forge exports 358 names and guessed props fail to compile. theme.css adds only what a data console needs and Forge has no opinion about: monospace identifiers, tabular numerals, shared verdict colours.

nodes.label: Contributing Guide
nodes.rationale: Structural rules are stricter than most projects because the platform is multi-tenant and its audit trail is part of the product.

nodes.label: Vendor Directory Read-Only Rule
nodes.rationale: The 21 upstreams are pinned as submodules for provenance; what was adopted from each is recorded in platform/src/pf/vendor/registry.yaml. Bumping a pin is a maintainer decision made through the weekly sync PR, never part of a feature change.

nodes.label: Entity Isolation Rule
nodes.rationale: Business logic under groups/<group>/projects/<project>/ belongs to one entity. An assumption carried across entities is a bug, not a refactor — never copy logic between groups or sister projects.

nodes.label: Append-Only Provenance Rule
nodes.rationale: The action record in provenance/ is append-only and written by the platform's hooks; pf provenance verify blocks CI if the chain is broken. Agents may not edit the record of what they did.

nodes.label: Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Pre-1.0: only the latest commit on main is supported. Vulnerabilities are reported privately by email, never as public issues.

nodes.label: Provenance Tampering In Scope
nodes.rationale: Findings that allow tampering with or bypassing the hash-chained provenance log (provenance/, docs/GOVERNANCE.md) are in scope and treated as high severity — the audit trail is part of the product.

nodes.label: Credentials Live In The Environment
nodes.rationale: Credentials live only in the environment (.env, dlt secrets.toml) — never in the repository. A committed secret is itself a reportable finding.

nodes.label: Loop State
nodes.rationale: Written by pf loop run. High priority: jaffle/jaffle-shop onboarding at stage review (6/6 open, all 3 checks passed). Cadence and budgets live in LOOP.md, binding constraints in loop-constraints.md, path policy in gate.yaml.

nodes.label: Third-Party Notices
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0 repo pinning 21 upstreams as read-only submodules. Submodules are pointers, not copies — cloning without --recurse-submodules fetches no upstream code. The authoritative per-path record of every borrowing is platform/src/pf/vendor/registry.yaml (pf vendor list -v, pf vendor why <file>).

nodes.label: FINOS AI Governance Framework
nodes.rationale: CC BY 4.0 control/risk catalogue and mitigation vocabularies, read at runtime and partially copied into pf.air; credit line emitted in every generated register (pf/air/sources.py).

nodes.label: OpenTopology
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0. Relationship vocabulary taken verbatim (governed_by, implemented_by, verified_by); schema validated against in place, never copied.

nodes.label: WrenAI
nodes.rationale: MDL field names and cardinality enum taken from core/ (Apache-2.0). Tri-licensed with a pre-emptive AGPL-3.0: no path is AGPL yet, but a vendor pin bump moving paths onto AGPL-3.0 is the event to watch for — the drift gate (pf vendor drift) is the mechanism that surfaces it.

nodes.label: Recce Vendor Family
nodes.rationale: recce (Apache-2.0), recce-ui (Apache-2.0) and recce-pr-update (MIT) are pinned for contract, drift-watch or CLI invocation only — no material adapted into this repo.

nodes.label: recce-claude-plugin Licence Gap
nodes.rationale: Declares no license (verified against the GitHub API 2026-08-19), so default is all-rights-reserved and the ported recce-review skill is a derivative of unlicensed content. Sibling repos are Apache-2.0/MIT so this reads as upstream oversight; fix is an upstream licence request or an independent rewrite. Tracked in registry.yaml under licence_review.

nodes.label: loop-engineering
nodes.rationale: MIT. Loop building blocks adapted into pf/loops/.

nodes.label: asqav-compliance ELv2 Constraint
nodes.rationale: Elastic License 2.0, executed unmodified from its submodule in CI. ELv2 forbids providing the software as a managed service: the platform must not expose the scanner as a compliance-scanning feature to its own tenants. Recorded in registry.yaml under licence_review.

nodes.label: dlthub-ai-workbench
nodes.rationale: Proprietary dltHub License. No source copied — the dlt toolkits are independent rewrites against dlt Core's public Apache-2.0 API. Standing note: confirm scope-of-use with counsel.

nodes.label: Capability Path Policy
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf new-project --with and merged over gate.yaml at load time by pf.loops.gate.load_policy — edit the capability, not this file. Denylist covers generated/derived artefacts (recce state, evidence build, air-register, workflows); impact_required covers reporting pages, recce.yml, expectations and air.yaml.

nodes.label: Per-Project DuckDB Writer Pools
nodes.rationale: Every writing asset is tagged with a per-project pool (duckdb_writer_<project>) limited to 1, letting sister companies run in parallel while respecting DuckDB's single-writer lock. Granularity must be op, not run: run granularity serialises whole runs but lets every step inside one run execute at once — the three dlt ingest assets fired concurrently and collided on the single-writer lock. runs and pools must both live under concurrency as of Dagster 1.13.

nodes.label: acme-eu CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf bootstrap — hand-edits are lost on the next bootstrap; change the contributing capability (pf.capabilities or pf.tools.<tool>) instead. Concurrency group per PR: a superseding push cancels the in-flight run rather than racing it, since two builds writing the same baseline is how a review compares against the wrong state.

nodes.label: Per-Area Change Filter
nodes.rationale: The changes job diffs the PR once against the merge base (fetch-depth: 0 is load-bearing) and publishes one boolean per area (models/sources/transform/reporting/any); every downstream job guards on it, so touching a page never starts a dbt review. Adding a capability adds a job and nothing else.

nodes.label: AIR Baseline Merge Gate
nodes.rationale: pf air gate blocks only on controls the entity actually committed to in its air.yaml baseline; everything else in the catalogue is reported into the job summary without failing — the platform ships with known gaps and says so rather than hiding them behind a green check. submodules: true is load-bearing and unique to this job: the control catalogue is vendored (vendor/ai-governance-framework), and without it every control assesses as unexercised and the gate passes for the wrong reason.

nodes.label: Blast-Radius Impact Gate
nodes.rationale: Runs the same pf impact-gate as the developer's pre-commit hook, so a change that bypassed the local hook (--no-verify, web edit, bot commit) still cannot merge unreported. Gates against the BASE graph, not the branch: an added model is not in the base graph so has no blast radius and does not block, while a deleted model is still in the base graph so its consumers are found. pf kg build must parse the dbt project first — without a manifest every blast-radius query is empty and the gate passes because it found nothing, not because there is nothing.

nodes.label: Recce Data Review
nodes.rationale: Reviews what the change did to the data, not just to the DAG. DataRecce/PR-Update keeps the branch merged with its base; DataRecce/recce runs preset checks and writes the summary. autoMerge is deliberately false: a merge is a write to someone's branch, and the platform's rule is that automation reports while a human merges. The baseline is pulled from the artefact store (pf tool recce ci), keyed by base branch — it used to travel in the repo but stopped scaling at 30 MB per project. Without artefact-store secrets the job still runs and reports the review as not exercised rather than failing.

nodes.label: Bot Findings Workflow
nodes.rationale: Review findings outlive their pull request: a bot review comment dies with its PR, so each finding becomes an issue on the findings board, closed again when the review thread resolves, citing the fixing commit. Two speeds on purpose — track immediately as a comment lands, then reconcile the whole PR after every other pipeline completes and any running check settles. Concurrency is serialised per PR and the fingerprint makes a late run a no-op rather than a duplicate. Board writes need a PROJECTS_TOKEN PAT; without it issues are still filed and only the board step is skipped. Delegates to .github/scripts/bot_findings.py.

nodes.label: Claude Review Workflow
nodes.rationale: Deliberately label-gated (add the claude-review label) rather than running on every PR: it is billed per Anthropic API run, and the checks that must always happen already run unconditionally elsewhere — this one is for reviews needing judgement rather than a rule. The platform's own verdicts (pf gate, pf check) go into the prompt as evidence; Claude reviews what a rule cannot decide, and disagreeing with the gate is itself a finding. Review criteria: SQL semantics, semantic-layer drift, unmentioned blast radius, entity isolation, secrets/PII. Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exits with an explanation rather than failing red. Review only — no file modification.

nodes.label: PR Impact Report Workflow
nodes.rationale: Every PR gets one impact report comment edited in place — a thread of eleven stale reports is how a reviewer learns to ignore the bot. The same JSON is uploaded as an artifact so pf ui shows the verdict CI computed instead of recomputing and disagreeing. Submodules are fetched with --depth 1 --filter=blob:none, never via checkout's fetch-depth: 0 + submodules: recursive, which full-clones every upstream — that combination wedged PR #201 in actions/checkout for twelve hours and held the concurrency group. pf vendor drift degrades visibly ('<id> not checked out') on a partial fetch. Verdict enforcement is a separate step from posting, so the report is visible whether or not it blocks.

nodes.label: Vendor Sync Workflow
nodes.rationale: loop-engineering's dependency-sweeper pattern held at L1: fetch, report, open a PR — never run pf vendor approve, because approval means 'a human read the diff' and a workflow cannot mean that. The PR body names the exact files of ours to re-read, which is the whole reason the provenance registry exists. One long-lived vendor/sync branch is force-updated rather than a new branch per week, avoiding a graveyard of stale sync PRs. Runs Monday 06:00 cron or on dispatch.

nodes.label: Four-Layer Semantic Stack
nodes.rationale: policy.yaml (what must HOLD, OpenTopology, with controls: ids like AIR-DET-21), topology.yaml (how they RELATE, OWL object properties), concepts.yaml (what things ARE, OWL classes), annotations (where they LIVE, per project). Built in this order deliberately: a topology without identity cannot generate a join, and a policy without an ontology has nothing to attach to. The knowledge graph is the join of all four.

nodes.label: Graph Projections
nodes.rationale: Everything downstream is a projection of the knowledge graph, never a parallel hand-maintained file: WrenAI MDL (pf semantic mdl) for BI/text-to-SQL/agents, OWL/RDF-XML (pf semantic owl), the context card (pf kg card) as the agent's always-on index, and the impact report (pf impact) for the merge gate.

nodes.label: Relations As Nodes, Not Edges
nodes.rationale: A bare edge cannot carry a name, an inverse, or a binding. MDL requires relationships[].name, a reverse-reading agent needs inverse, and the physical join must be bound to an actual foreign-key column — so a relation is a node with domain_of/range_of edges into it and a realises edge from the implementing column.

nodes.label: Derived Join Conditions
nodes.rationale: Nothing is guessed from a naming convention: a column realises a relation, the relation's range class carries an identity column, and the join condition plus cardinality fall out — cardinality is inverted when the foreign key sits on the range side, since the FK is always on the many side.

nodes.label: WrenAI MDL Projection
nodes.rationale:
pf semantic mdl emits a manifest validated against core/wren-mdl/mdl.schema.json from Canner/WrenAI, written to groups//projects/

/mdl/mdl.json. Adopting Wren repeats no modelling work because the manifest is generated from the same graph agents already query. pf.role, pf.pii (drives masking), pf.relation, pf.also_realises, grain and layer are carried in MDL properties so nothing is lost in translation.

nodes.label: Control Plane Stack
nodes.rationale: OpenMetadata, Dagster and recce on one database, one origin (nginx at :8080) and one image — everything above the database line runs in one container, pf_stack, while Postgres and Elasticsearch stay separate because folding a database into an application image is how you lose the database. PF_REPO must be the repo root and is bind-mounted at its host path, because Dagster's workspace holds absolute working_directory entries. Code servers are standalone grpc_server processes (a python_module entry forks per-location children in both webserver and daemon — 19 processes, 3.1 GB); recce servers (~350 MB each) start only where there is a review. Recce state lives in R2 via pf artifacts, not in a database.

nodes.label: One Database, Two Schemas
nodes.rationale: openmetadata_db holds OpenMetadata (public, ~176 tables) and Dagster (dagster schema, owned by a role with no rights in public). Dagster has no schema setting, so search_path is urlencoded onto the libpq connection string via params/options. Dropping that one parameter does not fail — Dagster's migrations run happily against public, interleaving tables with OpenMetadata's, and the damage only shows at the next OpenMetadata upgrade. Unset PF_STACK_PG_HOST means SQLite, and pf stack render removes the storage block entirely rather than pointing at an unreachable Postgres, which would fail at import and take every code location down.

nodes.label: Path-Based Origin Merge
nodes.rationale: OpenMetadata's UI and recce's UI are both root-anchored SPAs; recce's Next.js static export has no basePath so a path-prefixed proxy renders its 404. The merge happens on paths instead: /api/v1/ is OpenMetadata's API, /api/ is recce's, and nginx's ^~ on /api/v1/ is the one rule holding the two APIs apart. /recce/<project> sets a pf_recce cookie that an nginx map turns into a port — one project in view at a time, which is what a review is. The injected navigation bar loads via sub_filter from /pf/bar.css and /pf/bar.js because OpenMetadata's CSP would drop an inline script. Stated cost: root routes /lineage, /checks, /query now belong to recce.

nodes.label: Self-Decrypting Catalogue Credential
nodes.rationale: catalog_sync authenticates to OpenMetadata as the ingestion bot. Inside the stack the publisher and server share a database and FERNET_KEY, so the entrypoint decrypts the bot's JWT from user_entity once at start and exports it — a credential nobody typed, held in the process environment and written nowhere. An explicit OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN still wins, so a narrower bot or remote catalogue is never silently replaced; outside the stack the env var remains the only source. Upstream trap: OpenMetadata 1.13.3's Postgres DDL generates isbot from json->>'deleted', so the bot flag is read out of the JSON instead.

nodes.label: Acme Group Skills Scope
nodes.rationale: Skills here encode acme's domain knowledge (a reconciliation procedure, a regulatory workflow, a naming rule the ontology cannot express) shared by every sister project. Infra skills come from platform/toolkits and must not be duplicated here.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Eval Ownership
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; evals are their tests. Platform tier owns health checks and templates, the group tier owns what every sister agrees on (ontology instance, conformed dimensions, group metrics), the project tier owns one entity's business logic. Placement rule: a case belongs at group level when it would be wrong for a sister to disagree with it; if one sister could legitimately answer differently, it is a project case. Any change to an agent prompt must keep these green.

nodes.label: Acme Group Card
nodes.rationale: Generated group index (2026-08-19). Three sister projects (acme-eu, acme-rollup, acme-us) share the ontology (Customer, Organization, Subscription, Payment, Usage, Product), conformed dimensions and group metrics, but have separate warehouses and run in parallel. Cross-entity questions are answered only in the rollup project, which attaches sister databases READ_ONLY — never read a sister project's files.

nodes.label: Stripe Ontology Proposal (2026-08-13)
nodes.rationale: Draft induced from the stripe source in acme/acme-us; nothing is in effect until pf ontology approve. Approval merges accepted axioms into groups/acme/ontology/extension.yaml and rebuilds the knowledge graph, MDL manifest and reporting for every project in the group — the platform ontology is never modified by group approval. Every axiom carries evidence and rationale so reviewers disagree with the reasoning, not just the conclusion.

nodes.label: Charge
nodes.rationale: New class proposed from table stripe.charges (1,800 rows): a table at a consistent grain proposes an entity. Identity id accepted because without an identity no join condition can be derived and every BI/MDL projection would be a guess. Carries money_amount+currency_code pair, status_enum, event_time created.

nodes.label: Customer
nodes.rationale: Reused existing ontology class rather than minting a synonym — reuse is the whole point of a shared vocabulary. The scanned identity conflicts with the curated one and is rejected: accepting it would replace a deliberate decision with a source detail.

nodes.label: Subscription
nodes.rationale: Reused existing ontology class; scanned identity conflicts with the curated identity and is rejected for the same reason as Customer. Carries plan/status enums, mrr_amount+currency pair, started_at/canceled_at event times.

nodes.label: PII Email Role Proposal
nodes.rationale: pii_email roles (Charge.receipt_email, Customer.email) are proposed but never auto-applied: a wrong PII tag carries authority it did not earn, and a missing one fails the mart policy loudly — so the default is accept: false pending human judgement.

nodes.label: Session Memory Notes
nodes.rationale: One lesson per file, written mid-task by agents. Promotion into groups/acme/CLAUDE.md (group-wide) or a platform RULES.md (universal) is a reviewed, human step — that promotion is what makes the platform compound instead of accumulating notes nobody reads.

nodes.label: Snowflake Metadata Ingestion Config
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata) from tools.yaml, pf.runtime.targets and dbt artefacts — never hand-edited. Credentials are env-var references (SNOWFLAKE_*, OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN); no secret is in the file. Publishes serviceName acme_acme_eu to the OpenMetadata server.

nodes.label: dbt Metadata Ingestion Config
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata). Feeds dbt manifest/catalog/run_results from transform/target into OpenMetadata service acme_acme_eu; dbtUpdateDescriptions false so the ontology, not dbt, owns meaning.

nodes.label: AIR Control Gate
nodes.rationale: pf air gate acme acme-eu blocks the merge when a control this project committed to is not enforced. Controls come from whichever catalogues are registered; pf air coverage derives — never stores — whether each control's enforcement resolves.

nodes.label: air.yaml Baseline Declaration
nodes.rationale: Hand-written and carries the judgement: baseline controls block the merge; accepted controls require reason and owner because an acceptance without them is a gap with better formatting. A project may add to its group's baseline but cannot remove from it — the only way to drop a control is accepted:, which leaves a name attached to the decision.

nodes.label: Generated AIR Register
nodes.rationale: governance/air-register.md is derived from air.yaml plus a fresh coverage run and is on the gate denylist — hand-editing it would make it disagree with the declaration it came from. It carries the credit line of every catalogue actually loaded, so a catalogue swapped out takes its obligation with it and one added brings its own.

nodes.label: Elementary Observability
nodes.rationale: Every dbt build records run results, test results (dbt's own, dbt-expectations', everyone's), model timings and schema snapshots into the main_elementary schema — observability is queryable tables with history, not a log that scrolled away. The CLI is installed isolated because it cannot share a lockfile with recce; transform/edr_target/ is a build artefact and gate-denied like target/.

nodes.label: Elementary Anomaly Tests
nodes.rationale: volume_anomalies, freshness_anomalies etc. are deliberately not generated: an anomaly threshold is a judgement about one table's behaviour, so it is declared in the model's own yml where that judgement lives. The elementary-observe skills (add-anomaly-tests, triage-observability) are the how; results land in the same tables and the same report.

nodes.label: Generated Expectations Floor
nodes.rationale: transform/tests/expectations/ holds dbt-expectations tests derived from the ontology via the chain annotations.yaml (column→role) → knowledge graph (role+pii per mart column) → generated test. The floor asserts only universals — an annotated mart must not be empty; its declared identity must be unique and never null — because anything sharper is a judgement about one table and belongs in that model's yml. Edit the roles, not the generated files.

nodes.label: Impact Gate CI Check
nodes.rationale: pf impact-gate runs on every PR touching this project's models or sources; a breaking blast radius fails the check and names the exposure owners. It needs no token because it runs inside the repo's own CI — write-scoped automation is kept a separate capability so the gate cannot be talked out of a verdict by the thing it is gating.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Catalogue Projection
nodes.rationale: The catalogue is where someone who does not read YAML finds what a table means. It is a projection, not a sync: nothing is read back, and a change made in the catalogue UI is overwritten on the next publish on purpose — the ontology is canonical and stays in git where pf check and the gate can judge it. We publish what tables mean (glossary terms, role tags, PII.Sensitive, relatedTerms); dbt publishes what they are (tables, columns, lineage via metadata ingest-dbt).

nodes.label: Recce Review
nodes.rationale: pf impact says what could break; Recce says what did change — baseline capture, rebuild, diff, serve. transform/recce_state.json and target-base/ are gate-denied for the same reason target/ is: hand-editing a recorded diff makes the review lie. The recce_review Dagster asset runs downstream of the marts; the single-pane view lives in pf ui → Review because Dagster OSS has no custom-tab extension point.

nodes.label: Recce Config Generation
nodes.rationale: transform/recce.yml is derived from contracts/annotations.yaml — a natural_key role becomes a value-diff primary key, a money_amount becomes a profile diff. Edit the roles, not the config; pf bootstrap regenerates it.

nodes.label: Recce Artefact Store
nodes.rationale: Baselines and reviews live in the artefact store, not git: the baseline is published under the ref it was built from, the review under the branch under review. With no store configured everything stays local — right on a laptop that built its own baseline ten seconds ago; in CI a runner has code and no warehouse, so an unconfigured store means the review reports not-exercised rather than green.

nodes.label: DuckDB-Dev / Snowflake-Prod Strategy
nodes.rationale: A developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project: every target but prod is a local DuckDB file, so dbt build works on a laptop, offline, with no credentials — and base exists so Recce has a second state to diff against. Only prod points at Snowflake and nothing can move dev/ci/base, by construction. There is deliberately no shortcut for DBT_TARGET=prod: the failure mode — believing you are on dev and being on prod — is worse than the typing.

nodes.label: Dialect Portability Gate
nodes.rationale: The sf_* macros in platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake dispatch per adapter so a model is written once and compiles to whatever the target understands. pf align validate --stage dialect is the gate that says whether the project is actually portable or merely untested — declaring the target does not make the models run on Snowflake; that gate passing is what does.

nodes.label: MDL Semantic Manifest
nodes.rationale: mdl/mdl.json is the project's semantic layer in MDL, the interchange format a BI or text-to-SQL layer consumes without being told our internals — generated from the knowledge graph by pf bootstrap, never hand-edited. There is no Wren web UI: upstream's chat-first Docker app is legacy/v1; current WrenAI is a CLI plus wren serve, which serves MCP, and the semantic surface is pf ui → Semantics. Nothing is being iframed because there is nothing to iframe.

nodes.label: Workspace Review Join
nodes.rationale: pf ui → Workspace joins the MDL manifest to Recce's recorded diff on the model behind each entity, so 'fct_revenue moved' is read as which semantic entity changed and which ontology roles ride on it — a diff read as published meaning, not a list of dbt node names. Needs both the wren and recce tools; both are on by default for a new group.

nodes.label: Eval Corpus
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests. Hand-written cases encode acme-eu's own business rules no toolkit could guess; the 'why' field is not decoration — without it a corpus decays into assertions nobody dares change. Prose matchers stay weak (contains_any, not exact strings): a case that pins wording fails on a harmless rewrite, and a suite that cries wolf gets switched off — which costs more than the case was ever worth. --samples N exposes unstable prompts: passing 4 in 5 is neither passing nor failing. Nothing here is read by a sister project. Target agents: test_failure_triage, freshness_triage, metric_gap_proposer.

nodes.label: Generated Eval Cases
nodes.rationale: generated/ is written by pf evals-gen: toolkit eval templates — the shape of a correct judgement with placeholders — resolved against this project's knowledge graph so cases name this project's models and columns. Regenerating overwrites the directory and deletes anything whose template is gone; never hand-edit a file in it.

nodes.label: Evidence Capability Card
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf context build from the Capability declaration, never edited directly. States the reporting contract for agents: every number traces to a compiled metric — a missing figure is a missing metric definition, not a page to write SQL into; never edit reporting/queries/metrics/; ratio metrics re-divide as sum(num)/sum(den), never avg(ratio).

nodes.label: Evidence BI Reporting
nodes.rationale: BI-as-code generated by pf report build via the pipeline dbt marts → MetricFlow metrics → MDL → queries/metrics/*.sql → pages/*.md. The one rule: pages never restate business logic — every number traces to a compiled metric, because two pages filtering differently is how one company ends up with two revenues. Generated pages are overwritten on regeneration; durable narrative belongs in an owned page or the metric description.

nodes.label: Evidence Theme Config
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build; DuckDB datasource plus categorical/status palettes. Palette values are validated — adjacent-pair CVD deltaE >= 8, normal-vision >= 15, contrast checked on both surfaces — because re-picking them by eye makes charts unreadable for ~8% of readers.

nodes.label: acme-eu Overview Page
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build; a projection of the metric definitions in transform/models/semantic/. Every number on the page is a governed metric compiled into queries/metrics/.

nodes.label: Active Customers Page
nodes.rationale: Customers with at least one active subscription, unfiltered, measured over created_at from dim_customers; dimensioned by customer_segment. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer and compiled to queries/metrics/ — the page does not restate it.

nodes.label: Average Order Value Page
nodes.rationale: Revenue divided by succeeded payment count, restricted to payment_status = 'succeeded', over paid_at from fct_payments — carried as revenue / payment_count so it re-divides correctly at any grain. Aggregated as sum(revenue)/sum(payment_count); averaging the ratio itself gives a different — and wrong — answer.

nodes.label: Gross Payment Volume Page
nodes.rationale: All payment attempts regardless of outcome, unfiltered — every row in the underlying fact counts — measured over paid_at from fct_payments; dimensioned by payment_status.

nodes.label: Payment Count Page
nodes.rationale: Count of succeeded payments, restricted to payment_status = 'succeeded', measured over paid_at from fct_payments.

nodes.label: Revenue Page
nodes.rationale: Net revenue — succeeded payments only. The single definition, restricted to payment_status = 'succeeded', measured over paid_at from fct_payments.

nodes.label: Revenue MoM Growth Page
nodes.rationale: Month-over-month change in net revenue, restricted to payment_status = 'succeeded', measured over paid_at from fct_payments.

nodes.label: acme_eu DuckDB reporting connection
nodes.rationale: One warehouse file per project is what lets sister companies run in parallel; the reporting layer only ever reads.

nodes.label: elementary edr profile
nodes.rationale: Derived from the project profile by pf tool elementary: one elementary output per project target, schema suffixed the way dbt composes custom schemas. Regenerated by pf bootstrap - retarget the project, not this block.

nodes.label: base comparison target
nodes.rationale: The comparison environment for a diff tool must be a separate materialisation: pointing a review tool at two sets of dbt artefacts that resolve to the same relation makes every value diff compare a table with itself and report clean - a false negative on every change, worse than having no review at all.

nodes.label: fct_revenue mart
nodes.rationale: Daily revenue by segment and plan, kept union-compatible across sister projects so the group rollup can union them.

nodes.label: exec_weekly_dashboard exposure
nodes.rationale: Weekly exec revenue review read by the CFO every Monday; owned by Finance.

nodes.label: crm_customer_sync exposure
nodes.rationale: Reverse-ETL of customer health back into the CRM; owned by RevOps.

nodes.label: revenue metric
nodes.rationale: Net revenue - succeeded payments only. The single definition.

nodes.label: acme-rollup project context
nodes.rationale: Conventions: annotate every dlt resource before writing models; marts declare meta.grain while the semantic layer owns aggregation policy; ask the graph before reading files; run impact_analysis before changing a column, model or metric.

nodes.label: acme-rollup AI controls declaration
nodes.rationale: baseline is a union with the group's air.yaml, not a replacement - an entity may commit to more than its family, never to less. accepted requires reason and owner: an acceptance without a reason is a gap with better formatting, one without an owner is a decision nobody can be asked about. The --suggest baseline proposes only what already passes - a ratchet against regression rather than a wall of work.

nodes.label: Snowflake metadata ingestion workflow
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata); rewritten from tools.yaml, pf.runtime.targets and dbt artefacts. Credentials are env-var references - no secret in the file.

nodes.label: dbt artefact ingestion workflow
nodes.rationale: Publishes dbt manifest/catalog/run_results into OpenMetadata; generated by pf bootstrap, never hand-edited.

nodes.label: pf air gate
nodes.rationale: Blocks the merge only on controls the project committed to in air.yaml; everything else is reported and advisory. A project may add to its group's baseline but cannot remove from it - the way to drop a control is accepted:, which leaves a name attached to the decision.

nodes.label: governance/air-register.md (generated)
nodes.rationale: Derived from air.yaml plus a fresh coverage run and gate-denylisted - hand-editing it would make it disagree with the declaration it came from. Credit lines are collected from the catalogues actually loaded rather than templated, so a swapped catalogue takes its obligation with it.

nodes.label: Elementary observability package
nodes.rationale: Every dbt build records itself: on-run-start/on-run-end hooks write run results, test results, model timings and schema snapshots into main_elementary beside the marts. Observability is queryable tables with history, not a log that scrolled away. The edr CLI installs isolated - it cannot share a lockfile with recce.

nodes.label: Elementary anomaly tests
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not generated: an anomaly threshold is a judgement about one table's behaviour, so it is declared in the model's own yml where that judgement lives.

nodes.label: generated expectations floor
nodes.rationale: Tests derived from the ontology: annotations.yaml maps column to role, the knowledge graph resolves role plus pii per mart column, the tool maps what the role asserts to a dbt-expectations test. Only universal assertions are generated (an annotated mart must not be empty; its declared identity must be unique and never null) - anything sharper is a judgement about one table and belongs in that model's yml. Edit the roles, not the generated files.

nodes.label: pf impact-gate CI check
nodes.rationale: Runs on every PR touching the project's models or sources; a breaking blast radius fails the check and names the exposure owners. Tokenless by design - it reads nothing beyond the diff, because the whole point of the gate is that it cannot be talked out of a verdict by the thing it is gating. Write-scoped automation must be a separate capability.

nodes.label: Recce dbt review
nodes.rationale: pf impact says what could break; Recce says what did change. recce_state.json and target-base/ are gate-denied build artefacts because hand-editing a recorded diff makes the review lie.

nodes.label: recce.yml generation from ontology roles
nodes.rationale: transform/recce.yml is derived from contracts/annotations.yaml: a natural_key role becomes a value-diff primary key, a money_amount becomes a profile diff. Edit the roles, not the config; pf bootstrap regenerates it.

nodes.label: artefact store for baselines and reviews
nodes.rationale: Baseline published under the ref it was built from; the recorded review under the branch under review. With no store configured everything stays local - right on a laptop, wrong in CI, where a runner has code and no warehouse, so an unconfigured store means the review reports not-exercised rather than green.
nodes.norm_label: artefact store for baselines and reviews

nodes.label: Snowflake production warehouse
nodes.rationale: Only the prod target points at Snowflake; the target is named on every invocation because believing you are on dev while on prod is worse than the typing. Declaring the target does not make models run on Snowflake - the dialect gate passing is what does.

nodes.label: DuckDB local development
nodes.rationale: A developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project; every target but prod is a local DuckDB file so dbt build works on a laptop, offline, with no credentials, in seconds. Nothing in the warehouse capability can move dev, ci or base, by construction.

nodes.label: sf_* adapter-dispatch macros
nodes.rationale: Macros in platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake dispatch per adapter so a model is written once and compiles to whatever the target understands.

nodes.label: Dialect portability gate (pf align validate --stage dialect)
nodes.rationale: The gate is what says whether the project is actually portable or merely untested.
nodes.norm_label: dialect portability gate (pf align validate --stage dialect)

nodes.label: Environment-variable credentials
nodes.rationale: Credentials are read from the environment at run time and never written to a file: profiles.yml holds env_var calls, not values, because it is committed. Key-pair auth is the default; pf doctor reports what is missing.

nodes.label: Wren MDL semantic layer (mdl/mdl.json)
nodes.rationale: MDL is the interchange format a BI or text-to-SQL layer consumes without being told internals; generated from the knowledge graph by pf bootstrap, never hand-edited.

nodes.label: Workspace semantic-diff review
nodes.rationale: pf ui -> Workspace joins the MDL manifest to Recce's recorded diff on the model behind each entity, so 'fct_revenue moved' is read as which semantic entity changed and which ontology roles ride on it. Needs the recce tool on; both are on by default for a new group.

nodes.label: Hand-written business-rule eval cases
nodes.rationale: Cases encoding this entity's own business rules that no toolkit could have guessed. Nothing here is read by a sister, and nothing a sister writes is read here. The why field is required because a corpus without it decays into assertions nobody dares change.

nodes.label: Keep prose matchers weak
nodes.rationale: A case that pins wording fails on a harmless rewrite, and a suite that cries wolf gets switched off - which costs more than the case was ever worth. Use contains_any, not exact strings.

nodes.label: Prompt stability via --samples
nodes.rationale: A case that passes 4 times in 5 is not passing and not failing - it is an unstable prompt, which is the most useful thing the suite can tell you before a prompt change ships.

nodes.label: AI risk register - acme/acme-rollup
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf air register from air.yaml; derived from the repository on every run so no verdict is stored; the path is on the gate denylist and hand-edits are discarded. Coverage: 11 of 23 controls enforced, 9 not enforced, 3 unexercised. Catalogue pinned at 274760ccd058.

nodes.label: elementary edr profile

Derived from the project profile by pf tool elementary: one elementary output per project target, schema suffixed the way dbt composes custom schemas. Regenerated by pf bootstrap - retarget the project, not this block.

PII-role columns are excluded from every value-level check because results land in recce_state.json, which is durable and shared.

nodes.label: ADR decision log

nodes.label: pf air gate (merge-blocking control gate)
nodes.rationale: Blocks the merge when a control the project committed to in air.yaml is not enforced; everything outside the baseline is reported and advisory. A project may add to its group's baseline; it cannot remove from it - the way to drop a control is accepted:, which leaves a name attached to the decision.

nodes.label: Generated register discipline
nodes.rationale: governance/air-register.md is derived from air.yaml plus a fresh coverage run and is on the gate denylist - hand-editing it would make it disagree with the declaration it came from. It carries the credit line of every catalogue actually loaded, so a catalogue swapped out takes its obligation with it, and one added brings its own.

nodes.label: Elementary data observability
nodes.rationale: Every dbt build records itself: the elementary-data/elementary package hooks on-run-start/on-run-end and writes run results, test results, model timings and schema snapshots into the main_elementary schema beside the marts. Observability is queryable tables with history, not a log that scrolled away.

nodes.label: Anomaly tests are declared, not generated
nodes.rationale: An anomaly threshold is a judgement about one table's behaviour, so declare it in the model's own yml where that judgement lives - deliberately not generated. The elementary-observe skills (add-anomaly-tests, triage-observability) are the how.
nodes.norm_label: anomaly tests are declared, not generated

nodes.label: elementary_report Dagster asset
nodes.rationale: Runs downstream of the project's marts and attaches the report link. The recording itself has no asset - it happens inside every dbt build already.

nodes.label: Isolated edr CLI install
nodes.rationale: report and serve need the CLI, installed isolated because it cannot share a lockfile with recce: uv tool install elementary-data[duckdb]==0.25.*. Recording needs nothing - the package rides inside dbt.

nodes.label: pf impact-gate PR Check
nodes.rationale: Runs on every PR touching this project's models or sources; a breaking blast radius fails the check and names exposure owners. Deliberately tokenless — it cannot open PRs, comment, or read beyond the diff — because a gate that holds write scopes can be talked out of a verdict by the thing it is gating. Write-scoped automation must be a separate capability.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Catalogue Projection
nodes.rationale: One-way projection, not a sync: concepts.yaml becomes glossary terms, ontology roles become PlatformRole/PII.Sensitive tags, topology relations become relatedTerms, recce checks become test cases carrying the review verdict; dbt target/*.json supplies tables and lineage via metadata ingest-dbt. Nothing is read back — catalogue-UI edits are overwritten on the next publish on purpose, because the ontology is canonical and stays in git where pf check and the gate can judge it. We publish what tables mean; dbt publishes what they are.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata JWT Credential Discipline
nodes.rationale: OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN must be set wherever ingestion runs; it is a credential and is never written into a generated file. Host and service name come from tools.yaml, defaulting to http://localhost:8585 and acme_acme-us.

nodes.label: Recce Baseline-Diff Review Loop
nodes.rationale: pf impact says what could break; Recce says what did change. Loop: build green, capture baseline, change a model, rebuild, diff against baseline, read in the Recce UI. recce_state.json and target-base/ are gate-denied build artefacts because hand-editing a recorded diff makes the review lie.

nodes.label: Recce Artefact Store Publication
nodes.rationale: Baselines and reviews live in the artefact store, not git: the baseline is published under the ref it was built from, the recorded review under the branch under review. Unconfigured store is fine on a laptop that built its own baseline, but in CI a runner has code and no warehouse, so no store means the review reports 'not exercised' rather than falsely green.

nodes.label: recce_review Dagster Asset
nodes.rationale: Runs downstream of this project's marts and attaches the diff summary plus a Recce UI link to the run. Dagster OSS has no custom-tab extension point, so the single-pane view lives in pf ui -> Review, which embeds Recce beside the lineage the platform already tracks.

nodes.label: DuckDB Dev / Snowflake Prod Dual Target
nodes.rationale: One set of models serves both warehouses via sf_* adapter-dispatch macros. Development stays on DuckDB because a developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project — every target but prod is a local file that builds offline in seconds, and base exists so Recce has a second state to diff against. There is deliberately no shortcut for prod: DBT_TARGET=prod is named on every invocation because believing you are on dev while on prod is worse than the typing.
nodes.norm_label: duckdb dev / snowflake prod dual target

nodes.label: Dialect Portability Gate
nodes.rationale: pf align validate --stage dialect is the gate that says whether the project is actually portable or merely untested. Declaring the Snowflake target does not make the models run on Snowflake; that gate passing is what does.

nodes.label: Snowflake Credentials via Environment
nodes.rationale: Credentials are read from the environment at run time and never written to a file — transform/profiles.yml holds env_var calls, not values, because it is committed. Key-pair auth by default (SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH); password only when key-pair is unavailable. pf doctor reports which are missing; never paste one into a chat, a model file, or the repository.

nodes.label: MDL Semantic Layer Manifest
nodes.rationale: mdl/mdl.json is the project's semantic layer in MDL, the interchange format a BI or text-to-SQL layer consumes without being told internals. Generated from the knowledge graph by pf bootstrap — never hand-edited. There is no Wren web UI: upstream's chat-first Docker app is legacy/v1; current WrenAI is a CLI plus 'wren serve' which serves MCP, so the semantic surface is pf ui -> Semantics reading this same manifest.

nodes.label: Workspace Review-Semantics Join
nodes.rationale: pf ui -> Workspace joins the MDL manifest to Recce's recorded diff on the model behind each entity, so 'fct_revenue moved' reads as which published semantic entity changed and which ontology roles ride on it, rather than a list of dbt node names. Needs both the wren and recce tools on; both are on by default for a new group.

nodes.label: acme-us Eval Corpus
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests. generated/ is overwritten by pf evals-gen and never hand-edited; everything else encodes acme-us's own business rules no toolkit could guess. Each case's 'why' field is mandatory because without it a corpus decays into assertions nobody dares change. Prose matchers stay weak (contains_any, not exact strings) — a case that pins wording fails on harmless rewrites and a suite that cries wolf gets switched off. --samples N exposes unstable prompts: passing 4 of 5 is neither passing nor failing. Targets agents test_failure_triage, freshness_triage, metric_gap_proposer; nothing here is read by a sister project.

nodes.label: pf evals-gen Template Grounding
nodes.rationale: Toolkits ship eval templates — the shape of a correct judgement with placeholders where table names go. Generation resolves those against this project's knowledge graph so cases name this project's models and columns. Regenerating overwrites generated/ and deletes anything whose template is gone.

nodes.label: AIR Coverage Register
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf air register from air.yaml and derived from the repository on every run — no verdict is stored, the path is gate-denied. 11 of 23 controls enforced, 9 not enforced, 3 unexercised (evidence resolves but has produced nothing). The committed baseline is empty, so pf air gate cannot block on it. Per-regime counts (EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST, IOSCO, ATR) are counted from the same verdicts so they cannot disagree. Catalogue pinned at 274760ccd058.

nodes.label: Evidence Capability Declaration
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf context build from the Capability declaration. Declares that this project publishes dashboards as code: every number traces to a compiled metric, a missing figure is a missing metric definition, queries/metrics/ is compiled from the semantic layer and never edited, and ratio metrics re-divide as sum(num)/sum(den).

nodes.label: Evidence BI-as-Code Pipeline
nodes.rationale: dbt marts -> MetricFlow metrics -> MDL -> queries/metrics/*.sql -> pages/*.md, generated by pf report build and never hand-maintained. Generated: queries/metrics/*.sql, pages/index.md, pages/metrics/*.md, sources/*/, evidence.config.yaml. Yours: extra hand-written pages, components/. Regenerating overwrites generated pages, so durable narrative belongs in an owned page or the metric description.

nodes.label: Pages Never Restate Business Logic
nodes.rationale: Every number traces to a metric compiled into queries/metrics/. If a dashboard needs a figure that does not exist, the fix is a metric definition in transform/models/semantic/, then pf report build — never SQL in a page. Two pages filtering differently is how one company ends up with two revenues.

nodes.label: Ratio Re-Division Rule
nodes.rationale: Ratio queries carry numerator and denominator so a page re-divides at its own grain: sum(num)/sum(den). Never avg(ratio) — it is wrong at every grain except the one it was computed at, and it is the most common BI bug there is.

nodes.label: Evidence Project Configuration
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build; declares the @evidence-dev/duckdb datasource plugin and a validated chart theme. Palette values are checked — adjacent-pair CVD deltaE >= 8, normal-vision >= 15, contrast verified on both light and dark surfaces — because re-picking them by eye makes charts unreadable for roughly 8% of readers.

nodes.label: acme-us Overview Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Loads all six compiled metric queries; KPI grid, revenue trend, payment-status breakdown. AOV KPI re-divides as sum(revenue)/nullif(sum(payment_count),0) rather than averaging a ratio. The date_bounds query unions min() and max() into one column because DateRange reads both bounds from rows of a single column, not two columns of one row. A projection of the semantic layer — regenerated by pf report build.

nodes.label: Active Customers Metric Page
nodes.rationale: Customers with at least one active subscription, unfiltered, measured over created_at from dim_customers; broken down by customer_segment. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer and compiled to queries/metrics/.

nodes.label: Average Order Value Metric Page
nodes.rationale: Ratio metric: revenue divided by succeeded payment count, restricted to payment_status = 'succeeded', measured over paid_at from fct_payments. Carried as revenue/payment_count columns so any grain re-divides as sum(revenue)/sum(payment_count); averaging the ratio itself gives a different and wrong answer.

nodes.label: Gross Payment Volume Metric Page
nodes.rationale: All payment attempts regardless of outcome, unfiltered, measured over paid_at from fct_payments; broken down by payment_status.

nodes.label: Payments Metric Page
nodes.rationale: Count of succeeded payments, restricted to payment_status = 'succeeded', measured over paid_at from fct_payments.

nodes.label: Revenue Metric Page
nodes.rationale: Net revenue — succeeded payments only. The single definition, restricted to payment_status = 'succeeded', measured over paid_at from fct_payments.

nodes.label: Revenue MoM Growth Metric Page
nodes.rationale: Month-over-month change in net revenue (derived metric), restricted to payment_status = 'succeeded', measured over paid_at from fct_payments.
