The way to change a check is to fix what the column means — a wrong check is a wrong role. PII-role columns are excluded from every value-level check because results land in recce_state.json, which is durable and shared. Suite: row_count_diff and schema_diff for all modified tables; value_diff keyed on natural keys (dim_customers/customer_id, fct_payments/payment_id); profile_diff on money and count columns; query_diff category-drift checks on categorical columns, because a category that appears or disappears breaks an accepted_values test downstream without moving the row count.

nodes.label: fct_payments (mart)
nodes.rationale: Payment fact kept at attempt grain; which payment statuses count as revenue is deliberately a semantic-layer policy, not baked into the mart.

nodes.label: fct_revenue (mart)
nodes.rationale: Daily revenue by segment and plan, kept union-compatible across sister projects so the group rollup can union them.

nodes.label: revenue (metric)
nodes.rationale: The single definition of net revenue: succeeded payments only. The status policy lives in the metric filter, not in the mart, so every consumer inherits the same revenue recognition rule.

nodes.label: exec_weekly (saved query)
nodes.rationale: Materialized as a table (export exec_weekly_summary into schema reporting) so BI reads a table while the numbers still derive from the single metric definitions.

nodes.label: payments (semantic model)
nodes.rationale: agg_time_dimension (paid_at) derives from the event_time role. Owns measures payment_amount and payment_count.

nodes.label: customers (semantic model)
nodes.rationale: Owns measures customer_count and active_customer_count.

nodes.label: stg_stripe__charges (staging model)
nodes.rationale: Revenue source of record, cleaned 1:1 from stripe.charges at one-payment-attempt grain. Maps to ontology concept Payment; receipt_email is flagged PII.

nodes.label: stg_stripe__customers (staging model)
nodes.rationale: Maps to ontology concept Customer; customer_email and customer_name are flagged PII.

nodes.label: stg_stripe__subscriptions (staging model)
nodes.rationale: Maps to ontology concept Subscription; carries plan_tier and mrr_amount at one-subscription grain.

nodes.label: stripe (dbt source)
nodes.rationale: Raw data landed by dlt; schema is owned by the source, not the transform layer.

nodes.label: metricflow_time_spine (utility model)
nodes.rationale: Daily time spine required by MetricFlow; materialized as a table with date_day at day granularity.

nodes.label: Generated expectations floor (acme-us)
nodes.rationale: GENERATED-marked *.sql tests are derived from the ontology: contracts/annotations.yaml maps columns to roles, and pf bootstrap translates what those roles assert into dbt-expectations tests. Edit the roles, not the files — regeneration discards edits and deletes tests whose model or role has gone. Sharper expectations (ranges, accepted sets, distributions) are judgements about one table and belong in that model's own yml.

nodes.label: acme_shared (dbt project)
nodes.rationale: Platform cleaning macros are loaded as root-project macros via macro-paths, not as a dbt package: pf gen-staging emits unqualified pf_clean calls and pf_clean dispatches to its clean_* siblings unqualified too; dbt namespaces package macros, so a pf.-prefixed call would still fail on the inner dispatch.

nodes.label: globex AIR control declaration
nodes.rationale: Declares the AI controls the whole globex family commits to; a sister project may add to baseline but cannot remove from it. baseline starts empty on purpose: a scaffolder that pre-commits a family to controls produces commitments nobody made, and the first gate run fails on a decision never taken. Fill it from pf air baseline --suggest, which proposes only what already passes — a ratchet against regression rather than a wall of work. Dropping a control requires accepted: with reason and owner, because an acceptance without a reason is a gap with better formatting and one without an owner is a decision nobody can be asked about.

nodes.label: globex tools declaration
nodes.rationale: Enables recce, wren, openmetadata, expectations and elementary for every sister project in globex. Read, not generated — managed by pf tool enable/disable but hand-editing is fine. A project can override any key in its own tools.yaml, including enabled: false. An enabled tool is scaffolded and bootstrapped by pf bootstrap and contributes its assets to Dagster.

nodes.label: globex group skills convention
nodes.rationale: A skill belongs here when it encodes globex's domain knowledge — a reconciliation procedure, a regulatory workflow, a naming rule the ontology cannot express — shared by every sister project. Infra skills come from platform/toolkits and must not be duplicated here.

nodes.label: Three-tier eval structure (globex)
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; evals are their tests. Three tiers run together and each owns what only it can know: platform owns health checks and templates, group owns what every sister agrees on, project owns one entity's business logic. A case belongs at group tier when it would be wrong for a sister to disagree with it; if one sister could legitimately answer differently, it is a project case. Any change to an agent prompt must keep these green.

nodes.label: globex (group)
nodes.rationale: Two sister projects (globex-core, globex-eu) sharing one ontology instance with classes Customer, Order, Payment, Refund, Product, Location, plus conformed dimensions and group metrics — but separate warehouses, run in parallel.

nodes.label: Rollup-only cross-entity access
nodes.rationale: Cross-entity questions are answered only in the group's rollup project, which attaches sister databases READ_ONLY. Never read a sister project's files from another project — business logic does not transfer between entities.

nodes.label: globex-core (project)
nodes.rationale: Project conventions: every dlt resource is annotated (@annotate) before any model is written; marts declare meta.grain; the semantic layer owns aggregation policy; ask the graph (kg_search, kg_neighbors, kg_path) before reading files; run impact_analysis before changing a column, a model or a metric.

nodes.label: globex-core AIR control declaration
nodes.rationale: Merged over the group's air.yaml as a union, not a replacement: an entity may commit to more than its family, never to less. Baseline is filled from pf air baseline --suggest, which proposes only what already passes; accepting the proposal stays a person's act.

nodes.label: Session memory promotion (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: One lesson per file, one-line summary on top, written mid-task by agents. Promotion into groups/globex/CLAUDE.md (group-wide) or a platform RULES.md (universal) is a reviewed, human step — that promotion is what makes the platform compound instead of accumulating notes nobody reads.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Snowflake ingestion (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata) — rewritten from tools.yaml, pf.runtime.targets and the project's dbt artefacts; do not hand-edit. Credentials are env-var references (SNOWFLAKE_*, OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN); no secret is in the file. Registers service globex_globex_core.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata dbt ingestion (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata); do not hand-edit. Ingests transform/target manifest.json, catalog.json and run_results.json into service globex_globex_core; updates owners and tags but not descriptions.

nodes.label: AIR control gate (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: air.yaml is hand-written and carries the judgement: baseline controls block the merge via pf air gate, accepted requires reason and owner. governance/air-register.md is derived from air.yaml plus a fresh coverage run and is on the gate denylist — hand-editing it would make it disagree with the declaration it came from; change air.yaml then pf air register. The register carries the credit line of every catalogue it drew from, collected from sources actually loaded rather than templated, so a swapped catalogue takes its obligation with it.

nodes.label: Elementary observability (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: Every dbt build records itself via elementary-data hooks into the main_elementary schema beside the marts — observability is queryable tables with history, not a log that scrolled away. The CLI installs isolated (uv tool install) because it cannot share a lockfile with recce; recording needs nothing since the package rides inside dbt. Anomaly tests are deliberately not generated: an anomaly threshold is a judgement about one table's behaviour, so it is declared in the model's own yml. The elementary_report Dagster asset runs downstream of the marts; the recording itself has no asset.

nodes.label: dbt-expectations generated floor (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: transform/tests/expectations/ holds tests derived from the ontology by the chain annotations.yaml (column to role) -> knowledge graph (role + pii per mart column) -> dbt-expectations test — the same chain that generates recce checks. The floor asserts only that an annotated mart is not empty and its declared identity is unique and never null; anything sharper is a judgement about one table and belongs in that model's yml. Edit the roles, not the generated files. Runs as ordinary dbt tests (tag:expectations); results land in Elementary's history.

nodes.label: pf impact-gate CI check
nodes.rationale: Runs on every PR touching this project's models or sources; a change with a breaking blast radius fails the check and names the exposure owners who need to know. It deliberately does not open PRs, comment, or read beyond the diff: those need a token, this needs none because it runs inside the repo's own CI. Write-scoped automation stays a separate capability — the whole point of the gate is that it cannot be talked out of a verdict by the thing it is gating.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Catalogue (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: The catalogue is where someone who does not read YAML finds out what a table means; the project publishes glossary terms, tags, related terms and test cases into it automatically. Tables and lineage come from metadata ingest-dbt: the platform publishes what tables mean, dbt publishes what they are.

nodes.label: Projection, Not Sync
nodes.rationale: Nothing is read back from the catalogue: an edit made in the catalogue UI is overwritten on the next publish, on purpose, because the ontology is canonical and stays in git where pf check and the gate can judge it.

nodes.label: Recce dbt Review (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: pf impact says what could break; Recce says what did change. recce_state.json and target-base/ are gate-denied because hand-editing a recorded diff makes the review lie.

nodes.label: Baseline-and-Diff Review Loop
nodes.rationale: Build green, capture that build as the baseline, change a model, rebuild, then diff against the baseline and read it in the Recce UI.

nodes.label: Snowflake Production Warehouse
nodes.rationale: globex-core develops on DuckDB and runs production on Snowflake; one set of models serves both. Declaring the target does not make the models run on Snowflake — the dialect gate passing is what does.

nodes.label: DuckDB-first Development
nodes.rationale: A developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project. Every target but prod is a local DuckDB file, so dbt build works on a laptop, offline, with no credentials, in seconds; base exists so Recce has a second state to diff against. Nothing in this capability can move dev, ci or base, by construction.

nodes.label: Explicit prod Target Naming
nodes.rationale: There is deliberately no shortcut: DBT_TARGET=prod is named on every invocation because the failure mode — believing you are on dev and being on prod — is worse than the typing.

nodes.label: Credentials via Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: Credentials are read from the environment at run time and never written to a file: transform/profiles.yml holds env_var calls, not values, because it is committed. Key-pair auth is the default; pf doctor reports what is missing.

nodes.label: Wren Semantic Layer (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: pf ui -> Workspace joins this manifest to Recce's recorded diff on the model behind each entity, so 'fct_revenue moved' is read as which semantic entity changed and which ontology roles ride on it.

nodes.label: No Wren Web UI
nodes.rationale: Upstream's Docker chat-first BI app is legacy/v1 (Wren GenBI Classic). Current WrenAI is a CLI plus wren serve, which serves MCP, not a web page; the semantic surface is pf ui -> Semantics, which reads the same manifest. Nothing is being iframed, because there is nothing to iframe.

nodes.label: Eval Corpus (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests. Hand-written cases encode globex-core's own business rules no toolkit could guess. Any change to an agent prompt must keep these green. Nothing here is read by a sister, and nothing a sister writes is read here.

nodes.label: Mandatory why Field
nodes.rationale: why is not decoration — without it a corpus decays into assertions nobody dares change because nobody remembers whether they were deliberate.

nodes.label: Weak Prose Matchers
nodes.rationale: Keep prose matchers weak (contains_any, not exact strings). A case that pins wording fails on a harmless rewrite, and a suite that cries wolf gets switched off — which costs more than the case was ever worth.

nodes.label: Unstable-Prompt Detection via --samples
nodes.rationale: --samples N runs each case N times. A case that passes 4 times in 5 is not passing and not failing — it is an unstable prompt, the most useful thing the suite can say before a prompt change ships.

nodes.label: AI Risk Register (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf air register from air.yaml; derived from the repository on every run — no verdict is stored, and the path is on the gate denylist. Coverage: 11 of 23 controls enforced, 9 not enforced, 3 unexercised; cross-walked to EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST SP 800-53, IOSCO and ATR. Catalogue pinned at 274760ccd058.

nodes.label: Capabilities Card (none enabled)
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf context build; edit the Capability declaration, never this file. Reports no capabilities enabled for globex/globex-core.

nodes.label: Evidence BI Reporting (globex-core)
nodes.rationale: BI-as-code generated by pf report build, never hand-maintained. Pipeline: dbt marts -> MetricFlow metrics -> MDL -> queries/metrics/*.sql -> pages/*.md. Durable narrative belongs in an owned page or the metric description, since regenerating overwrites generated pages.

nodes.label: Pages Never Restate Business Logic
nodes.rationale: Every number traces to a metric compiled into queries/metrics/. If a dashboard needs a figure that does not exist, the fix is a metric definition in transform/models/semantic/, then pf report build — not SQL in a page. Two pages filtering differently is how one company ends up with two revenues.

nodes.label: Ratio Metrics Re-divide at Grain
nodes.rationale: Ratio queries carry their numerator and denominator so a page re-divides at its own grain: sum(num) / sum(den). Never avg(ratio) — it is wrong at every grain except the one it was computed at, and it is the most common BI bug there is.

nodes.label: Node 20 Runtime Boundary
nodes.rationale: Evidence 40 does not build on Node 24 / npm 11 — verified by building a pristine evidence-dev/template which fails the same way, so this is Evidence's supported-runtime boundary rather than anything about this project. npm run build needs Node 20 (.nvmrc committed).

nodes.label: Evidence Theme Configuration
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build; declares the @evidence-dev/duckdb datasource plugin plus light/dark categorical palettes and status colors.

nodes.label: Validated CVD-safe Palette
nodes.rationale: Palette values are validated — adjacent-pair CVD deltaE >= 8, normal-vision >= 15, contrast checked on both surfaces. Re-picking them by eye makes charts unreadable for ~8% of readers.

nodes.label: globex-core Overview Page
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build; a projection of the metric definitions in transform/models/semantic/. Every number is a governed metric compiled from the dbt semantic layer into queries/metrics/.

nodes.label: DuckDB Reporting Connector
nodes.rationale: Points Evidence at ../../../data/globex_core.duckdb. One warehouse file per project is what lets sister companies run in parallel; the reporting layer only ever reads.

nodes.label: globex_core dbt Project
nodes.rationale: Staging materialized as views in the staging schema; marts as tables in the marts schema; profile globex_core.

nodes.label: Platform Macros as Root-Project Macros
nodes.rationale: The platform cleaning macros are loaded via macro-paths, not as a package: pf gen-staging emits unqualified {{ pf_clean(...) }} and pf_clean dispatches to its clean_* siblings unqualified too. dbt namespaces package macros, so a pf.-prefixed call would still fail on the inner dispatch.

nodes.label: Elementary Schema Isolation
nodes.rationale: Elementary's observability models (run results, test history, schema snapshots) are written by the package's on-run-end hooks on every dbt build; +schema: elementary keeps them out of the marts. Managed by pf tool elementary.

nodes.label: dbt_utils 1.4.1 Lock Pin
nodes.rationale: Lock resolves only dbt-labs/dbt_utils 1.4.1 with a sha1 hash, although packages.yml declares three packages — the other two are not pinned here.

nodes.label: globex_core dbt Profile
nodes.rationale: Targets dev/ci/base are DuckDB on PF_DUCKDB_PATH; prod is Snowflake via env_var references. Default target comes from DBT_TARGET, falling back to dev.

nodes.label: prod Snowflake Target
nodes.rationale: All Snowflake connection fields are env_var references (account, user, private key path or password, role, warehouse, database, schema) — no value is committed.

nodes.label: base Comparison Target
nodes.rationale: The comparison environment for a diff tool: same database file, different schema prefix, so base_marts.fct_revenue and main_marts.fct_revenue both exist and can be queried against each other in one connection. It has to be a separate materialisation — pointing a review tool at two sets of dbt artefacts that resolve to the same relation makes every value diff compare a table with itself and report clean, a false negative on every change, worse than no review at all.

nodes.label: elementary edr Profile
nodes.rationale: How the Elementary CLI (edr) reads the tables the dbt package writes. Derived from the project profile by pf tool elementary — one elementary output per project target, schema suffixed the way dbt composes custom schemas, so DBT_TARGET=prod edr report reads production and the default reads dev. Regenerated by pf bootstrap — retarget the project, not this block.

nodes.label: Generated Recce Checks
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap: row_count_diff over modified table models and schema_diff. Regenerate with pf tool recce config.

nodes.label: Checks Derived from Ontology Roles
nodes.rationale: Every check is derived, not written: contracts/annotations.yaml maps column to ontology role, concepts.yaml maps role to review intent and pii flag, pf.tools.recce maps intent to check type. The way to change a check is to fix what the column means — a wrong check is a wrong role. Columns whose role is PII are excluded from every value-level check, because results land in recce_state.json, which is durable and shared.

nodes.label: metricflow_time_spine Model
nodes.rationale: Daily time spine required by MetricFlow; date_day at day granularity, unique and not_null tested, materialized as a table.

nodes.label: globex-eu Project Context
nodes.rationale: Project context for globex-eu in group globex; the sister roster lives in the group card. No business rules recorded yet.

nodes.label: Sister-Project Isolation
nodes.rationale: Do not read a sister's files from here — business logic does not transfer between entities, so an assumption carried across is a bug.

nodes.label: Graph-First Convention
nodes.rationale: Ask the graph before reading files (kg_search, kg_neighbors, kg_path); run impact_analysis before changing a column, a model or a metric; annotate every dlt resource before any model is written; marts declare meta.grain and the semantic layer owns aggregation policy.

nodes.label: globex-eu AIR Declaration
nodes.rationale: Read, not generated — governance/air-register.md is the generated half. Merged over the group's air.yaml: baseline is a union with the group's, not a replacement — an entity may commit to more than its family, never to less. Baseline and accepted are both currently empty.

nodes.label: Baseline as Ratchet
nodes.rationale: Start from pf air baseline --suggest, which proposes only what already passes — a ratchet against regression rather than a wall of work nobody agreed to. Accepting the proposal stays a person's act.

nodes.label: Acceptance Requires Reason and Owner
nodes.rationale: Controls consciously not taken require reason and owner: an acceptance without a reason is a gap with better formatting, and one without an owner is a decision nobody can be asked about.

nodes.label: Session Memory Notes (globex-eu)
nodes.rationale: One lesson per file, one-line summary on top, written mid-task by agents.

nodes.label: Memory Promotion Workflow
nodes.rationale: Promotion into groups/globex/CLAUDE.md (group-wide) or a platform RULES.md (universal) is a reviewed, human step — that promotion is what makes the platform compound instead of accumulating notes nobody reads.

nodes.label: Snowflake Metadata Ingestion (globex-eu)
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata) from tools.yaml, pf.runtime.targets and the project's dbt artefacts; rewritten on regeneration. OpenMetadata DatabaseMetadata workflow for serviceName globex_globex_eu; all credentials are env-var references, no secret in the file.

nodes.label: dbt Artefact Ingestion (globex-eu)
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata). OpenMetadata DBT workflow for serviceName globex_globex_eu, reading transform/target manifest.json, catalog.json and run_results.json locally; updates owners and tags but not descriptions.

nodes.label: pf air gate (merge blocker)
nodes.rationale: Blocks the merge when a control the project committed to in air.yaml is not enforced. Coverage is derived by `pf air coverage`, never stored, so the gate cannot drift from the repository state. Controls come from whichever catalogues are registered (`pf air catalogues`).

nodes.label: air.yaml control baseline declaration
nodes.rationale: Hand-written and carries the judgement: `baseline:` controls block the merge; `accepted:` controls require reason and owner because 'an acceptance without them is a gap with better formatting'; a project may add to its group's baseline but cannot remove from it — the only way to drop a control is `accepted:`, which leaves a name attached to the decision.

nodes.label: Elementary observability recording
nodes.rationale: The elementary-data/elementary package hooks on-run-start/on-run-end so every dbt build records run results, all test results, model timings and schema snapshots into the main_elementary schema — observability is queryable tables with history, not a log that scrolled away. The edr CLI is installed isolated because it cannot share a lockfile with recce; recording itself needs nothing because the package rides inside dbt.

nodes.label: Elementary anomaly tests (volume/freshness)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not generated: an anomaly threshold is a judgement about one table's behaviour, so it is declared in the model's own yml where that judgement lives. The elementary-observe skills (add-anomaly-tests, triage-observability) are the how; results land in the same Elementary tables and report.

nodes.label: dbt-expectations generated floor
nodes.rationale: transform/tests/expectations/ holds tests derived from the ontology via the chain annotations.yaml (column->role) -> knowledge graph (role+pii per mart column) -> generated dbt-expectations test. The floor asserts only that an annotated mart is not empty and its declared identity is unique and never null — anything sharper is a judgement about one table and belongs in that model's yml. Edit the roles, not the generated files; pf bootstrap regenerates. Runs as ordinary dbt tests under tag:expectations.

nodes.label: pf impact-gate CI check
nodes.rationale: Runs on every PR touching this project's models or sources; a change with a breaking blast radius fails the check and names the exposure owners. Deliberately token-less — it does not open PRs, comment, or read beyond the diff — because the whole point of the gate is that it cannot be talked out of a verdict by the thing it is gating. Write-scoped automation belongs in a separate capability.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata catalogue projection
nodes.rationale: A projection, not a sync: nothing is read back, and a change made in the catalogue UI is overwritten on the next publish on purpose — the ontology is canonical and stays in git where pf check and the gate can judge it. Concepts become glossary terms, ontology roles become PlatformRole tags (PII roles also get PII.Sensitive), topology relations become relatedTerms, recce checks become test cases carrying the review verdict. Tables and lineage come from metadata ingest-dbt: 'We publish what they mean; dbt publishes what they are.' OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN is a credential and is never written into a generated file.

nodes.label: Recce review loop
nodes.rationale: 'pf impact says what could break. Recce says what did change.' Loop: build green, capture baseline, change a model, rebuild, diff against the baseline, read it in the Recce UI. recce_state.json and target-base/ are gate-denied build artefacts because hand-editing a recorded diff makes the review lie.

nodes.label: Recce artefact store publication
nodes.rationale: Baselines are published under the ref they were built from; the recorded review under the branch under review. With no store configured everything stays local — right on a laptop that built its own baseline, wrong in CI: a runner has code and no warehouse, so an unconfigured store there means the review reports 'not exercised' rather than green.

nodes.label: DuckDB-dev / Snowflake-prod dual target
nodes.rationale: One set of models serves both warehouses: sf_* macros in platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake dispatch per adapter. Development stays on DuckDB because a developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project — every target but prod is a local file that works offline with no credentials. Declaring the target does not make models run on Snowflake; the dialect gate (pf align validate --stage dialect) passing does. DBT_TARGET=prod is named explicitly on every invocation, deliberately with no shortcut, because believing you are on dev while on prod is worse than the typing.

nodes.label: Snowflake credentials from environment
nodes.rationale: Credentials are read from the environment at run time and never written to a file because transform/profiles.yml is committed — it holds env_var calls, not values. Key-pair auth (SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH) is the default; password only when key-pair is unavailable. pf doctor reports which variables are missing.

nodes.label: MDL semantic-layer manifest (mdl/mdl.json)
nodes.rationale: The project's semantic layer in MDL, the interchange format a BI or text-to-SQL layer consumes without being told internals. Generated from the knowledge graph by pf bootstrap, never hand-edited. There is no Wren web UI: upstream's Docker chat-first app is legacy/v1; current WrenAI is a CLI plus `wren serve`, which serves MCP, not a web page — the semantic surface is pf ui -> Semantics reading this same manifest.

nodes.label: pf ui Workspace review-semantics join
nodes.rationale: Joins the MDL manifest to Recce's recorded diff on the model behind each entity, so 'fct_revenue moved' is read as which published semantic entity changed and which ontology roles ride on it, rather than a list of dbt node names. Needs both the wren and recce tools on; both are on by default for a new group.

nodes.label: globex-eu eval corpus
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests. generated/ is written by pf evals-gen from toolkit templates resolved against this project's knowledge graph (cases name your models and columns); regenerating overwrites it. Hand-written cases encode entity-specific business rules no toolkit could guess. The `why` field is required because without it a corpus decays into assertions nobody dares change. Prose matchers stay weak (contains_any) because a suite that cries wolf gets switched off, which costs more than any case was worth. --samples N surfaces unstable prompts: a case passing 4 of 5 is neither passing nor failing.

nodes.label: globex-eu AI risk register (generated)
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf air register and on the gate denylist: air.yaml is the declaration it derives from and the next run discards hand-edits. Derived from the repository on every run — no verdict is stored. Snapshot: 11 of 23 controls enforced, 9 not enforced, 3 unexercised; the committed baseline is empty, so pf air gate cannot block on it. Catalogue pinned at 274760ccd058.

nodes.label: globex-eu capabilities card (none enabled)
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf context build — edit the Capability declaration, never this file. No capabilities enabled for globex/globex-eu at generation time.

nodes.label: Validated chart palette (evidence.config.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build. Palette values are validated — adjacent-pair CVD deltaE >= 8, normal-vision >= 15, contrast checked on both light and dark surfaces. Re-picking them by eye makes charts unreadable for ~8% of readers. Also declares the @evidence-dev/duckdb datasource plugin and status colors.

nodes.label: globex-eu overview page (generated)
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build; a projection of the metric definitions in transform/models/semantic/. Every number is a governed metric compiled into queries/metrics/ — nothing restates business logic.

nodes.label: Evidence DuckDB connector (globex_eu)
nodes.rationale: Points Evidence at ../../../data/globex_eu.duckdb. One warehouse file per project is what lets sister companies run in parallel; the reporting layer only ever reads.

nodes.label: globex_eu dbt project config
nodes.rationale: Loads the platform cleaning macros as root-project macros via macro-paths (../../../../../platform/dbt/macros), not as a package: pf gen-staging emits unqualified {{ pf_clean(...) }} and pf_clean dispatches to its clean_* siblings unqualified too; dbt namespaces package macros, so a pf.-prefixed call would still fail on the inner dispatch. Staging materializes as views in the staging schema, marts as tables in the marts schema.

nodes.label: Elementary +schema model config
nodes.rationale: Elementary's observability models (run results, test history, schema snapshots) are written by the package's on-run-end hooks on every dbt build; the +schema: elementary setting keeps them out of the marts. Managed by pf tool elementary.

nodes.label: dbt package lock (dbt_utils 1.4.1)
nodes.rationale: Pins dbt-labs/dbt_utils at 1.4.1 with a sha1 hash. Note: the lock covers only dbt_utils while packages.yml declares three packages (dbt_utils, dbt_expectations, elementary) — the lock predates or has not been refreshed for the other two.

nodes.label: dbt package declarations
nodes.rationale: Declares dbt-labs/dbt_utils (>=1.3.0,<2.0.0), metaplane/dbt_expectations (>=0.10.4,<0.11.0) and elementary-data/elementary (>=0.25.0,<0.26.0), each minor-pinned. pf bootstrap adds entries; the project's own pin wins.

nodes.label: globex_eu dbt profile
nodes.rationale: Target chosen by DBT_TARGET env var, defaulting to dev. dev, ci and base are local DuckDB (path from PF_DUCKDB_PATH); prod is Snowflake configured entirely through env_var calls — no credential values are committed.

nodes.label: base comparison target
nodes.rationale: The comparison environment for a diff tool: same DuckDB file, different schema prefix, so base_marts.fct_revenue and main_marts.fct_revenue both exist and can be queried against each other in one connection. This has to be a separate materialisation — pointing a review tool at two sets of dbt artefacts that resolve to the same relation makes every value diff compare a table with itself and report clean: a false negative on every change, worse than having no review at all.

nodes.label: elementary edr profile (derived)
nodes.rationale: How the Elementary CLI (edr) reads the tables the dbt package writes. DERIVED from the project profile by pf tool elementary: one elementary output per project target, schema suffixed the way dbt composes custom schemas (main_elementary, base_elementary, <schema>_elementary on prod), so DBT_TARGET=prod edr report reads the production warehouse. Regenerated by pf bootstrap — retarget the project, not this block.

nodes.label: Generated Recce checks (recce.yml)
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf bootstrap; every check is derived, not written: contracts/annotations.yaml (column->role) -> ontology concepts.yaml (role->review intent, pii flag) -> pf.tools.recce (intent->check type). The way to change a check is to fix what the column means — a wrong check is a wrong role. Columns whose role is PII are excluded from every value-level check because results land in recce_state.json, which is durable and shared. Currently: row_count_diff on modified table models and schema_diff.

nodes.label: metricflow_time_spine model
nodes.rationale: Daily time spine required by MetricFlow; materialized as a table with date_day as the standard day-granularity column, tested unique and not_null.

nodes.label: globex_shared dbt project config
nodes.rationale: The group-level shared dbt project (conformed dimensions). Uses the same root-project macro-paths mechanism as the sister projects to load platform cleaning macros unqualified, for the same pf_clean dispatch reason.

nodes.label: Sister-project isolation rule
nodes.rationale: Only the <group>-rollup project may read sister data, and only via ATTACH READ_ONLY. Never read a sister project's files from another project — business logic does not transfer between entities.

nodes.label: Jaffle Group AIR Declaration
nodes.rationale: Read, not generated — declares which AI controls the whole jaffle family commits to; declared here means declared for every sister project, which may add but never remove.

nodes.label: Empty-by-Default AIR Baseline
nodes.rationale: baseline starts empty on purpose: a scaffolder that pre-commits a family to controls produces commitments nobody made, and the first gate run fails on a decision never taken. Fill from `pf air baseline --suggest`, which proposes only what already passes — a ratchet against regression rather than a wall of work.

nodes.label: Accepted (Consciously Not Taken) Controls
nodes.rationale: reason and owner are both required: an acceptance without a reason is a gap with better formatting, and one without an owner is a decision nobody can be asked about.

nodes.label: Jaffle Group Tools Declaration
nodes.rationale: Enabled at group level means enabled for every sister project; a project can override any key in its own tools.yaml, including enabled: false. A tool enabled here is scaffolded by pf bootstrap and contributes assets to Dagster.

nodes.label: Jaffle Group Skills
nodes.rationale: A skill belongs here when it encodes jaffle's domain knowledge (reconciliation procedure, regulatory workflow, naming rule the ontology cannot express); infra skills come from platform/toolkits and must not be duplicated.

nodes.label: Jaffle Group Evals
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests. A case belongs at group level when it would be wrong for a sister to disagree with it; if one sister could legitimately answer differently, it is a project case.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Eval Model
nodes.rationale: platform / group / project tiers run together and each owns what only it can know: platform owns health checks and templates, group owns what every sister agrees on, project owns one entity's business logic.

nodes.label: Jaffle Seeds Ontology Proposal (applied)
nodes.rationale: Induced from jaffle-seeds on 2026-08-14 and approved by the onboarding-ladder: 58 class axioms, 57 identities, 446 properties, 65 refers_to relations. Approval merges accepted axioms into groups/jaffle/ontology/extension.yaml then rebuilds the knowledge graph, MDL manifest and reporting layer for every project in the group; the platform ontology is deliberately NOT modified. All 65 refers_to relation names were left unaccepted because placeholder names (payment_refers_to_customer) tell a reader nothing — relations need their real business verb.

nodes.label: Evidence-and-Rationale Axiom Review
nodes.rationale: Every axiom carries evidence (what was observed) and rationale (why the rule fired) so a reviewer can disagree with the reasoning, not just the conclusion; anything left accept: false is dropped, and the draft is meant to be edited.

nodes.label: PII Tags Proposed, Never Auto-Applied
nodes.rationale: A wrong PII tag carries authority it did not earn, and a missing one fails the mart policy loudly — so pii_email / pii_name roles are proposed at medium confidence and default to accept: false.

nodes.label: Term Reuse Over Synonym Minting
nodes.rationale: Reusing an existing ontology term rather than minting a synonym is the whole point of a shared vocabulary; a reused class's curated identity is protected — the scanned raw column must not silently replace a deliberate decision (override: true required).

nodes.label: Jaffle-Shop Project
nodes.rationale: Project context router for jaffle-shop in group jaffle; conventions: every dlt resource is @annotate-d before models, marts declare meta.grain, ask the graph before reading files, run impact_analysis before changing a column, model or metric.

nodes.label: Jaffle-Shop Semantic Stack
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary is platform-wide and already loaded in the project's graph before any data exists — kg_search finds concepts, relations and policies on day one; pf semantic topology/policy/mdl and pf bootstrap regenerate the projections.

nodes.label: Declared Join Binding
nodes.rationale: A foreign key must be declared with links={"col": "SomeClass"} and the topology must already relate the two classes — that binding makes join conditions derivable rather than guessed; pf check fails on an undeclared join.

nodes.label: Jaffle-Shop AIR Declaration
nodes.rationale: Merged over the group's air.yaml: baseline is a union with the group's, not a replacement — an entity may commit to more than its family, never to less. Accepting a --suggest proposal stays a person's act.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Snowflake Ingestion Workflow
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata), rewritten from tools.yaml, pf.runtime.targets and the project's dbt artefacts; credentials are env-var references (SNOWFLAKE_*, OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN) — no secret is in the file. Service name jaffle_jaffle_shop.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata dbt Ingestion Workflow
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata); ingests transform/target/manifest.json, catalog.json and run_results.json into service jaffle_jaffle_shop with dbtUpdateOwners and tags on, descriptions off.

nodes.label: AIR Gate (pf air gate)
nodes.rationale: pf air gate jaffle jaffle-shop blocks the merge when a committed control is not enforced; baseline controls block, everything else is reported and advisory; a project may add to its group's baseline but the only way to drop a control is accepted:, which leaves a name attached to the decision.

nodes.label: Generated AIR Register Principle
nodes.rationale: governance/air-register.md is derived from air.yaml plus a fresh coverage run and is on the gate denylist — hand-editing it would make it disagree with the declaration it came from; it carries the credit line of every catalogue actually loaded, so a swapped catalogue takes its obligation with it.

nodes.label: Anomaly Tests Are Declared, Not Generated
nodes.rationale: An anomaly threshold is a judgement about one table's behaviour, so volume/freshness anomaly tests are deliberately not generated — declare them in the model's own yml where that judgement lives; the elementary-observe skills (add-anomaly-tests, triage-observability) are the how.
nodes.norm_label: anomaly tests are declared, not generated

nodes.label: pf impact-gate (GitHub CI)
nodes.rationale: Runs on every PR that touches this project's models or sources; a breaking blast radius fails the check and names the exposure owners. It deliberately needs no token — it does not open PRs, comment, or read beyond the diff — because the whole point of the gate is that it cannot be talked out of a verdict by the thing it is gating; write-scoped automation is a separate capability.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Catalogue Publication
nodes.rationale: The catalogue is where someone who does not read YAML finds out what a table means: concepts.yaml becomes glossary terms, ontology roles become PlatformRole tags (PII roles also get PII.Sensitive), topology relations become relatedTerms, the policy layer becomes constraint glossary terms, dbt target/*.json becomes tables/columns/lineage, and recce checks become test cases carrying the review verdict. We publish what tables mean; dbt publishes what they are.

nodes.label: Projection, Not Sync
nodes.rationale: Nothing is read back from the catalogue: a change made in the catalogue UI is overwritten on the next publish, on purpose — the ontology is canonical and stays in git where pf check and the gate can judge it.

nodes.label: Generated recce.yml
nodes.rationale: transform/recce.yml is derived from contracts/annotations.yaml — a natural_key role becomes a value-diff primary key, a money_amount becomes a profile diff. Edit the roles, not the config; pf bootstrap regenerates it. recce_state.json and target-base/ are gate-denied build artefacts because hand-editing a recorded diff makes the review lie.

nodes.label: Snowflake Production Target
nodes.rationale: One set of models serves DuckDB dev and Snowflake prod: the sf_* macros in platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake dispatch per adapter, and pf align validate --stage dialect is the gate that says whether the project is actually portable or merely untested. Credentials are env_var calls in committed profiles.yml, never values; key-pair auth by default. The target is named on every invocation (DBT_TARGET=prod) because believing you are on dev while being on prod is worse than the typing.

nodes.label: DuckDB-First Development
nodes.rationale: A developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project: every target but prod is a local DuckDB file, so dbt build works on a laptop, offline, with no credentials, in seconds — and base exists so Recce has a second state to diff against. Nothing in the capability can move dev, ci or base, by construction.

nodes.label: No Wren Web UI
nodes.rationale: Upstream's Docker chat-first BI app is legacy/v1 (Wren GenBI Classic); current WrenAI is a CLI plus wren serve, which serves MCP, not a web page — so the semantic surface is pf ui -> Semantics reading the same manifest. Nothing is iframed because there is nothing to iframe.

nodes.label: Jaffle-Shop Project Evals
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests — one JSON per case, run with pf evals jaffle jaffle-shop; any change to an agent prompt must keep them green.

nodes.label: Jaffle-Shop AI Risk Register
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf air register and derived from the repository on every run — no verdict is stored. Coverage: 11 of 23 controls enforced, 9 not enforced, 3 unexercised; committed baseline is empty so pf air gate cannot block. Notable enforced controls: AIR-DET-21 agent decision audit, AIR-PREV-18 least privilege, AIR-PREV-22 multi-agent isolation, AIR-PREV-23 credential protection. Catalogue pinned at 274760ccd058.

nodes.label: Evidence BI Reporting Layer
nodes.rationale: BI-as-code generated by pf report build, never hand-maintained: dbt marts -> MetricFlow metrics -> MDL -> queries/metrics/*.sql -> pages/*.md. Requires Node 20 (Evidence 40 does not build on Node 24/npm 11 — a verified Evidence supported-runtime boundary, not a project issue). Regenerating overwrites generated pages, so durable narrative belongs in an owned page or the metric description.

nodes.label: Pages Never Restate Business Logic
nodes.rationale: Every number traces to a metric compiled into queries/metrics/; if a dashboard needs a figure that does not exist, the fix is a metric definition in transform/models/semantic/ then pf report build — not SQL in a page. Two pages filtering differently is how one company ends up with two revenues.

nodes.label: Ratio Re-Aggregation Rule
nodes.rationale: Ratio queries carry their numerator and denominator so a page re-divides at its own grain: sum(num)/sum(den). Never avg(ratio) — it is wrong at every grain except the one it was computed at, and it is the most common BI bug there is.

nodes.label: Governed metric projection
nodes.rationale: Reporting pages never restate business logic: every figure is a governed metric compiled from the dbt semantic layer into queries/metrics/. If a figure is missing, the fix is a metric definition, not SQL in the page. Metric definitions live in transform/models/semantic/; pages are projections generated by pf report build.

nodes.label: DateRange two-row bounds workaround
nodes.rationale: Evidence's DateRange component reads min()/max() from one column, so both date bounds must arrive as two rows in that column (via union all), not as two columns of one row.

nodes.label: Ratio metric aggregation (drink revenue %)
nodes.rationale: Carried as drink_revenue / revenue numerator and denominator columns so the ratio re-divides correctly at any grain: aggregated as sum(drink_revenue) / sum(revenue) at whatever grain you group by. Averaging the ratio itself gives a different — and wrong — answer.

nodes.label: Ratio metric aggregation (food revenue %)
nodes.rationale: Carried as food_revenue / revenue numerator and denominator columns so the ratio re-divides correctly at any grain: aggregated as sum(food_revenue) / sum(revenue) at whatever grain you group by. Averaging the ratio itself gives a different — and wrong — answer.

nodes.label: Per-project warehouse isolation
nodes.rationale: One DuckDB warehouse file per project (data/jaffle_shop.duckdb) is what lets sister companies run in parallel; the reporting layer only ever reads from it.

nodes.label: Elementary schema isolation
nodes.rationale: Elementary's observability models (run results, test history, schema snapshots) are written by the package's on-run-end hooks on every dbt build; the +schema: elementary override keeps them out of the marts. Managed by pf tool elementary.

nodes.label: Domain/layer/criticality tag taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Models are tagged along orthogonal axes — layer (staging/marts/utility), domain (core, finance, supply_chain, marketing, hr_ops, product, cross_domain), criticality (high/medium/low), type (metric, kpi, alert, snapshot, ...) and audience (cfo, data_team) — so selection and gating can target any slice without renaming models.

nodes.label: Seed loading gated by load_source_data var
nodes.rationale: Every seed folder (jaffle-data, finance-data, supply-chain-data, marketing-data, hr-ops-data, product-data) is enabled only when var('load_source_data') is true, so routine dbt builds skip re-loading raw source seeds; seeds land in the raw schema.

nodes.label: Recce artefact store publishing
nodes.rationale: Baselines publish under the ref they were built from; reviews under the branch under review. Unconfigured store is right on a laptop that built its own baseline, wrong in CI: a runner has code and no warehouse, so an unconfigured store there means the review reports 'not exercised' rather than green.

nodes.label: Workspace join of review and semantic layer

nodes.label: MDL manifest (mdl/mdl.json)

nodes.label: Weak prose matchers

Coverage: 11 of 23 controls enforced, 9 not enforced, 3 unexercised; committed baseline empty, so pf air gate cannot block. Per-regime counts (EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST SP 800-53, IOSCO, ATR) are counted from the same verdicts so they cannot disagree.

nodes.label: Evidence capability card — zenith-de

nodes.label: Evidence BI reporting — zenith-de

nodes.label: Ratio metrics re-divide at grain
