nodes.label: Evidence config and validated palette
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build. Palette values are validated — adjacent-pair CVD deltaE >= 8, normal-vision >= 15, contrast checked on both light and dark surfaces; re-picking them by eye makes charts unreadable for ~8% of readers. Declares the @evidence-dev/duckdb datasource plugin.

nodes.label: zenith-de overview page
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build; a projection of the metric definitions in transform/models/semantic/. States on-page that every number is a governed metric compiled into queries/metrics/ and that a missing figure means a missing metric definition, not SQL in the page.

nodes.label: Evidence DuckDB connector — zenith_de
nodes.rationale: Points Evidence at data/zenith_de.duckdb. One warehouse file per project is what lets sister companies run in parallel; the reporting layer only ever reads.

nodes.label: dbt project — zenith_de
nodes.rationale: Profile zenith_de; staging materialized as views in a staging schema, marts as tables in a marts schema. Elementary's observability models (run results, test history, schema snapshots, written by the package's on-run-end hooks) get +schema: elementary to keep them out of the marts; managed by pf tool elementary.

nodes.label: pf_clean root-macro loading
nodes.rationale: Platform cleaning macros load as root-project macros via macro-paths (../../../../../platform/dbt/macros), not as a package: pf_clean dispatches to its clean_* siblings unqualified, and dbt namespaces package macros, so a package install fails on the inner dispatch.

nodes.label: dbt package lock
nodes.rationale: Pins dbt-labs/dbt_utils at 1.4.1 with a sha1 hash; dbt_expectations and elementary from packages.yml are not present in the lock.

nodes.label: dbt profile targets (dev/ci/prod/base)
nodes.rationale: dev/ci/base are DuckDB on PF_DUCKDB_PATH; prod is Snowflake via env_var calls only (key-pair or password, role/warehouse/schema defaulted). base is a separate materialisation with its own schema so base_marts.fct_revenue and main_marts.fct_revenue coexist in one connection: pointing a review tool at two sets of dbt artefacts resolving to the same relation makes every value diff compare a table with itself and report clean — a false negative on every change, worse than no review at all.

nodes.label: Elementary CLI profile block
nodes.rationale: How the Elementary CLI (edr) reads the tables the dbt package writes. DERIVED from the project profile by pf tool elementary: one elementary output per project target, schema suffixed the way dbt composes custom schemas, so DBT_TARGET=prod edr report reads production and the default reads dev. Regenerated by pf bootstrap — retarget the project, not this block.

nodes.label: Recce checks config
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap; every check is derived, not written: annotations.yaml maps column → ontology role, concepts.yaml maps role → review intent and PII flag, pf.tools.recce maps intent → check type. The way to change a check is to fix what the column means — a wrong check is a wrong role. PII-role columns are excluded from every value-level check because results land in recce_state.json, which is durable and shared. Current checks: row_count_diff on modified table models, schema_diff.

nodes.label: metricflow_time_spine
nodes.rationale: Daily time spine required by MetricFlow; date_day is the standard granularity column, tested unique and not_null; materialized as a table.

nodes.label: zenith-uk project context
nodes.rationale: Group zenith; sister roster lives in the group card — do not read a sister's files from here. Conventions: every dlt resource annotated (@annotate) before any model is written; marts declare meta.grain and the semantic layer owns aggregation policy; ask the graph (kg_search, kg_neighbors, kg_path) before reading files; run impact_analysis before changing a column, model or metric.

nodes.label: AIR control commitments — zenith-uk
nodes.rationale: Read, not generated — governance/air-register.md is the generated half. baseline is a union with the group's air.yaml, not a replacement: an entity may commit to more than its family, never to less. Baseline currently empty, so pf air gate cannot block; pf air baseline --suggest proposes only what already passes — a ratchet against regression, and accepting it stays a person's act. accepted controls require reason and owner: an acceptance without a reason is a gap with better formatting, and one without an owner is a decision nobody can be asked about.

nodes.label: Session memory notes — zenith-uk
nodes.rationale: One lesson per file, one-line summary on top, written mid-task by agents. Promotion into groups/zenith/CLAUDE.md (group-wide) or a platform RULES.md (universal) is a reviewed human step — that promotion is what makes the platform compound instead of accumulating notes nobody reads.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Snowflake ingestion — zenith-uk
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap (pf.tools.openmetadata), rewritten from tools.yaml, pf.runtime.targets and the project's dbt artefacts. Ingests Snowflake database metadata into serviceName zenith_zenith_uk at http://localhost:8585/api; credentials are env-var references (SNOWFLAKE_*, OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN) — no secret in the file.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata dbt ingestion — zenith-uk
nodes.rationale: Reads transform/target manifest.json, catalog.json and run_results.json into serviceName zenith_zenith_uk. dbtUpdateDescriptions is false — table meaning stays owned by the ontology projection while dbt supplies what the tables are; owners and tags are taken (dbtUpdateOwners true, includeTags true).

nodes.label: Generated AI risk register mechanism
nodes.rationale: governance/air-register.md is derived from air.yaml plus a fresh coverage run and is on the gate denylist — hand-editing it would make it disagree with the declaration it came from. Credit lines are collected from the catalogues actually loaded rather than templated, so a swapped catalogue takes its obligation with it and an added one brings its own.

nodes.label: Elementary data observability package
nodes.rationale: Every dbt build records itself via on-run-start/on-run-end hooks into the main_elementary schema — observability is queryable tables with history, not a log that scrolled away. The edr CLI is installed isolated because it cannot share a lockfile with recce; recording itself needs nothing because the package rides inside dbt.

nodes.label: Elementary anomaly tests (deliberately not generated)
nodes.rationale: volume_anomalies, freshness_anomalies etc. are deliberately not generated: an anomaly threshold is a judgement about one table's behaviour, so it is declared in the model's own yml where that judgement lives. The elementary-observe skills (add-anomaly-tests, triage-observability) are the how.

nodes.label: dbt-expectations test vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Great Expectations' vocabulary as native dbt tests, installed project-wide; usable directly in any model's yml for per-table judgements.

nodes.label: Generated expectations floor (ontology-derived tests)
nodes.rationale: transform/tests/expectations/ holds tests derived from annotations.yaml roles resolved through the knowledge graph — the same chain that generates recce checks. The floor only asserts: an annotated mart must not be empty, its declared identity unique and never null. Anything sharper is a judgement about one table and belongs in that model's yml, not a generator. Edit the roles, not the generated files.

nodes.label: OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN credential rule
nodes.rationale: Must be set wherever ingestion runs; it is a credential and is never written into a generated file. Host and service name come from tools.yaml.

nodes.label: pf ui Workspace review-to-semantic join
nodes.rationale: Joins the recorded Recce review to the MDL manifest on the model, so a diff is read as which published entity moved and what it carries rather than a list of dbt node names. Needs both the recce and wren tools on; both are on by default for a new group.

nodes.label: DuckDB-dev / Snowflake-prod dual target strategy
nodes.rationale: A developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project. Every target but prod is a local DuckDB file, so dbt build works on a laptop, offline, with no credentials, in seconds. Only prod points at Snowflake; nothing in the capability can move dev, ci or base, by construction. Declaring the target does not make models run on Snowflake — the dialect gate passing does.

nodes.label: sf_* adapter-dispatch macros and dialect gate
nodes.rationale: The sf_* macros in platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake dispatch per adapter so a model is written once and compiles to whatever the target understands. pf align validate --stage dialect is the gate that says whether the project is actually portable or merely untested.
nodes.norm_label: sf_* adapter-dispatch macros and dialect gate

nodes.label: Explicit DBT_TARGET=prod invocation rule
nodes.rationale: There is deliberately no shortcut: the target is named on every invocation because the failure mode — believing you are on dev and being on prod — is worse than the typing.

nodes.label: Environment-only Snowflake credentials
nodes.rationale: Credentials are read from the environment at run time and never written to a file — profiles.yml holds env_var calls, not values, because it is committed. Key-pair auth is the default (SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH); password only if key-pair is unavailable. pf doctor reports which are missing.

nodes.label: Wren MDL semantic-layer manifest
nodes.rationale: mdl/mdl.json is the project's semantic layer in MDL, the interchange format a BI or text-to-SQL layer consumes without being told internals. Generated from the knowledge graph by pf bootstrap — never hand-edited.

nodes.label: zenith-uk eval corpus
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests. Hand-written cases encode zenith-uk's own business rules no toolkit could guess. Nothing here is read by a sister, and nothing a sister writes is read here. Agents under test: test_failure_triage, freshness_triage, metric_gap_proposer. Any change to an agent prompt must keep these green.

nodes.label: Generated eval cases from toolkit templates
nodes.rationale: Each toolkit ships eval templates — the shape of a correct judgement with placeholders; pf evals-gen resolves those against this project's knowledge graph so cases name your models and columns. Regenerating overwrites the directory and deletes anything whose template is gone; never hand-edit a file in it.
nodes.norm_label: generated eval cases from toolkit templates

nodes.label: Mandatory why field on eval cases
nodes.rationale: why is not decoration — without it a corpus decays into assertions nobody dares change because nobody remembers whether they were deliberate.
nodes.norm_label: mandatory why field on eval cases

nodes.label: Weak prose matchers principle
nodes.rationale: Keep prose matchers weak (contains_any, not exact strings). A case that pins wording fails on a harmless rewrite, and a suite that cries wolf gets switched off — which costs more than the case was ever worth.

nodes.label: Prompt stability via --samples
nodes.rationale: --samples N runs each case N times. A case that passes 4 times in 5 is not passing and not failing — it is an unstable prompt, the most useful thing the suite can report before a prompt change ships.

nodes.label: zenith-uk AI risk register
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf air register; derived from the repository on every run — no verdict is stored. Coverage: 11 of 23 controls enforced, 9 not enforced, 3 unexercised. The committed baseline is empty, so pf air gate cannot block on it. On the gate denylist; catalogue pinned at 274760ccd058.

nodes.label: zenith-uk capabilities card
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf context build from the Capability declaration; never edited directly. Currently: no capabilities enabled.

nodes.label: Evidence BI reporting pipeline
nodes.rationale: BI-as-code generated by pf report build, never hand-maintained. Pipeline: dbt marts -> MetricFlow metrics -> MDL -> queries/metrics/*.sql -> pages/*.md. Generated pages, sources and config are overwritten on regeneration; durable narrative goes in an owned page or the metric description.

nodes.label: Pages never restate business logic
nodes.rationale: Every number traces to a metric compiled into queries/metrics/. If a dashboard needs a missing figure, the fix is a metric definition in transform/models/semantic/, not SQL in a page. Two pages filtering differently is how one company ends up with two revenues.

nodes.label: Ratio metrics re-divide at grain
nodes.rationale: Ratio queries carry numerator and denominator so a page re-divides at its own grain: sum(num)/sum(den). Never avg(ratio) — it is wrong at every grain except the one it was computed at, and it is the most common BI bug there is.

nodes.label: Evidence requires Node 20
nodes.rationale: Evidence 40 does not build on Node 24 / npm 11 — verified by building a pristine evidence-dev/template, which fails the same way, so this is Evidence's supported-runtime boundary rather than anything about this project. npm run sources and dev work on newer Node; npm run build needs 20. .nvmrc is committed.

nodes.label: Validated Evidence chart palette
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build. Palette values are validated — adjacent-pair CVD deltaE >= 8, normal-vision >= 15, contrast checked on both light and dark surfaces. Re-picking them by eye makes charts unreadable for ~8% of readers.

nodes.label: zenith-uk overview dashboard page
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build; a projection of the metric definitions in transform/models/semantic/. Every number on it is a governed metric compiled from the dbt semantic layer into queries/metrics/.

nodes.label: Evidence DuckDB source connector
nodes.rationale: Points at data/zenith_uk.duckdb. One warehouse file per project is what lets sister companies run in parallel; the reporting layer only ever reads.

nodes.label: zenith_uk dbt project config
nodes.rationale: macro-paths pulls platform/dbt/macros in as root-project macros, not a package: pf_clean dispatches to its clean_* siblings unqualified, and dbt namespaces package macros, so a package install fails on the inner dispatch. Elementary's observability models get +schema: elementary to keep them out of the marts; staging is views in a staging schema, marts are tables in a marts schema.

nodes.label: package-lock dbt_utils pin
nodes.rationale: Resolves dbt-labs/dbt_utils to exactly 1.4.1 with a sha1 hash.

nodes.label: zenith_uk dbt profile (dev/ci/prod/base)
nodes.rationale: Target selected by DBT_TARGET env var, defaulting to dev. dev/ci/base are DuckDB at PF_DUCKDB_PATH; only prod is Snowflake.

nodes.label: base comparison target
nodes.rationale: The comparison environment for a diff tool: same database file, different schema prefix, so base_marts.fct_revenue and main_marts.fct_revenue both exist and can be queried against each other in one connection. It has to be a separate materialisation — pointing a review tool at two sets of dbt artefacts that resolve to the same relation makes every value diff compare a table with itself and report clean, a false negative on every change, which is worse than having no review at all.

nodes.label: elementary edr profile (derived)
nodes.rationale: How the Elementary CLI (edr) reads the tables the dbt package writes. DERIVED from the project profile by pf tool elementary: one elementary output per project target, schema suffixed the way dbt composes custom schemas, so DBT_TARGET=prod edr report reads the production warehouse and the default reads dev. Regenerated by pf bootstrap — retarget the project, not this block.

nodes.label: prod Snowflake target
nodes.rationale: Every connection attribute is an env_var call (SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT, SNOWFLAKE_USER, SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH, SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD, SNOWFLAKE_ROLE, SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE, SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE, SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA) — no values are committed.

nodes.label: Generated Recce checks config
nodes.rationale: GENERATED by pf bootstrap; every check is derived: annotations.yaml maps column to ontology role, concepts.yaml maps role to review intent and pii flag, pf.tools.recce maps intent to check type. The way to change a check is to fix what the column means — a wrong check is a wrong role. Columns whose role is PII are excluded from every value-level check because the results land in recce_state.json, which is durable and shared. Currently ships row_count_diff and schema_diff checks.

nodes.label: metricflow_time_spine model
nodes.rationale: Daily time spine required by MetricFlow; materialized as a table with date_day at day granularity, tested unique and not_null.

nodes.label: zenith_shared dbt project config
nodes.rationale: The group-shared transform project (zenith_shared): macros only, holding what sister projects share at the group level.

nodes.label: pf Platform dbt Project
nodes.rationale: Minimal platform-level dbt project whose only job is exposing shared macros via macro-paths.

nodes.label: Control Plane Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: Three containers where there were five: postgresql (one database, two schemas), elasticsearch (OpenMetadata search index), and a combined stack image (OpenMetadata + Dagster + recce + nginx). PF_REPO must mount at the same path as on the host because Dagster's workspace.yaml holds absolute working_directory paths.

nodes.label: pf_postgresql Service
nodes.rationale: Pinned independently of OM_VERSION: following OpenMetadata's postgresql tag looks tidy but a Postgres major bump would meet the old data directory and refuse to start, taking both OpenMetadata and Dagster (same instance) down. Loopback-only publish; dev database with a published default password.

nodes.label: pf_elasticsearch Service
nodes.rationale: Independent of OM_VERSION for the opposite reason: OpenMetadata constrains which Elasticsearch majors it talks to, so this may need to move with an upgrade (PF_OM_REINDEX=recreate). Heap trimmed to 512m — the index holds ~1200 tables and a glossary; 1g starved the stack beside it.

nodes.label: pf_stack Service (OpenMetadata + Dagster + recce + nginx)
nodes.rationale: One combined image. OpenMetadata uses the public schema and Dagster the dagster schema of the same openmetadata_db. Own DAGSTER_HOME (.dagster-stack), not the repo's .dagster, so the host's instance config never names a database it cannot reach. Credentials come from .env, never baked into the image.

nodes.label: External Volumes Fail Loudly
nodes.rationale: Volumes are external on purpose: they hold the previous hand-started OpenMetadata stack's 1205 catalogued tables and search index. A compose-owned volume would silently start empty; external: true fails loudly if missing.

nodes.label: Party (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Abstract: any actor that can enter into an agreement.

nodes.label: Customer (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A party that buys; person or organization. Identity: customer_id.

nodes.label: Organization (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A legal entity; customers may belong to one.

nodes.label: Employee (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Internal actor, used for attribution.

nodes.label: Agreement (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Abstract: a commitment between parties, with a lifecycle.

nodes.label: Subscription (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A recurring agreement with a plan, term and status.

nodes.label: Order (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A one-off purchase commitment.

nodes.label: Contract (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A negotiated agreement, usually with custom terms.

nodes.label: Event (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Abstract: something that happened at a point in time. Immutable.

nodes.label: Payment (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Movement of money settling an agreement.

nodes.label: Refund (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Negative movement of money against a prior payment.

nodes.label: Usage (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Metered consumption attributable to an agreement.

nodes.label: Interaction (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A touchpoint (email, call, session) with a party.

nodes.label: Product (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A sellable thing; plans and SKUs are Products.

nodes.label: Location (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A geography: country, region, or address.

nodes.label: Currency (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: An ISO 4217 currency; qualifies every money amount.

nodes.label: Platform Ontology v2
nodes.rationale: v2 adds identity (which property identifies an instance — without it no join condition can be derived, so BI and MDL projections are guesses) and datatype properties on the class itself. Kept deliberately small: a 200-class upper ontology nobody maintains is worse than 15 classes everybody uses; groups select a subset in instance.yaml.

nodes.label: Column Semantic Roles
nodes.rationale: Every annotated column carries exactly one role. Each role's `review` intent (identity / distribution / categories / none) is tool-agnostic: the ontology states the question, each review tool translates it. Strings must declare whether they are categories or free text — guessing wrong makes every review noisy. pii: true forces review none, because a value-level diff would persist real PII into a durable shared state file.

nodes.label: Microsoft Ontology-Playground
nodes.rationale: External reference modelling the same class + datatype-property and OWL object-property pairs.

nodes.label: Topology v2 (Named Relations)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the flat from/to edge list with four load-bearing changes: relation names (MDL requires relationships[].name), OWL domain/range framing, MDL's cardinality enum verbatim (a '1:N' string needed translating, and translation is where direction gets silently flipped), and an inverse name so every relation reads both ways. The physical join condition is deliberately NOT here — derived at projection time from each project's links_to annotations, keeping the topology warehouse-independent.

nodes.label: MDL (WrenAI Modeling Definition Language)
nodes.rationale: The projection target for the semantic layer: requires named relationships and understands the ONE_TO_ONE | ONE_TO_MANY | MANY_TO_ONE | MANY_TO_MANY cardinality enum verbatim.

nodes.label: Control Plane UI (single-file)
nodes.rationale: Self-contained HTML+JS control plane: sidebar shell (replacing a 15-wide tab strip that wrapped and lost its selected state), light/dark theme tokens, and tabs for lineage, models, metrics, ontology, topology/policy chain, MDL, workspace, review, impact, PRs, tools, agents/spend, upstreams and context card. Charts use two panels sharing an x-axis, never one plot with two y-scales — a percentage and a count are different units.

nodes.label: loadAll
nodes.rationale: Startup loader; failure is logged as well as rendered because the tile row is inside the overview panel, which is not what you are looking at when a later tab failed.

nodes.label: drawGraph
nodes.rationale: Layered lineage rendering: five ordinal layer columns (ontology, raw, staging/intermediate, marts, semantic/consumption), shape per node kind, click runs impact analysis.

nodes.label: loadTopology
nodes.rationale: Renders topology relations and the policy chain; a policy whose enforcement resolves to nothing renders a NOTHING pill — unenforced policies are the interesting output.

nodes.label: loadWorkspace
nodes.rationale: Joins the recorded Recce diff to the semantic layer on the model, rather than leaving prediction and measurement side by side for the reader to correlate by eye. A zero only means 'nothing moved' once something has been measured; before that it is the absence of a number.

nodes.label: renderWsJoin
nodes.rationale: Legend that is also the filter: the count is the control. Status is never carried by colour alone — each row also states the word.

nodes.label: loadReview
nodes.rationale: Renders whichever enabled tool exposes an embeddable surface — discovered, not hardcoded: today Recce, tomorrow whatever was installed. Re-probed on tab open so a stale 'server down' never sends someone to debug a fixed problem.

nodes.label: Workspace Four-State Review Model
nodes.rationale: Four states, not two: moved (a difference was measured), held (checked, nothing moved), uncovered (published but no check covers it), unreviewed (no review has been run). Both held and uncovered look like 'no differences' if you only render the diff, and only one of them is reassuring.

nodes.label: Control Plane Web Entry (Vite/React)
nodes.rationale: Minimal Vite entry mounting /src/main.tsx into #root; same 'Data Platform — Control Plane' title as the single-file static UI.

nodes.label: Tool Precedence Order
nodes.rationale: Four upstream skill sets are merged and overlap; without this order an agent answers a governed metric question with ad-hoc SQL. Order: structure/lineage → kg tools and impact_analysis (never grep first); business metric → query_metrics (name the missing definition, never fall back to SQL); exploratory → read-only SQL, never staging when a mart covers the grain; cross-sister → _rollup via ATTACH READ_ONLY only; missing data → dlt-ingest. Raw SQL that recomputes a defined metric is a bug, not a shortcut.

nodes.label: Toolkit Index (generated)
nodes.rationale: Generated by `pf context build` — edit a toolkit's CONTEXT.md or a skill's frontmatter, never this file. Lists every toolkit, its skills and its rules.

nodes.label: Skill: build-assets (Dagster)
nodes.rationale: Never scaffold a Definitions object — a second Definitions silently shadows the factory's resources and is the most likely way to break the repo. The pipeline builds itself: sources/, dbt models and sisters maps are auto-discovered; definitions.py never changes after scaffolding. dbt models emit one asset per model, never one shelled-out dbt build — one opaque asset produces a node with no edges. Asset keys are project-prefixed because sisters have identically-named models across code locations. Adapted from dagster-io/skills (Apache-2.0).

nodes.label: Skill: contracts-and-access (dbt governance)
nodes.rationale: Contracts, groups, access and versions are dbt Core features — use them. access: private on staging/intermediate, public only on marts consumed outside the group. Mesh caveat: cross-project ref is dbt Cloud only — here the boundary is the project; sisters do not ref each other, cross-entity data flows through _rollup via ATTACH READ_ONLY. Declare exposures for every dashboard or impact analysis cannot name an owner.

nodes.label: Skill: troubleshoot-runs
nodes.rationale: No Cloud Jobs API; the equivalents are run_results.json (failed_nodes) and the Dagster run log. Classify before fixing: upstream_data / model_logic / stale_source / test_too_strict — 're-run it' is only correct for stale_source. A test that fails because the test is wrong is a real outcome; say so rather than contorting the model.

nodes.label: Skill: upgrade-and-migrate
nodes.rationale: Upgrade dbt Core by bumping the platform pin once (applies to every project), migrate to Fusion via dbtf parse, retarget the warehouse by changing only warehouse.py and the profile template. All three are plan-then-apply operations — never run from a chat turn.

nodes.label: Skill: fetch-docs
nodes.rationale: Prefer the local manifest over the internet; this is dbt Core + dbt-duckdb + MetricFlow CLI, so ignore dbt Cloud-only guidance (Semantic Layer API, Discovery API, Jobs API, cross-project ref) — the local equivalents are mf query, manifest.json, run_results.json and per-project isolation.

nodes.label: Skill: run-commands
nodes.rationale: Always run dbt via dbt_build/dbt_test/dbt_list so target and PF_DUCKDB_PATH are wired. state:modified+ is the CI selector and the input to impact analysis. Never --full-refresh from a chat turn — destructive operations go through pf plan → human review → pf apply.

nodes.label: dbt Layer Boundaries
nodes.rationale: staging owns cleaning (never joins, aggregation, grain changes); intermediate owns joins and reshaping (never exposed to BI); marts own grain and the physical table (never an aggregation policy); semantic owns metric definitions (never stores data). Enforced in review, and agents blur them constantly.

nodes.label: Skill: answer-with-metrics
nodes.rationale: The Cloud Semantic Layer API does not exist here; the equivalent is the MetricFlow CLI wrapped as query_metrics. If no metric covers the question, say so and name the missing definition — that gap report is how the semantic layer grows from real questions. Recomputing a defined metric in ad-hoc SQL is how one company ends up with four different revenues. Always state which metric and filter were used.

nodes.label: Skill: build-semantic-layer
nodes.rationale: The mart declares the grain; the semantic layer declares how to aggregate it. Derive agg_time_dimension from the column annotated event_time and measures from money_amount/quantity. Ratio and derived metrics compose existing metrics — never recompute a numerator in SQL. saved_queries with exports keep BI tables derived from the single definition.

nodes.label: dbt-snowflake Toolkit (portable sf_* macros)
nodes.rationale: Snowflake functions as dbt macros compiling to whatever the target adapter understands, so one set of models runs on DuckDB in development and Snowflake in production. The macros reproduce the SOURCE dialect's semantics, not the local warehouse's: sf_least returns NULL if any argument is NULL, sf_div0 returns 0 on a zero divisor, sf_datediff takes the part first. Each is asserted against a real dbt run. The sf_ prefix names the dialect the SQL came from; a BigQuery-origin project gets a sibling bq_* toolkit.

nodes.label: Ambiguous Dialect Functions
nodes.rationale: Functions whose meaning depends on which dialect wrote them are deliberately never translated automatically: date_trunc is (part, date) in Snowflake and (date, part) in BigQuery — both parse, one returns wrong dates silently. Listed in AMBIGUOUS in pf/onboard/dialect.py and reported by pf dialect for a human to resolve, because a wrong argument order compiles, runs, and produces numbers no review catches.

nodes.label: Skill: port-snowflake-sql
nodes.rationale: Start with the pf dialect report, not the SQL. Work ambiguous first and by hand (nothing fails, so nothing tells you), then the mechanical needs-wrapping pile (loud, cheap), then unsupported. Macro arguments are quoted SQL fragments — a bare identifier renders empty and fails to compile, the good kind of failure. Do not wrap what dbt-core already handles. New macros must pin the source dialect's answer in test_toolkit_macros.py.

nodes.label: Skill: add-tests
nodes.rationale: Generate tests from annotations rather than by hand — roles already declare intent (natural_key → unique + not_null, foreign_key → relationships, status_enum → accepted_values...). Severity deliberate: error on key/referential, warn on distribution; a test that always warns and is never fixed is noise. transform/tests/expectations/ is the generated floor — fix the role, never the file. A rule that cannot be written down is a monitor, not a test.

nodes.label: Skill: add-unit-test
nodes.rationale: Data tests check the output of a real run; unit tests check the logic against fixed inputs, catching a broken CASE branch current data never hits. Write one for every model encoding a business rule, and test-drive it: failing unit test first, then the SQL.

nodes.label: Skill: explore-data
nodes.rationale: Order: list_tables → display_schema → preview_table → aggregate with execute_sql_query. Read-only and truncated by policy; if capped, aggregate in SQL rather than asking for more rows. Stop and re-route to query_metrics if the question is a business-metric question. Notebooks read the project DuckDB file read-only and never write to the warehouse.

nodes.label: Stripe Connector Registry Entry
nodes.rationale: Verified source stripe_analytics; maps charges to Payment, customers to Customer, subscriptions to Subscription, all incremental on created. Notes: amounts arrive in minor units (divide by 100 in staging); Stripe status enum drifts when new states are added, caught by the status_enum monitor.

nodes.label: DuckDB Single-Writer Constraint
nodes.rationale: DuckDB allows a single writer per database file. This constraint is why the platform gives every project its own file and its own Dagster writer pool -- it is what makes sister companies genuinely parallel. Never propose a shared file for multiple writers.

nodes.label: elementary-observe Toolkit Context
nodes.rationale: Every dbt build records itself into main_elementary (the elementary tool is on by default); these skills are how that recording gets used rather than merely collected.

nodes.label: Test vs Monitor Distinction
nodes.rationale: A test asserts a rule; a monitor learns a baseline from history and flags departures. Add monitors exactly where a rule cannot be written down (volumes, freshness, distributions). Anomaly monitors are severity: warn because an anomaly is a question, not a verdict -- a monitor that pages on every marketing campaign gets deleted.

nodes.label: add-anomaly-tests Skill
nodes.rationale: Monitors are chosen from the ontology role, not guessed: event_time gives timestamp_column, the table gets volume_anomalies, status_enum/geo/booleans get dimension_anomalies, money_amount gets column_anomalies, contract-critical tables get schema_changes. Declared in the model's own yml because it is a judgement about one table. Build twice before trusting -- first build passes vacuously. Never monitor a PII column's values: value-level metrics would put real values into the durable shared main_elementary schema.

nodes.label: triage-observability Skill
nodes.rationale: Triage queries the recorded history (main_elementary tables), not the log of whichever run failed: one failure is an incident, the history says whether it is new, recurring or flaky, and those get different fixes. Verdicts: upstream_data, model_logic, stale_source, test_too_strict, expected_anomaly. An anomaly you cannot classify is a finding -- report it as unexplained. A monitor acknowledged every week is a broken monitor or an unowned problem.

nodes.label: Immutable Record Principle
nodes.rationale: Never edit main_elementary tables or transform/edr_target: the record of what happened is gate-denied for the same reason provenance/** is -- you may not edit the record of what you did. The report is regenerated, never patched.

nodes.label: Metric-First Reporting Principle
nodes.rationale: Every number on a page traces to a metric in queries/metrics/. A figure with no metric is a metric PR, not page SQL.

nodes.label: Ratio Re-Division Rule
nodes.rationale: Never avg(ratio). Ratio queries carry numerator and denominator so pages re-divide at their own grain: sum(num)/sum(den).

nodes.label: Status Never Colour Alone
nodes.rationale: Every verdict renders a dot and the word (see src/components/Verdict.tsx): screenshots get printed and pasted into tickets, and roughly one reader in twelve cannot separate the red from the green.

nodes.label: A Zero Is Not a Result
nodes.rationale: Distinguish 'checked, found nothing' from 'nothing checked it'. A green nought over an unmeasured project is a clean bill of health nobody issued.
nodes.norm_label: a zero is not a result

nodes.label: Entity Isolation Principle
nodes.rationale: Never read another group or a sister project; cross-entity work happens only in _rollup. Business logic does not transfer between entities -- an assumption carried across is a bug.

nodes.label: Graph-Before-Files Principle
nodes.rationale: kg_search costs a few hundred tokens; reading four models to find the same edge costs thousands and is likelier to be wrong. impact_analysis before changing any column, model or metric.

nodes.label: Read-Only Verifier Principle
nodes.rationale: The verification subagents are read-only by construction: a verifier that can edit stops being a second opinion and becomes a second author. If one finds a fault, it reports; the main session fixes.

nodes.label: Found-None vs No-Impact Distinction
nodes.rationale: Never say 'no impact' when what you mean is 'I found none' -- state which one it is. An empty result from an empty or stale graph is not evidence; compare the graph's mtime against the newest model file and declare the verification incomplete if stale.

nodes.label: secrets-auditor agent
nodes.rationale: Read-only subagent that hunts leaked credentials and PII; never prints a secret it finds, only location and shape, so the report is safe to paste into a ticket.

nodes.label: Exposed / Exposable / Placeholder triage
nodes.rationale: Remediation differs by class: exposed credentials must be rotated before removal because deleting a file does not un-expose git history; exposable paths need the gate rule fixed before the next run collects secrets; placeholders are named explicitly so nobody re-audits them.

nodes.label: semantic-conformance agent
nodes.rationale: Checks that the semantic claims a project makes are still true — not whether the SQL runs, but whether what it says it means holds. Unverifiable is a legitimate result; silence about it is not.

nodes.label: Semantic chain: ontology to annotation to model to metric to contract
nodes.rationale: Meaning flows link by link; break any link and everything downstream is decoration. A resource annotated after models were written has causality backwards — meaning reverse-engineered from models rather than models derived from meaning.
nodes.norm_label: semantic chain: ontology to annotation to model to metric to contract

nodes.label: Conformed dimensions belong to the group
nodes.rationale: Two sisters with private definitions of the same dimension will eventually disagree about a customer and neither will be obviously wrong; a local re-implementation is a finding — compare against the group, never a sister project.
nodes.norm_label: conformed dimensions belong to the group

nodes.label: sql-reviewer agent
nodes.rationale: Reviews compiled dbt SQL (not the Jinja) for correctness faults, ranked by how often each is actually wrong; every finding names the wrong answer it produces as a concrete scenario, with a query that demonstrates the fault and passes after the fix.

nodes.label: Grain uniqueness verification
nodes.rationale: A mart whose declared meta.grain is not unique is the single most common cause of double-counted metrics downstream. Verify with select grain, count(*) group by all having count(*) > 1 rather than trusting the declaration.

nodes.label: Faults that produce wrong numbers without erroring
nodes.rationale: The dangerous fault class errors nowhere: join fanout multiplying rows before aggregates, an inner join silently dropping rows, a left join with a where on the right table acting as inner, not-in with a nullable subquery returning no rows, a wrong incremental unique_key corrupting data over time rather than failing once.
nodes.norm_label: faults that produce wrong numbers without erroring

nodes.label: Architecture as checkable claims
nodes.rationale: In this platform architecture is not a diagram but a set of claims the graph can check; review means finding the claims that are no longer true.

nodes.label: Declared joins (links plus topology)
nodes.rationale: Every foreign key must be declared as links={col: SomeClass} AND the topology must already relate the two classes — one without the other is the common half-failure where nothing is derivable. An undeclared join is a join whose condition was guessed; pf check fails on it, the highest-value signal in the review.

nodes.label: /ast-grep command
nodes.rationale: Structural, syntax-aware search for when regex would match the wrong thing. Not installed by default — say so and fall back to Grep rather than silently degrading. Scope to one project or platform/; a bare dot walks vendor/ and .venv and crosses entity boundaries. The graph outranks both search tools for dependency questions.

nodes.label: Blast radius / impact_analysis
nodes.rationale: pf impact / impact_analysis reports downstream reach, not a verdict. The dangerous class is metrics: a metric depending on a changed column changes value silently — nothing errors, the number is just different. Changes reaching published contracts (mdl.json, openmetadata.json) affect external consumers and must be announced, not just merged.

nodes.label: Empty blast radius trichotomy
nodes.rationale: An empty result means one of three non-equivalent things: nothing depends on it (proceed), the graph lacks the node (rebuild and re-ask), or there is no graph at all — then the gate is inert and every edit is unverified. Never treat silence as safety.

nodes.label: Enforced context budget (pf tokens)
nodes.rationale: Over budget is a build failure, not a warning, because every session pays the preamble for the whole life of the project. Repair by regenerating the card, not trimming by hand; if still over, the fix is fewer better entries, not a bigger budget.

nodes.label: Graph queries instead of file reads
nodes.rationale: The cheapest large-context strategy is not loading the context: kg_neighbors instead of reading four models, kg_search instead of grepping for a concept, impact_analysis instead of reading downstream models — and never reading a sister project at all.
nodes.norm_label: graph queries instead of file reads

nodes.label: /gemini-analyze command
nodes.rationale: Hands a repo-sized question to Gemini's large context window instead of compacting the session. Read-only; never include secrets since @ inlines file contents into a third-party request. Treat output as a lead, not a finding — verify each claim against the file it names.

nodes.label: Large-context delegation scope rule
nodes.rationale: Run gemini from the active project directory and never pass @ paths reaching another group or sister; --all_files from the repo root sweeps every entity — exactly the cross-entity read the gate exists to prevent — and drags vendor/ and .venv into the prompt.

nodes.label: Measure before recommending
nodes.rationale: dbt already recorded the timing in run_results.json — read it, do not re-run. The top three slowest rows are the audit; everything below them is noise until those are addressed. A plausible optimisation targeting the wrong stage is worse than none.

nodes.label: PII check on committed recce_state.json
nodes.rationale: The repo deliberately commits transform/recce_state.json, and value_diff checks write compared row values into it. That is only safe while PII columns (email, phone, name, address, dob, ssn, iban, card) stay excluded from those checks — a hit is critical because the values are already in git history.

nodes.label: Gate coverage as holes, not rules
nodes.rationale: The question is not what the gate denies but what it fails to deny: every generator-written artefact must be on the denylist (otherwise drift reappears as a hand edit the next regeneration discards silently), every denylist_except entry must be a deliberate still-true exception.
nodes.norm_label: gate coverage as holes, not rules

nodes.label: Ordered ship sequence
nodes.rationale: Each step produces the input for the next; a failure stops the sequence rather than being noted and passed over. A commit that does two things cannot be reverted for one of them. A denied path is not a thing to argue with; the pre-commit hook re-running the gate is right when it blocks — --no-verify is not part of this workflow.

nodes.label: Inert governance as the costliest debt
nodes.rationale: Debt in a data platform is mostly governance that went inert: a gate that cannot fire, a graph that no longer matches the models, a contract nobody regenerated. A stale graph is worse than none because it reports a blast radius that is wrong. Anything that makes a gate inert is silently disabling a control — the only debt that gets worse without being touched.
nodes.norm_label: inert governance as the costliest debt

nodes.label: project-onboarding rules
nodes.rationale: The toolkit's binding rules: the stage order is a dependency not a preference; implement addresses one finding per iteration; maker and checker must not be the same agent; three failures open a circuit breaker to escalate, never clear; never --force past a blocker except for a later stage's findings.

nodes.label: onboard-project skill
nodes.rationale: Onboarding is not a prompt, it is a loop you design and then run: adopting the files is cheap; making the project mean something — ontology, layers, metrics, review discipline — is the work. Names its own three failure modes: verification quietly becoming manual, comprehension debt, and cognitive surrender after the fortieth green check.

nodes.label: Gated onboarding ladder
nodes.rationale: import, ontology, dialect, layers, metrics, review — the order is a dependency: annotations cannot be written against SQL that will not compile, metrics cannot precede the marts they measure, recce cannot diff a project that never built. Out of order, every stage is redone when the one beneath it lands. pf align status re-derives every stage from disk and never reads a stored verdict, because a recorded pass outlives the change that invalidated it.

nodes.label: Maker/checker separation (validate vs verify)
nodes.rationale: validate asks is the project correct now; verify asks is the change that got it there one we would accept. Both must pass and they catch different things — a project passes every gate if you delete the failing test. The checker's default stance is no; it cannot check intent, so the implementing agent must never be the verifying agent.

nodes.label: Three-failure circuit breaker
nodes.rationale: Every validate result is written to loop-ledger.json; three consecutive failures of a stage open a breaker. Deliberate: an agent re-reading 'max three attempts' cannot know it is on the fourth, and a count held in conversation resets on restart. A finding that survived three implement phases is a decision someone has to make, not a bug being failed at — pf loop reset is for after the decision, not instead of it.

nodes.label: Unexercised is not a pass
nodes.rationale: unexercised is what a check reports when the tool that would decide it is not installed. Reporting it green is the difference between an onboarding that was verified and one that was assumed — yet it also must not close the gate, because a missing CLI must not wall a project off from the ladder.

nodes.label: Entity boundary rule
nodes.rationale: Never read another group or another sister project: business logic does not transfer between entities, and an assumption carried across is a bug that is invisible in review because it looks like knowledge. Escalate business meaning, never guess it — which of two revenue definitions a company means is not inferable from its SQL.

nodes.label: Stage 1: import
nodes.rationale: Goal: the repository is here, every model name is unique, no dbt built-in overridden. Deliberately leaves behind profiles.yml (the platform owns targets), generate_schema_name (its usual override collapses schemas and defeats the layer separation the graph and impact gate read), build artefacts, and unpinned unused packages. A new group asserts a shared ontology instance, conformed dimensions and a meaningful roll-up — folding an unrelated company in to save a directory is how conformed dimensions stop conforming.

nodes.label: Stage 2: ontology, topology, annotations
nodes.rationale: First for a reason: annotations drive generated staging, currency normalisation, PII policy, the knowledge graph, the MDL projection and the impact gate — modelling before annotating means modelling against a vocabulary nobody has agreed on yet. Roles are the contract; a mart is not annotated because that would give a definition two homes.

nodes.label: Ontology / topology / annotations split
nodes.rationale: Ontology (what kinds of thing exist) is warehouse-independent; topology names how kinds relate; the binding to physical columns lives only in per-project annotations — which is why the same topology serves sister companies whose tables look nothing alike.

nodes.label: Ontology proposal flow (scan / review / approve)
nodes.rationale: When the ontology has no word for it, do not force a bad fit — annotating a supplier as Organization makes the validator pass and every downstream projection wrong. pf semantic scan induces a proposal, review shows the diff, approve merges into the group extension (not the platform ontology) so a new concept reaches the sisters that need it without imposing on every company. Approving is a human decision.

nodes.label: Stage 3: dialect — one SQL, two targets
nodes.rationale: The same models compile on DuckDB in development and on the production warehouse and mean the same on both. Development is DuckDB because a developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project. There are not two copies of the SQL — a per-warehouse fork diverges on the first bug fix.
nodes.norm_label: stage 3: dialect — one sql, two targets

nodes.label: Ambiguous cross-dialect functions
nodes.rationale: Two failure classes, not equally dangerous: unsupported functions (iff, nvl, div0) fail the build loudly and cost minutes; ambiguous ones compile and run on both sides and return a different number, costing a dashboard — least(1, NULL) is NULL in Snowflake and 1 in DuckDB, datediff and date_trunc swap argument order between dialects. Give the ambiguous findings the attention: they are already running and can already be wrong.

nodes.label: Portable sf_* dispatch macros
nodes.rationale: Macros from platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake use adapter.dispatch so one call compiles to whatever the target understands — and they pin the source dialect's semantics everywhere, which is the point: sf_least(1, NULL) is NULL on DuckDB too. Three deliberately differ from DuckDB natives (sf_least, sf_div0, sf_safe_divide); do not 'fix' them. Missing macros are added from a platform session, never a project one.

nodes.label: Stage 4: layers — staging, marts, semantic
nodes.rationale: Goal: every model sits in the layer whose rules it obeys. intermediate/ maps to marts/ — not a demotion: an intermediate model is a mart nothing exposes yet, and internal-vs-published is a tag, not a directory. A join in staging hides a business decision in a layer the platform treats as mechanical, and gen-staging will overwrite it.

nodes.label: Four-layer contract (staging / marts / semantic / utils)
nodes.rationale: Each layer is a contract, not a folder: staging is 1:1 with raw (no joins, no aggregation), marts declare a grain, semantic is MetricFlow YAML only. The knowledge graph derives lineage depth from them, the PII audit only flags columns reaching a mart, the impact gate weighs mart changes more heavily, and the semantic layer treats marts/ as measurable — a model in the wrong layer is reasoned about wrongly by four different tools.

nodes.label: Config re-keying after directory moves
nodes.rationale: dbt_project.yml blocks are keyed by directory: after a move, a block naming a directory that no longer exists silently stops applying every tag under it — the build is green and the tags are gone. Verify by counting tagged nodes in the manifest, not by reading the YAML.

nodes.label: Stage 5: MetricFlow metrics
nodes.rationale: A mart nothing measures is a table. The semantic model binds a mart to entities, dimensions and measures — the ontology-stage annotations say which column is which: natural_key becomes the primary entity, links become foreign entities, event_time the agg_time_dimension, money_amount a measure.

nodes.label: One definition per business quantity
nodes.rationale: The point of the semantic layer is that revenue has exactly one definition — the alternative is two dashboards filtering differently and nobody able to say which is right. Compose (ratio, derived with offset) rather than recompute: recomputing is how the second definition gets in. Definitions come from the source repository's own KPI marts and analyses, cited in the description — inventing a revenue definition for a company onboarded this morning is exactly the guess the platform says to escalate.

nodes.label: Stage 6: Recce review
nodes.rationale: Goal: the difference between what was there and what is there now has been looked at. Look at row counts on every mart, then value diffs on the models wrapped in the dialect stage (the highest-yield checks in the whole ladder), then schema diffs where models moved layers. Record the outcome in decisions/ — a diff nobody wrote up is a diff nobody looked at three months from now.

nodes.label: Recce diff between built states
nodes.rationale: Every prior stage was supposed to be behaviour-preserving; lineage says what could break, only a diff says what did. Recce compares two built states — the base target writes the same DuckDB file under a base schema so both states are reachable from one connection and the seeds load once.

nodes.label: quality-stack skill
nodes.rationale: Every dbt project answers three questions with evidence, not vibes: did my change move the numbers (recce), does the data hold what the ontology asserts (dbt-expectations), what has been true over time (elementary). All three are pluggable tools: one tools.yaml decision per family, everything else derived — never hand-wire what bootstrap derives. Declaration is not proof: run the derivation chain and check each link.

nodes.label: Coverage is annotation
nodes.rationale: A mart with no generated expectations and no recce value checks is an unannotated mart — the fix is contracts/annotations.yaml, then re-derive: that one edit updates tests, review checks and monitors together. Judgements stay human: anomaly monitors and sharper expectations go in the model's own yml.

nodes.label: dignified-python skill
nodes.rationale: Production Python conventions adapted from dagster-io/skills dignified-python (Apache-2.0): 3.11-3.12 typing, LBYL over blanket except, pathlib everywhere, comment constraints the code cannot show, match the surrounding file's idiom rather than importing a house style.

nodes.label: Lazy-import heavy optional deps
nodes.rationale: dlt, dagster and dbt are imported inside functions rather than at module top so the platform core works without them installed.

nodes.label: Form first, colour last
nodes.rationale: Most bad charts are chosen the other way round, and no palette rescues the wrong form. The data's job picks the type; never a dual-axis chart — two measures of different scale become two charts, small multiples, or an index to a common base.

nodes.label: Theme-invariant mermaid styling
nodes.rationale: GitHub renders one mermaid source on both light and dark pages and does not recolour explicit classDef fills — so use pale fill + saturated stroke of the same hue + near-black ink. Escape every interpolated string (# opens an entity reference, quotes end the label, angle brackets are silently parsed as tags under htmlLabels). Never derive node ids from data: two boxes sharing an id are merged without error and a layer quietly vanishes.

nodes.label: validate-references pre-commit hook
nodes.rationale: Local pre-commit hook in the vendored FINOS AI Governance Framework: runs scripts/validate-references.py over docs/_data/references/*.yml to enforce the standard reference schema (title, description, entries).

nodes.label: Use-Case-Led Threat Modelling Approach
nodes.rationale: Deliberate trade-off: focus on a subset of the problem via concrete use cases to deliver a complete vertical slice early, leverage existing FS technology-risk frameworks rather than inventing new ones, and use threat modelling to map risks to mitigations.

nodes.label: Consensus-Based Decision Making
nodes.rationale: Agreement of all participants is preferred but not required; maintainers determine consensus in good faith based on dominant view and nature of objections. Appeals go via PR or issue. A fast-track lane lets maintainers merge non-material changes (docs, CI/CD, build) at personal discretion, avoiding consensus overhead where it adds no value.

nodes.label: Risk-Mitigation Cross-Linking (mitigates list)
nodes.rationale: The relationship is deliberately one-way: mitigations declare a mitigates list of risk ids (ri-N); risk files carry no mitigations section. Backlinks are computed by brute-force looping over document objects matching sequence numbers, so link authors never have to track title-suffixed filenames.

nodes.label: AIR-* Numbering Convention
nodes.rationale: Risks are numbered AIR-<risk_type>-<number> and mitigations AIR-<mitigation_type>-<number>; the ids are generated dynamically by the risk-id.html and mitigation-id.html templates from file metadata, with the type vocabularies defined centrally in _config.yml so ids stay consistent across the site.

nodes.norm_label: document status lifecycle (pre-draft / draft / working-group-approved / approved-specification)

nodes.label: Heuristic GenAI Risk Identification Framework
nodes.rationale: An eight-step guided question set (define use case and context, identify data, model and technology, output and decision impact, regulatory mapping, security considerations, controls identification, decision and documentation) so stakeholders systematically evaluate a GenAI use case before deployment. Context frames risk tolerance: internal advisory tools tolerate more error than customer-facing or automated decision systems; review intervals (~6 months) are mandated because AI risk profiles change fast.

nodes.label: AIGF Value Proposition
nodes.rationale: Why AIGF exists despite ISO and NIST: financial-services-specific focus (model risk, auditability, regulated environments), faster community-driven open-source evolution, reference implementations and tooling (open source controls in Common Cloud Controls), FS regulatory mapping as a first-class feature, and direct regulator engagement within the community.

nodes.label: Use Case Proposal Form
nodes.rationale: Client-side only by design: the form builds YAML front matter mirroring existing use-case files and opens a pre-filled GitHub issue in a new tab, so no data is sent to any server and maintainers can copy the YAML directly into a new .md file.

nodes.label: LLM Workflow Patterns (Prompt Chaining, Routing, Parallelization, Orchestrator-Workers, Evaluator-Optimizer)
nodes.rationale: Workflow patterns are deliberately kept separate from agent patterns: in workflows control flow is defined in predefined code paths, whereas in agent patterns control flow emerges from LLM decisions. The split follows Anthropic's Building Effective Agents taxonomy.
nodes.norm_label: llm workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer)

nodes.label: Payment Authentication Data (SAD never-store rule)
nodes.rationale: Sensitive Authentication Data is classified separately from cardholder data because no compensating controls exist: PCI DSS prohibits post-authorisation storage regardless of encryption, so the classification prescribes in-memory processing only.

nodes.label: Reference Data Schema
nodes.rationale: Entry keys must be stable kebab-case identifiers, based on the regulation's official numbering scheme where one exists, because mapping files cross-reference them - renaming a key is a breaking change. Sections and tiers are expressed as comments between entries rather than structural grouping to keep the schema flat.

nodes.rationale: Renders the two-column risk/mitigation catalogue with client-side search, type and category (OP/SEC/RC risk, PREV/DET mitigation) filtering, and expand/collapse of either column; summaries are derived by splitting page content on Summary/Purpose/Description headings.

nodes.label: AIR Mitigation ID Formatter
nodes.rationale: Generates the canonical AIR-{type}-{zero-padded sequence} mitigation identifiers (e.g. AIR-DET-021) that the data platform's policy.yaml controls: lists reference.

nodes.label: Reference Entry Card Include
nodes.rationale: Implements the reverse crosswalk: for one reference entry it scans all risks and mitigations whose {dataset}_references frontmatter cites the entry key, and deliberately produces no output when nothing maps to it.

nodes.label: AIR Risk ID Formatter
nodes.rationale: Generates the canonical AIR-{type}-{zero-padded sequence} risk identifiers used across the catalogue and crosswalk pages.

nodes.label: Default Layout
nodes.rationale: Base HTML shell for the FINOS AI Governance Framework site (air-governance-framework.finos.org); loads Bootstrap 5.3.2 and declares the CC-BY-4.0 licence in the footer.

nodes.label: Mitigation Page Layout
nodes.rationale: Renders one mitigation with sidebars for Key Risks (matched via 'ri-{sequence}' prefixes in page.mitigates), Related Mitigations ('mi-{sequence}'), External Controls, and a Regulatory & Standards References card iterating every dataset in site.data.references.

nodes.label: Reference Page Layout
nodes.rationale: Renders one regulatory framework page from site.data.references[page.dataset], emitting a reference-entry-card per entry so each article/control shows the AIGF risks and mitigations that cite it.

nodes.label: Risk Page Layout
nodes.rationale: Renders one risk with Related Risks, Key Mitigations (mitigations whose 'mitigates' contains 'ri-{sequence}'), and a Regulatory & Standards References card iterating every dataset in site.data.references.

nodes.label: Use Case Page Layout
nodes.rationale: Renders one use case (UC-nnn) with data classifications, jurisdiction-badged regulations (SR 11-7, EU AI Act), standards (NIST AI 600-1, FFIEC, ISO 42001, NIST SP 800-53r5), further reading, and related risks/mitigations.

nodes.label: Data Filtering From External Knowledge Bases (mi-2)
nodes.rationale: Filtering must happen before embedding: once data is converted to embeddings in a vector store it becomes opaque to traditional security tooling and cannot be retroactively filtered or access-controlled.
nodes.norm_label: data filtering from external knowledge bases (mi-2)

nodes.label: User/App/Model Firewalling/Filtering (mi-3)
nodes.rationale: Static filters catch well-defined patterns only; nuanced attacks need an LLM judge. Streaming outputs conflict with complete output filtering, so on-the-fly detection with cancel-and-remove accepts a brief exposure window as a deliberate trade-off.

nodes.label: AI System Alerting and Denial of Wallet (DoW) / Spend Monitoring (mi-9)
nodes.rationale: Consumption-based AI pricing creates Denial-of-Wallet exposure; five stacked control levels (enterprise cap down to per-key token quotas) trade bluntness against granularity.
nodes.norm_label: ai system alerting and denial of wallet (dow) / spend monitoring (mi-9)

nodes.label: AI Model Version Pinning (mi-10)
nodes.rationale: Pinning is not about avoiding upgrades but forcing a controlled, testable upgrade path: stability and predictability are prioritized over model freshness because unvetted version changes can silently shift behaviour, bias and security posture.

nodes.label: Role-Based Access Control for AI Data (mi-12)
nodes.norm_label: role-based access control for ai data (mi-12)

nodes.label: Providing Citations and Source Traceability for AI-Generated Information (mi-13)
nodes.rationale: Citations are only feasible for RAG-attributable claims; abstractive parametric generation must be flagged as uncitable rather than given fabricated citations. A citation proves the source of a statement, not the truth of the source.
nodes.norm_label: providing citations and source traceability for ai-generated information (mi-13)

nodes.label: Encryption of AI Data at Rest (mi-14)
nodes.rationale: Vector databases are new enough that default encryption postures vary widely; in-memory operation (e.g. FAISS) is no substitute for encryption once anything is persisted.
nodes.norm_label: encryption of ai data at rest (mi-14)

nodes.label: Using Large Language Models for Automated Evaluation (LLM-as-a-Judge) (mi-15)
nodes.rationale: Judge LLMs scale evaluation where human review cannot, but the judge itself has biases and must be calibrated against human SME judgments; it augments rather than replaces human oversight.
nodes.norm_label: using large language models for automated evaluation (llm-as-a-judge) (mi-15)

nodes.label: Preserving Source Data Access Controls in AI Systems (mi-16)
nodes.rationale: System-prompt-based access control is explicitly rejected as insecure and easily bypassed by adversarial prompting; enforcement must live in the data stores, metadata query-time filtering, or the application layer.
nodes.norm_label: preserving source data access controls in ai systems (mi-16)

nodes.label: Agent Authority Least Privilege Framework (mi-18)
nodes.rationale: Static RBAC is insufficient for agents that autonomously choose tools; privileges must adjust dynamically to context, transaction value and time bounds, with the tool manager as the enforcement point.

nodes.label: MCP Server Security Governance (mi-20)
nodes.rationale: Tiered adoption: start with a centrally-administered MCP proxy, allowlist and human-in-the-loop approval, progressing to distributed many-to-many only as maturity grows; the proxy trades a single point of failure for governable supply-chain control.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Isolation and Segmentation (mi-22)
nodes.rationale: At scale, monitoring inter-agent interactions may itself require dedicated monitoring agents - the monitoring workload is distributed with the multi-agent system.

nodes.label: Prompt Injection (ri-10)
nodes.rationale: LLMs do not distinguish instructions from data, so injection is broader and less predictable than SQL injection; it needs no privileges, making it the most accessible LLM attack vector.

nodes.label: Tool Manager
nodes.rationale: The component mediating between agents and external APIs/tools, translating agent requests into concrete API calls; chosen as the critical authorization enforcement point because every call passes through it.

nodes.label: Canary Tokens (Honey Tokens)
nodes.rationale: Deception-based detection: uniquely identifiable non-sensitive markers embedded in data streams sent to AI models, then monitored for on public and dark web sources as leak tripwires.

nodes.label: Denial of Wallet (DoW) Attack
nodes.rationale: Attack targeting consumption-based AI pricing: exhausting service budgets through excessive resource use, causing suspension or financial impact rather than classic denial of service.

nodes.label: Indirect Prompt Injection
nodes.rationale: Malicious instructions hidden in third-party content (documents, websites, emails) later ingested by the model; especially dangerous in automated and multi-agent workflows where it can hijack decision-making.

nodes.label: Two-Way Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: Frames third-party hosted LLM interactions: neither the data sent for inference nor the output received can be trusted by default, so controls are needed on both directions of the exchange.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
nodes.rationale: Grounds LLM responses in retrieved institutional knowledge to reduce hallucination, at the cost of new attack and leakage surfaces in the retrieval layer (embeddings, vector stores, retrieved-content injection).

nodes.label: Model Risk Management (SR 11-7 / PRA SS1-23)
nodes.rationale: Jurisdictions diverge: PRA SS1/23 pulls generative and agentic AI into model risk management, while the 2026 US interagency revision (OCC Bulletin 2026-13) explicitly excludes GenAI/agentic systems from SR 11-7 scope, shifting US obligations to fair-lending, FCRA, FFIEC third-party and state AI law.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
nodes.rationale: MCP extends agent capabilities through external servers; centralized proxy architectures with pre-approved servers reduce the attack surface relative to decentralized many-to-many MCP deployments.

nodes.label: Dual-Loop Orchestration (System 1 / System 2)
nodes.rationale: System 1 (fast path) generates investment plans; System 2 (metacognitive reflection) critiques them against long-term client constraints before execution, so compelling short-term signals cannot override fiduciary constraints established months earlier.

nodes.label: Graph-Based Memory (Mem0)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over flat vector storage so contradictory context (e.g. 'user wants crypto' vs 'user is risk-averse') is structured and prioritized, preventing context dilution; the concentrated client relationship graph in turn requires TEE isolation.

nodes.label: Loan Approval Use Case (UC-3)
nodes.rationale: Automates end-to-end loan evaluation, approval, pricing, documentation, and disbursement to cut cycle time while preserving human oversight for borderline, suspicious, or policy-sensitive cases. Regulatory drivers: EU AI Act high-risk classification for creditworthiness, ECOA/fair lending adverse-action explanations, GDPR Article 22 safeguards for automated decisions.

nodes.label: Hybrid Multi-Agent Loan Approval Workflow
nodes.rationale: A hybrid hierarchical and parallel multi-agent design: a loan approval orchestrator coordinates specialist agents for document intelligence, fraud detection, compliance review, credit risk assessment, dynamic pricing, and document generation. Chosen so document-heavy, manually intensive underwriting is parallelized while human review checkpoints stay in the loop.

nodes.label: Deterministic Policy Gates
nodes.rationale: AI agent outputs are probabilistic and not guaranteed repeatable, so consistency is enforced by deterministic underwriting thresholds and policy rules rather than by the agents themselves. Also the primary control for non-deterministic behaviour: model version pinning offers limited durability because hosted providers deprecate versions within months, so regression and re-baselining tests run whenever an underlying model changes.

nodes.label: Information Leaked to Hosted Model (ri-1)
nodes.rationale: Material when document intelligence, fraud detection, credit scoring, or pricing agents use third-party hosted models over identity, income, credit, and financial records.

nodes.label: Hallucination and Inaccurate Outputs (ri-4)
nodes.rationale: Document intelligence and credit risk agents may extract wrong values or fabricate data; mitigated with source citations, confidence thresholds, deterministic validation rules, and human review of low-confidence outputs.

nodes.label: Non-Deterministic Behaviour (ri-6)
nodes.rationale: LLM sampling plus multi-agent interaction can yield different recommendations for similar applications even with prompts, models, tools, and context held constant.

nodes.label: Inadequate System Alignment (ri-14)
nodes.rationale: Agents may optimize for speed, approval rate, or pricing outcomes against fair lending, risk appetite, or customer protection; countered with policy constraints, supervisor-agent controls, human review thresholds, compliance gates, and acceptance testing.

nodes.label: Lack of Explainability (ri-17)
nodes.rationale: Applicants, officers, and regulators need understandable reasons for approval, rejection, pricing, and manual review; mitigated with decision audit trails, source traceability, adverse action reason mapping, and separating AI recommendations from deterministic policy rules.

nodes.label: Data Quality and Drift (ri-19)
nodes.rationale: Arises from stale bureau data, macroeconomic shifts, document format changes, and evolving fraud typologies.

nodes.label: Anti-Financial Crime Investigation Use Case (UC-4)
nodes.rationale: GenAI assists L2 AML investigators across alert triage, case enrichment, adverse media screening, typology matching, disposition support, narrative generation, and STR/SAR drafting. GenAI drafts, summarizes, retrieves, and recommends but never closes an alert, decides not to file, or submits a report autonomously: the investigator stays accountable for every disposition and the MLRO/BSA officer for every filing. Regulatory frame: BSA/FinCEN 31 CFR 1020.320 (30/60-day SAR deadlines and confidentiality), EU AMLR 2024/1624 with the Article 73 tipping-off prohibition, FATF R.20/R.21, EU AI Act Articles 10/12/13/14 as internal benchmark, and SR 11-7 successor SR 26-2 model risk management.

nodes.label: STR/SAR Confidentiality and Tipping-Off
nodes.rationale: Sending case content, draft narratives, or alert metadata to a third-party hosted model, or persisting it in shared vector stores or provider logs, is treated as potential unlawful disclosure rather than a privacy incident, because leakage revealing that a filing exists can itself breach SAR confidentiality and tipping-off prohibitions. Controls must still allow disclosures authorized under 31 CFR 1020.320(e).

nodes.label: MLRO/BSA Officer Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Close recommendations are advisory-only and the MLRO/BSA approval gate sits outside the AI system's authority, because the workflow rests on statutory obligations with personal accountability; monitoring of agreement rates, edit distance, escalation rates, and narrative similarity guards against rubber-stamping under volume pressure.

nodes.label: AI in Finance Use Case Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical taxonomy of AI/ML/GenAI financial use cases across six domains: customer and relationship management, risk and compliance, investment and portfolio management, operations, strategic insights, and cross-cutting capabilities (feature stores, MLOps, privacy-preserving AI, adversarial robustness, drift monitoring).
