The NIST SP 800-53r5 PDF navigation pane is incomplete, so manual additions for CA-2, CA-7, IR-5, PM-25, PM-31, and PT-1 may need reapplying after regeneration; script updates may also require updating annotate_yaml_front_matter.py.

nodes.label: FFIEC IT Booklets Manager
nodes.rationale: Online HTML booklet versions are preferred over PDFs for deep linking, and stale 2004-era web copies must be checked against the archived-booklets page. dl_ffiec-itbooklets.py generates ffiec_{abbrev}_{section} keys (abbreviations from docs/_config.yml) consumed by the ffiec-itbooklets_references sections of risk files, filtering navigation from downloaded HTML before pandoc conversion.

nodes.label: Mitigation Page Template
nodes.rationale: Canonical structure for mitigation pages: frontmatter with sequence, mitigation layout, type (PREV, DET, or RESP), iso-42001_references, and a mitigates list of risk ids, followed by Purpose, Key Principles, Implementation Guidance, Challenges, Importance and Benefits, and Additional Resources sections.

nodes.label: ASQAV Pre-commit Compliance Scan Hook
nodes.rationale: Local pre-commit hook that runs npm run test as an AI agent governance compliance check on ts, js, json, and yaml files before every commit; always_run with pass_filenames false.

nodes.label: asqav-compliance Contributing Guide
nodes.rationale: New compliance rules are regex patterns appended to category arrays in src/scanner.ts; adding a whole category also requires extending the AnalysisResult interface, the analyzeFile check logic, calculateScore weighting, and report generation.

nodes.label: Governance Scan Categories
nodes.rationale: Five regex-driven governance categories: AUDIT_TRAIL_PATTERNS, POLICY_PATTERNS, REVOCATION_PATTERNS, HUMAN_OVERSIGHT_PATTERNS, and ERROR_HANDLING_PATTERN. Each category contributes 20 points to a 100-point compliance score.

nodes.label: Asqav Compliance Scanner
nodes.rationale: Positioned as 'Dependabot but for AI compliance': governance gaps in AI agent code are caught in CI on every pull request rather than in after-the-fact audits. Static pattern matching runs entirely inside the CI runner so code, prompts, and agent context never leave the repository.

nodes.label: Five Governance Check Categories
nodes.rationale: Audit trail, policy enforcement, revocation capability, human oversight, and error handling were chosen as statically scannable proxies for EU AI Act, DORA, and ISO 42001 obligations, evaluated per Python file that imports one of 12 AI agent frameworks.

nodes.label: Compliance Score (0-100)
nodes.rationale: Each of the 5 categories contributes up to 20 points, proportional to the percentage of agent files passing, which makes governance posture measurable and gateable via fail-on-gaps.

nodes.label: Hash-Only Mode
nodes.rationale: GDPR-aware data minimization: when the SDK auto-detects the Asqav cloud (*.asqav.com) it sends only a hash plus a small metadata bag (action_type, agent_id, session_id, model_name, tool_name); self-hosted deployments receive full context because the customer controls the server.

nodes.label: Asqav SDK
nodes.rationale: Companion runtime-governance SDK (audit trails, policy enforcement, signing); the division of labour is explicit: SDK for runtime governance, the compliance action for CI/CD checks.

nodes.label: Asqav Compliance Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Scopes vulnerability reports to scanner rule evaluation, findings-output injection into CI reports, paths where scanner input can alter host state, and false-negative patterns that let known-bad code pass; rule-tuning false positives are explicitly routed to regular issues.

nodes.label: AI Agent Governance Scanner Action
nodes.author: Asqav
nodes.rationale: GitHub Action metadata: node20 runtime executing dist/index.js; inputs github-token, scan-path, fail-on-gaps; outputs score, agent-files, gaps, report.

nodes.label: Asqav Compliance CI Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Lint (tsc --noEmit) and test jobs plus a ci-ok gate job that fails unless both succeed, giving a single required status check.

nodes.label: Public Sector AI Playbook
nodes.author: Linda Oraegbunam
nodes.rationale: The UK Government AI Playbook (Feb 2025) tells practitioners what to think about; this repository exists to supply the working artefacts (fill-in templates, checklists, decision frameworks) needed to act on it, grounded in UK and EU regulation. CC BY 4.0 licensed.

nodes.label: 8 Core Responsible AI Principles
nodes.rationale: Explicitly framed as a decision-making framework rather than a checklist: used to evaluate proposed AI projects, design governance from the outset, challenge vendor proposals, and communicate with citizens and oversight bodies. Grounded in the UK AI Playbook, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and the UK's five AI regulation principles. Public value first: deploy only for measurable citizen benefit, never for novelty or political pressure; proportionality favours the simplest (and least energy-intensive) AI that solves the problem.

nodes.label: Meaningful Human Oversight
nodes.rationale: Human in the loop means a human with time, information, and authority to intervene, not a rubber-stamp checkbox. Override rates should be documented because a human who never overrides the system is evidence the oversight may not be meaningful.

nodes.label: AI Readiness Assessment
nodes.rationale: 25 questions across 5 dimensions (strategic clarity, data readiness, technical capability, governance and legal, procurement) each worth 20 points; the 0-100 score maps to readiness bands where below 45 means do not proceed, making readiness a gate rather than advice.

nodes.label: Use Case Decision Framework
nodes.rationale: AI is not always the answer: a decision tree diverts ill-defined tasks to process redesign, data-poor problems to rule-based systems, and simple patterns to cheaper more auditable rules engines before AI is considered. Benefit and eligibility decisions are flagged as an EU AI Act high-risk category where full automation should be avoided in favour of decision support.

nodes.label: Four-Tier Risk Classification
nodes.rationale: An impact score out of 20 (affected population, decision reversibility, citizen vulnerability, consequence of error, automation level) maps to Tiers 1-4, and governance burden scales with citizen impact: Tier 2 adds DPIA/EIA/risk register/ATRS, Tier 3 adds SRO, bias audit and model card, Tier 4 adds independent audit, ministerial sign-off, and mandatory human override.

nodes.label: AI Contract Clause Library
nodes.rationale: Ready-to-adapt procurement clauses graded mandatory/recommended/optional by risk tier, covering model cards, decision explanation, ATRS support, override and emergency shutdown, data processing and residency, prohibition on training use, security standards and AI-specific testing, IP ownership of derived models, SLAs, drift monitoring, audit rights, and environmental reporting.

nodes.label: Human Override and Emergency Shutdown Clauses (C1-C3)
nodes.rationale: The supplier may never implement features that impede or discourage override; every override is logged with timestamp, operator, and reason; monthly override-rate reporting surfaces systematic model issues; and full suspension must be possible within 4-24 hours with an annually tested shutdown procedure.
nodes.norm_label: human override and emergency shutdown clauses (c1-c3)

nodes.label: Audit Rights Clause (G3)
nodes.rationale: The authority or its nominee can audit the AI system on 30 days notice, including training data, evaluation results, model cards, output testing, security controls, and personnel interviews, with the supplier bearing its own costs.

nodes.label: Model Drift Monitoring Clause (G2)
nodes.rationale: Contractualises drift detection: supplier must alert within 48 hours of threshold breach, root-cause within 10 business days, and remediate within 20.

nodes.label: AI Supplier Due Diligence Checklist
nodes.rationale: 40+ pass/fail items across 7 sections (company fundamentals, model and training data, data protection, transparency, security, contractual, human oversight) with sign-off by DPO, legal, and infosec. Any Fail in Data Protection or Security is a mandatory exclusion criterion unless adequately mitigated.

nodes.label: Healthcare AI Playbook
nodes.rationale: Healthcare AI errors are not just operational failures, they can cause direct patient harm or death, so governance sits at the intersection of MHRA, CQC, NHS England ADRS, ICO special-category data rules, and NICE evidence standards, with clinical safety (DCB0129 Clinical Safety Officer and safety case) layered on top of the generic tiers.

nodes.label: Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) Classification
nodes.rationale: AI intended to aid clinical decision-making or diagnose/treat disease likely qualifies as SaMD, triggering MHRA risk-class determination (Class I-III), conformity assessment, and UKCA marking before deployment; non-device AI may still need NICE EFS evaluation for NHS procurement.
nodes.norm_label: software as a medical device (samd) classification

nodes.label: NHS National Data Opt-Out
nodes.rationale: Any AI using NHS patient data must implement opt-out filtering before data reaches training pipelines and audit compliance annually, because health data is special category data requiring Article 9(2)(h) or DPA 2018 Schedule 1 legal bases.

nodes.label: NHS Radiology AI Triage Pattern
nodes.rationale: Case study pattern: AI triages chest X-rays to prioritise abnormal findings but cannot issue a report; a radiologist reviews all AI-flagged cases, an override rate above 10% triggers model review, false-negative rate must stay at or below the baseline radiologist rate, and the Class IIa SaMD carries UKCA marking and a DCB0129 safety case. Human authority is preserved by design.

nodes.label: Local Government AI Playbook
nodes.rationale: Councils combine budget constraints, ageing IT, diverse vulnerable populations, and accountability to elected members; obligations include PSED, FoIA, the Local Government Transparency Code, and ATRS. Use cases are split into high-value/lower-risk (document processing, RAG knowledge assistants) versus higher-risk entitlement decisions (benefits triage, housing allocation, fraud detection) that demand full governance.

nodes.label: AI Governance Board Structure
nodes.rationale: Decision authority scales with risk tier: Tier 1-2 to service directors, Tier 3 to the AI Governance Board (SRO, DPO, IT, legal, procurement, equality lead, elected member for scrutiny), Tier 4 to Cabinet or Full Council, and anything affecting children or vulnerable adults requires an additional safeguarding sign-off.

nodes.label: AI-Assisted Planning Application Triage Pattern
nodes.rationale: An NLP classifier categorises 4,000 planning applications per year into fast-track or full review, but explicitly never approves, refuses, or issues decisions; planning officers review every output, bias is tested by deprived-versus-affluent location, an override rate above 25% triggers model review, and the appeal rate must not increase.

nodes.label: AI Risk Register Template
nodes.rationale: Seven pre-populated risks (bias, hallucination, data breach, oversight loss, drift, vendor failure, trust) with likelihood x impact scoring, named risk owners, explicit review triggers, quarterly review for Tier 2-4, and an independent reviewer sign-off required before Tier 4 go-live.

nodes.label: RISK-001 Algorithmic Bias and Discriminatory Outcomes
nodes.rationale: Root causes named as biased training data, unrepresentative samples, proxy variables, and historical discrimination encoded in data; controls are EIA, pre-deployment bias testing, and disaggregated performance monitoring.
nodes.norm_label: risk-001 algorithmic bias and discriminatory outcomes

nodes.label: RISK-004 Loss of Meaningful Human Oversight
nodes.rationale: Automation bias: high AI accuracy creates over-trust and rubber-stamping. Notably the review trigger inverts the usual metric - an override rate dropping below about 5% is itself the warning sign that humans have stopped exercising independent judgment.
nodes.norm_label: risk-004 loss of meaningful human oversight

nodes.label: RISK-005 Model Drift and Performance Degradation
nodes.norm_label: risk-005 model drift and performance degradation

nodes.label: Pre-Deployment Bias Audit Template
nodes.rationale: Two anti-gaming rules are built in: fairness thresholds must be defined before running the audit, not after seeing results, and an unrepresentative test set halts the audit entirely. Includes intersectional analysis where sample sizes (>=30) allow, and must be repeated after any significant model update or population change.

nodes.label: Fairness Metrics Triplet (Demographic Parity, Equal Opportunity, Predictive Parity)
nodes.rationale: Three complementary group-fairness definitions each with a <=0.05 maximum difference threshold: positive prediction rate parity, true positive rate parity, and precision (calibration) parity across protected groups.
nodes.norm_label: fairness metrics triplet (demographic parity, equal opportunity, predictive parity)

nodes.label: Proxy Variable Analysis
nodes.rationale: Apparently neutral model variables (e.g. postcode) can proxy protected characteristics like ethnicity or deprivation, so correlation with protected characteristics must be assessed for each model input.

nodes.label: Model Card Template
nodes.rationale: Structured transparency for every deployed public-sector model: intended/out-of-scope/prohibited uses, training data provenance and limitations, per-subgroup performance disaggregation, fairness assessment, known failure modes, monitoring commitments, and named accountability contacts. Published alongside the ATRS entry and updated on retraining or at minimum annually.

nodes.label: Mitchell et al. (2019) Model Cards for Model Reporting
nodes.norm_label: mitchell et al. (2019) model cards for model reporting

nodes.label: Readiness Scorer CLI
nodes.rationale: Interactive CLI (rich + typer) that walks through the AI Readiness Assessment and emits a scored Markdown report plus JSON output.

nodes.label: Governance Report Generator
nodes.rationale: Takes a JSON project definition and generates a formatted Markdown governance pack; --example emits a reference config showing all fields.

nodes.label: Playbook Contribution Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Content standards enforce practitioner utility: plain English for non-technical public servants, every guidance grounded in a cited UK act/article/guidance document, devolved differences (England/Wales/Scotland/NI) marked, no personal data in case studies, and no legal advice.

nodes.label: Validate Playbook Workflow
nodes.rationale: CI validates the playbook as an artefact: py_compile and smoke-runs of both Python tools, existence checks for every expected template file, and grep checks that the README keeps its key sections.

nodes.label: Agentic Skill-Based System Architecture (Coding Agent with Skills, No Skill Sandboxing)
nodes.rationale: C4-style container diagram annotating every component of a skill-based coding agent with FINOS AI Governance Framework risk ids (RI-1 through RI-32); its central design observation is that skills run with no sandboxing, so risk concentrates in the supply chain and the single runtime consent gate.
nodes.norm_label: agentic skill-based system architecture (coding agent with skills, no skill sandboxing)

nodes.label: User Interface (CLI / IDE Extension)
nodes.rationale: Accepts user prompts, displays responses and artifacts, and requests tool-use approval. Annotated with risks RI-10, RI-18, RI-20.

nodes.label: Tests & Guardrails (Evaluation Suite)
nodes.rationale: Pre-deploy evals, prompt tests, and policy compliance checks (RI-5, RI-6, RI-14). Sits outside the runtime path: it validates before deployment rather than gating live actions.

nodes.label: Agent Orchestrator (Agentic Loop + Skill Context)
nodes.rationale: Plans, reasons, and selects tools; skill content is injected into the system prompt with no isolation boundary (RI-4, RI-10, RI-17, RI-24, RI-25, RI-27, RI-28, RI-32). The missing isolation boundary is the diagram's core architectural risk.

nodes.label: Shell Execution (Bash / System Shell)
nodes.rationale: Runs commands on the user's machine with the user's full permissions; no containerization or isolation. Executes agent-generated and skill-bundled scripts alike (RI-24, RI-29, RI-1) — the 'No Sandbox' half of the diagram title.

nodes.label: Project & System Files (Local File System)
nodes.rationale: Source code, configs, .env files, credentials, and build artifacts with full read/write access (RI-1, RI-19, RI-23, RI-29).

nodes.label: MCP Registry & Router (Connector Hub)
nodes.rationale: Discovers and routes to MCP servers and connectors (RI-26, RI-7).

nodes.label: Local MCP Servers (File System / DB / Git)
nodes.norm_label: local mcp servers (file system / db / git)

nodes.label: Remote MCP Servers (SaaS Integrations)
nodes.rationale: Access to external services: Slack, Jira, GitHub, etc. (RI-1, RI-7, RI-22, RI-26, RI-29).

nodes.label: Vendor API Endpoint (API Gateway)
nodes.rationale: Handles inference requests, meters usage, and applies safety filters (RI-1, RI-7, RI-8, RI-22).

nodes.label: Foundation Model (Large Language Model)
nodes.rationale: Generates reasoning, code, and tool calls. Skill-injected instructions are indistinguishable from the system prompt (RI-4, RI-5, RI-6, RI-8, RI-16, RI-17) — the model cannot tell skill text from operator text.

nodes.label: Permission & Approval Layer (User Consent Gate)
nodes.rationale: Prompts the user before bash, file writes, and MCP calls. It is the ONLY runtime guardrail for skill-initiated actions (RI-24, RI-25, RI-29, RI-31), which is why approval fatigue (RI-31) is called out as degrading the whole runtime defense.

nodes.label: Agent State & Memory (AGENTS.md / Session History)
nodes.rationale: Project instructions, conversation context, and learned preferences (RI-27, RI-1, RI-2, RI-32).

nodes.label: Skill Bundled Code (scripts/*.py, schemas, configs)
nodes.rationale: Helper scripts executed via bash, shipped alongside SKILL.md with no code review, signing, or execution isolation (RI-8, RI-9, RI-25, RI-26, RI-29, RI-30) — Layer 2 of the dual attack surface.

nodes.label: Skill Loader (File Reader / Slash Command)
nodes.rationale: Reads SKILL.md on invocation and injects prompt content into agent context with no integrity verification or sandboxing (RI-8, RI-9, RI-10, RI-26, RI-30, RI-32).

nodes.label: Skill Prompt Content (SKILL.md / REFERENCE.md)
nodes.rationale: Markdown instructions that steer agent reasoning, tool selection, and code generation patterns; untrusted text treated as system-level instructions (RI-8, RI-9, RI-10, RI-23, RI-26, RI-30, RI-32) — Layer 1 of the dual attack surface.

nodes.label: Dual Attack Surface (RI-30)
nodes.rationale: The diagram's key risk annotation: Layer 1 is prompt authority delegation (RI-32) — SKILL.md is injected into the system prompt with full instruction authority, indistinguishable from the agent's own; Layer 2 is code execution — bundled scripts run via bash unsandboxed. Approval fatigue (RI-31) degrades the only runtime guardrail.

nodes.label: RAG System Architecture (v0, no risks)
nodes.rationale: C4-style container diagram of a reference RAG system used by the FINOS AI Governance Framework as the baseline architecture onto which risk annotations are overlaid in companion diagrams. The 'no-risks' variant establishes the components and trust boundaries before risks are mapped.

nodes.label: RAG Knowledge Base Preparation - Data Processing Environment (Internal OnPrem/Cloud)
nodes.rationale: System boundary A: the offline knowledge-base preparation pipeline runs inside the organization (on-prem or org cloud), keeping raw private data processing internal and separate from the user-facing inference path.
nodes.norm_label: rag knowledge base preparation - data processing environment (internal onprem/cloud)

nodes.label: RAG Inference for Users - Instrumentation Environment (Internal OnPrem/Cloud)
nodes.rationale: System boundary B: the online, user-facing query orchestration layer is kept internal so that user interaction and pipeline orchestration can be instrumented and validated (via Tests) inside the organization.
nodes.norm_label: rag inference for users - instrumentation environment (internal onprem/cloud)

nodes.label: Inference Environment (SaaS)
nodes.rationale: The model-serving endpoints and model weights sit in a third-party SaaS boundary, outside the enterprise. The diagram draws this as a separate system boundary, making the org-to-vendor trust boundary (crossed only via HTTPS requests) the governance-relevant edge of the architecture.

nodes.label: Private Knowledge Data Source [Database]
nodes.rationale: Raw organizational data; the origin of all knowledge that eventually becomes retrievable context for the LLM.

nodes.label: Data Processor and Filtering [Service]
nodes.rationale: Processes and filters raw data before it enters the knowledge base; the point where data cleaning/redaction decisions are enforced.

nodes.label: Refined Knowledge Data Source [Database]
nodes.rationale: Cleaned and processed data staged between filtering and embedding generation.

nodes.label: Vector Data Loader [Service]
nodes.rationale: Converts refined data to embeddings by calling the external Embeddings Endpoint over HTTPS - the point where internal knowledge-base content crosses the SaaS boundary during preparation.

nodes.label: Vector Database [Vector Store]
nodes.rationale: Stores embeddings for retrieval; the shared store bridging the offline preparation pipeline and the online inference path (written by Vector Data Loader, searched by Query Processing).

nodes.label: User Query [Interface]
nodes.rationale: Query input interface; receives requests from the User and validated queries from the Tests suite, and returns responses.

nodes.label: Query Processing [Service]
nodes.rationale: Orchestrates the RAG pipeline: embeds the query via the Embeddings Endpoint, performs vector search against the Vector Database, and sends the inference request to the Inference Endpoint. The central hub of the online path.

nodes.label: Tests [Test Suite]
nodes.rationale: System validation: sends validated queries through the User Query interface and checks test responses, exercising the full RAG path end-to-end rather than components in isolation.

nodes.label: Embeddings Endpoint [API]
nodes.rationale: SaaS API that generates embeddings; serves both the offline Vector Data Loader and the online Query Processing service, backed by the Embeddings Model.

nodes.label: Inference Endpoint [API]
nodes.rationale: SaaS API that handles inference requests from Query Processing, backed by the LLM Model.

nodes.label: Embeddings Model [ML Model Store]
nodes.rationale: Text embedding model weights/data hosted in the SaaS environment behind the Embeddings Endpoint.

nodes.label: LLM Model [ML Model Store]
nodes.rationale: Large language model weights/data hosted in the SaaS environment behind the Inference Endpoint.

nodes.label: User (Person)
nodes.rationale: External person who performs queries against the RAG system; sits outside every system boundary in the diagram, sending requests to and receiving responses from the User Query interface.

nodes.label: RAG System Architecture (with FINOS Risk Annotations)
nodes.rationale: C4-style container diagram of a reference RAG deployment inside an enterprise boundary, split into three systems: an internal knowledge-base preparation environment, an internal inference/instrumentation environment, and a SaaS inference environment. Each container is annotated with the FINOS AIR risk identifiers (RI-x) that apply to it, mapping catalogue risks onto concrete architecture components.
nodes.norm_label: rag system architecture (with finos risk annotations)

nodes.label: Private Knowledge Data Source
nodes.rationale: Database of raw organizational data feeding the RAG pipeline. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-19, RI-23.

nodes.label: Data Processor and Filtering
nodes.rationale: Service that processes and filters raw data before refinement. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-9, RI-19, RI-23.

nodes.label: Refined Knowledge Data Source
nodes.rationale: Database of cleaned and processed data, intermediate between raw source and vectorization. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-2, RI-19.

nodes.label: Vector Data Loader
nodes.rationale: Service that converts refined data to embeddings by calling the SaaS Embeddings Endpoint over HTTPS, then stores them in the Vector Database. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-1, RI-2, RI-8.

nodes.label: Vector Database
nodes.rationale: Vector store holding embeddings for retrieval; queried at inference time via vector search. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-2, RI-16.

nodes.label: Query Processing
nodes.rationale: Service orchestrating the RAG pipeline: embeds the query via the Embeddings Endpoint, retrieves context via vector search, and sends the inference request to the Inference Endpoint. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-1, RI-2, RI-4, RI-16, RI-17.

nodes.label: Tests (System Validation Suite)
nodes.rationale: Test suite that sends validated queries into the User Query interface and checks test responses, providing system validation of the RAG loop. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-5, RI-6, RI-11, RI-14.

nodes.label: Embeddings Endpoint
nodes.rationale: SaaS API that generates embeddings, serving both the offline Vector Data Loader and the online Query Processing service. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-1, RI-7, RI-8, RI-22.

nodes.label: Inference Endpoint
nodes.rationale: SaaS API handling inference requests, backed by the LLM model store. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-1, RI-7, RI-8, RI-22.

nodes.label: Embeddings Model
nodes.rationale: ML model store holding text-embedding model weights/data behind the Embeddings Endpoint. Annotated with FINOS AIR risks RI-5, RI-6, RI-8, RI-11, RI-16.

nodes.label: LLM Model
nodes.rationale: ML model store holding the large language model weights/data behind the Inference Endpoint. Carries the largest risk annotation set in the diagram: RI-4, RI-5, RI-6, RI-8, RI-11, RI-16, RI-17.

nodes.label: FINOS AIR Risk Identifier Annotations (RI-1 to RI-23)
nodes.rationale: The diagram's central device: every container lists the FINOS AI-readiness risk identifiers that apply to it (e.g. raw data RI-19/RI-23; query interface RI-10/RI-18/RI-20; SaaS endpoints RI-1/RI-7/RI-8/RI-22; LLM model RI-4/RI-5/RI-6/RI-8/RI-11/RI-16/RI-17). This grounds the framework's abstract risk catalogue in a concrete RAG architecture, showing where in the system each risk materializes.
nodes.norm_label: finos air risk identifier annotations (ri-1 to ri-23)

nodes.label: Graph-Motif AI Monogram
nodes.rationale: The 'AI' letterforms in the logo icon are rendered as a node-and-edge graph: three circular nodes joined by strokes form a triangular 'A', and two stacked nodes joined by a bar form the 'I'. The design choice visually equates AI governance with a connected network/graph of controls and relationships, signalling structure and traceability rather than a black box.

nodes.label: AI Lettermark
nodes.rationale: The letters 'A' and 'I' are the sole subject of the mark, branding the framework as AI-specific at a glance; white letterforms on a saturated blue rounded square follow app-icon conventions so the framework reads as a product identity, not just a document.

nodes.label: Node-and-Edge Graph Motif
nodes.rationale: Both letterforms are constructed from circular vertices connected by thick straight strokes — the 'A' as a three-node triangle with a light periwinkle fill, the 'I' as a two-node vertical edge sharing the baseline node region with the A. Rendering the letters as a graph visually encodes networks/relationships, matching a governance framework whose substance is a mapped structure of risks, mitigations, and cross-walked standards.

nodes.label: AI Governance Framework Stacked Logo (2025)
nodes.rationale: Stacked (vertical) brand lockup: an icon above a two-line wordmark reading 'AI GOVERNANCE' in primary blue and 'FRAMEWORK' in a lighter periwinkle blue, giving the project a formal visual identity for its documentation.

nodes.label: AI Graph-Network Monogram Icon
nodes.rationale: Design decision: the letters 'A' and 'I' are drawn as a node-and-edge network (circles joined by white struts on a rounded blue square), visually encoding AI systems as connected graphs — an apt motif for a framework whose controls map relationships between risks, mitigations, and regulations.
