nodes.label: mental-health CI workflow
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap; hand-edits are lost on regeneration — change the contributing capability. Concurrency cancels superseded runs so two builds never write the same baseline.

nodes.label: changes job
nodes.rationale: Diffs the PR once and publishes one boolean per area so touching a page never starts a dbt review; fetch-depth 0 because the diff is against the merge base.

nodes.label: air-baseline job
nodes.rationale: Blocks only on controls the entity committed to; known gaps are reported, not hidden. submodules:true is load-bearing — without the vendored catalogue every control assesses unexercised and the gate passes for the wrong reason.

nodes.label: impact-gate job
nodes.rationale: Gates against the base graph, not the branch: added models have no blast radius there, deleted models' consumers are still found. An empty graph would pass because it found nothing.

nodes.label: recce job
nodes.rationale: autoMerge deliberately false — automation reports, a human merges. Baseline is pulled from the artefact store (in-repo baselines stopped scaling at 30 MB); missing secrets degrade to not-exercised rather than failing.

nodes.label: Infra is shared; business logic is not
nodes.rationale: The organising principle that appears in every layer of the platform.
nodes.norm_label: infra is shared; business logic is not

nodes.label: Ontology derives everything
nodes.rationale: A dlt source declares concept, roles and links once; staging, PII policy, monitors, metric candidates, graph edges and conformance are derived. Nothing semantic is written twice.

nodes.label: Retrieval, not grep
nodes.rationale: kg_search/kg_neighbors/kg_path plus a ~400-token context card let an agent route before it reads; the preamble stays ~1000 tokens regardless of group count.

nodes.label: Controls named, actions recorded
nodes.rationale: Governance enforced by artefacts that resolve and a hash-chained ledger the agent cannot edit — never by instructions an agent must remember.

nodes.label: platform/ engine layer (pf)
nodes.rationale: One pf package: one CLI, one MCP server, one Dagster workspace, 21 toolkits; optional tools as extras so a missing tool degrades to not-installed.

nodes.label: Groups and projects tenancy
nodes.rationale: Isolation is physical: one DuckDB file, one Dagster code location and writer pool per project. Roll-ups ATTACH sisters READ_ONLY — safe because the group ontology forced the same grain.

nodes.label: Vendor layer of pinned upstreams
nodes.rationale: Read-only submodules; every borrowing a recorded path pair; bumping a pin is a human decision, never an agent's.

nodes.label: The data path
nodes.rationale: dlt sources to dbt marts to MetricFlow; five projections (Evidence BI, WrenAI MDL, OpenMetadata, OpenTopology, knowledge graph) are generated views of one declaration — hand-editing any is denied or pointless.

nodes.label: Quack dev serving on ADBC/Arrow
nodes.rationale: Read-only wire enforced twice (engine read_only plus client-side real-parser refusal); writers take a write window; localhost-only 0600 token; custody recorded as provenance.

nodes.label: Five-stage provenance ledger
nodes.rationale: Intent, decision, execution, SHA-256 chain, RFC 3161 + OpenTimestamps anchor. provenance/** denied to every agent; pf provenance verify blocks CI.

nodes.label: The path gate
nodes.rationale: gate.yaml plus generated gate.capabilities.yaml, enforced by PreToolUse hook, pre-commit hook and pf gate.

nodes.label: Named controls (policy.yaml + pf air)
nodes.rationale: Coverage is derived, never stored; a control whose enforced_by resolves to nothing reports as failing — which is the point.

nodes.label: Impact analysis as merge gate
nodes.rationale: The graph names downstream models, metrics and owners before a change lands; recce supplies the empirical half; enforced at pf check, pre-commit and PreToolUse.

nodes.label: The session layer
nodes.rationale: pf work scopes a session to one project; power-tools ships the pf MCP server, verification subagents and hooks.

nodes.label: Extension seams
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap STEPS, the Tool framework, capability-declared CI jobs, toolkits and vendoring — the platform grows here and deliberately nowhere else.

nodes.label: Ontology segregation test suite
nodes.rationale: Proves the three ontology layers stay separate by leak direction (upward, sideways, downward, selection, project). Groups discovered by glob, so a new group is covered automatically.

nodes.label: Three-layer ontology contract
nodes.rationale: Platform defines universal vocabulary and all policy; a group extension adds its own terms; an instance selects, never defines; a project binds columns. policies: in an extension is ignored — governance does not federate.

nodes.label: Vendored upstreams index
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf vendor card: coupling kind and state per upstream, plus the schema contracts that can fail a build.

nodes.label: Vendor registry and lock
nodes.rationale: 22 upstreams, 83 adoptions, 47 declines as verifiable path pairs. vendor.lock.json records the human-reviewed commit versus the gitlink's checkout — the gap is what makes drift observable. Weekly automation opens PRs but never approves.

nodes.label: Executable vendor contracts
nodes.rationale: Generated output is validated against the vendored schema file, not against memory — an upstream field change breaks the build at the pin bump instead of in a consumer.

nodes.label: FINOS AI Governance Framework pin
nodes.rationale: The missing referent: 23 risks and 23 controls with stable ids, cross-walked to EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST, OWASP. Agentic risks 24-29 are this platform's actual threat surface. Pinned as a catalogue, not the catalogue — a CatalogueSource entry point; nothing in pf.air names FINOS.

nodes.label: ASQAV compliance scanner pin
nodes.rationale: A static second opinion with a different failure mode: sees controls that exist but never ran. Its score never gates the merge — regex over source mistakes a comment for revocation.

nodes.label: Public Sector AI Playbook pin
nodes.rationale: The artefacts a regulator is handed (model card, risk register). Carried, not copied — templates belong to a deployment, and CC BY attribution travels with the derived artefact.

nodes.label: duckdb-quack pin
nodes.rationale: Reference source for the wire behaviour pf quack serve is built around; the experimental client ATTACH cannot carry schema DDL, so reads route through quack_query and writers use the file in a write window.

nodes.label: Evidence BI pin
nodes.rationale: BI as a projection of the semantic layer, not a second place metrics live; a hand-written query in a page is a second definition and the audit flags it. No upstream LICENSE — reference only.

nodes.label: gate.yaml safety policy
nodes.rationale: Hand-maintained half; capability-contributed rules live in generated gate.capabilities.yaml merged at load so comments survive. maxFiles 12 per loop run; blocks at severity breaking.

nodes.label: Agent write denylist
nodes.rationale: Secrets, the warehouse, generated artefacts, provenance/** (an agent that can edit the record of what it did has no record) and the quack state file (rewriting it could repoint readers or lift the token).

nodes.label: Denylist exceptions
nodes.rationale: mdl.json and the catalogue projection are carried so contracts diff in review; generated workflows must be committed or the merge gate exists on disk and nowhere else; recce artefacts moved to the artefact store when they hit 30 MB per project.

nodes.label: Platform denylist for project sessions
nodes.rationale: Platform infra is shared — a change made while working on one company silently affects every other.

nodes.label: Impact-required paths
nodes.rationale: Models, macros, model YAML and dlt sources require the blast radius to be reported before change.

nodes.label: Hospital group skills convention
nodes.rationale: Only domain knowledge lives here (reconciliation procedures, regulatory workflows, naming rules the ontology cannot express); infra skills come from platform/toolkits and are never duplicated.

nodes.label: Hospital group context
nodes.rationale: Sisters share the ontology instance, conformed dimensions and group metrics but have separate warehouses and run in parallel.

nodes.label: Conformed diagnosis bridge rule
nodes.rationale: ICD-10 groups per CSO Ireland HRA71 are the group-wide bridge between clinical facts and population benchmarks; a future sister (e.g. an HMS entity) must map into the same groups, not invent parallel ones.

nodes.label: Special-category data rule
nodes.rationale: Mental-health data is special-category under GDPR / EU AI Act even when synthetic; anything predictive on episode outcomes is high-risk — declare AIR controls before building it.

nodes.label: Rollup-only cross-entity rule
nodes.rationale: Only the rollup project may read sister data, and only via ATTACH READ_ONLY; never read a sister project's files from another project.

nodes.label: Hospital AIR baseline commitments
nodes.rationale: Baseline starts empty on purpose — a scaffolder that pre-commits a family produces commitments nobody made. Filled from --suggest, a ratchet against regression; dropping a control requires accepted: with reason and owner. Declared here means declared for every sister; a project may add but not remove.

nodes.label: Hospital group eval tier
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests. A case belongs at group tier when it would be wrong for a sister to disagree with it; three tiers (platform, group, project) each own what only it can know.

nodes.label: Hospital group index card
nodes.rationale: Generated index: one sister (mental-health); ontology classes in scope Party, Agreement, Event, Interaction.

nodes.label: Hospital ontology extension
nodes.rationale: Layers over the platform ontology, never replaces it — another company never inherits a word that means nothing to them. The class split mirrors Karolinska Institutet GPH constructs per mental-health ADR-0001.

nodes.label: Patient class
nodes.rationale: A person receiving care; distinct from survey respondents, who are anonymous and never joined to Patient data. Identity patient_id.

nodes.label: Diagnosis class
nodes.rationale: The conformed diagnosis dimension: maps each source vocabulary onto the ICD-10 diagnostic groups of the national in-patient registry (CSO Ireland HRA71). The only sanctioned bridge between patient-level facts and population-level benchmarks.

nodes.label: TreatmentEpisode class
nodes.rationale: One course of outpatient treatment — a commitment with start, duration and outcome. Score columns are an episode-grain snapshot, not a longitudinal series.

nodes.label: ScreeningAssessment class
nodes.rationale: One behavioural screening against an expert diagnosis (bipolar I/II, depression, normal); the cohort is unrelated to TreatmentEpisode patients.

nodes.label: EcgRecording class
nodes.rationale: Summary features of one 12-lead ECG segment from a psychiatric cohort. Raw signals stay out of the warehouse; extraction reproducible via scripts/extract_ecg_features.py.

nodes.label: SurveyResponse class
nodes.rationale: One response to a population survey; respondents are anonymous members of the public, never Patients. Upstream carries exact duplicates (292,364 rows, ~290k distinct) — raw lands as-is and the content-hash surrogate key drives the dedupe in staging.

nodes.label: PopulationStatistic class
nodes.rationale: One cell of a published national statistic (CSO Ireland HRA71, 2001-2023). NULL is a suppressed or not-applicable cell — never zero. Benchmark grain only; joined to patient facts only through Diagnosis.icd10_group at year grain.

nodes.label: Karolinska GPH research anchors
nodes.rationale: EPiCSS (psychiatric epidemiology) anchors SurveyResponse and PopulationStatistic; PRIME Health anchors TreatmentEpisode outcomes; GH-Pharma anchors the medication/therapy attributes.

nodes.label: Hospital ontology instance
nodes.rationale: Selects the platform classes this group models (Party, Agreement, Event, Interaction); validated against platform concepts.yaml by pf check. The instance layer selects, never defines.

nodes.label: Session memory promotion convention
nodes.rationale: One lesson per file, written mid-task by agents. Promotion to group CLAUDE.md or a platform RULES.md is a reviewed human step — what makes the platform compound instead of accumulating notes nobody reads.

nodes.label: mental-health project context
nodes.rationale: Domain facts an agent cannot derive from the models; design rationale and research anchors live in decisions/ADR-0001.

nodes.label: Registry NULL suppression rule
nodes.rationale: Registry NULLs are suppressed/not-applicable cells — never zero-fill, never coalesce. A published 0 is a real zero; NULL is absence of publication.

nodes.label: Survey respondents are not patients
nodes.rationale: Survey respondents are anonymous members of the public, not Patients — never join survey data to patient-grain facts.

nodes.label: Benchmark-only join rule
nodes.rationale: Patient-level and population-level data meet only in fct_diagnosis_benchmark, only as shares at conformed ICD-10 group grain.

nodes.label: No-time-axis cohorts rule
nodes.rationale: Screening and ECG cohorts have no event time upstream — they carry no time axis and stay out of the semantic layer by design.

nodes.label: diagnosis_map.csv bridge rule
nodes.rationale: transform/seeds/diagnosis_map.csv is the diagnosis vocabulary bridge; changing a mapping changes the benchmark — run pf impact first. Anchored in decisions/ADR-0001.

nodes.label: Project semantic stack
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary is platform-wide and loaded in the project graph before any data exists. A foreign key must be declared with links= and the topology must already relate the classes — that binding makes join conditions derivable rather than guessed; pf check fails on an undeclared join.

nodes.label: AIR Control Declaration
nodes.rationale: Hand-written half of AI governance; governance/air-register.md is the generated half. Merged over the group's air.yaml.

nodes.label: AIR Baseline Controls
nodes.rationale: Union with the group's baseline — an entity may commit to more than its family, never less. pf air baseline --suggest proposes only what already passes: a ratchet against regression, and accepting stays a person's act. Failing baseline controls block the merge.

nodes.label: AIR Accepted Risks
nodes.rationale: reason and owner both required: an acceptance without a reason is a gap with better formatting, one without an owner is a decision nobody can be asked about.

nodes.label: Candidate Admission Criteria
nodes.rationale: Governed backlog, never a bulk import: license permits use, grain documented as one of three natures (ADR-0001), maps onto dim_diagnosis or adds a genuinely new axis, and pf semantic scan induces a steward-approved proposal.

nodes.label: Psych_data Conversations Corpus
nodes.rationale: Not landed — conversational NLP shape, not relational. Revisit as evaluation corpus or document-grain resource; never a clinical fact. Apache-2.0.

nodes.label: Multilingual MH NLP Dataset Survey
nodes.rationale: Catalog, not a dataset — mine it for candidates adding a language axis; each entry admits individually.

nodes.label: ODSC Mental-health Dataset Listicle
nodes.rationale: Catalog, not a dataset — verify each entry's original source and license, never the blog's re-host.

nodes.label: Kaggle Mental Health Tag Feed
nodes.rationale: Discovery channel — checked via uvx kaggle datasets list --tags 4171 when looking for new axes.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata dbt Ingestion Workflow
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf bootstrap from tools.yaml, pf.runtime.targets and dbt artefacts (manifest/catalog/run_results under transform/target). Credentials are env-var references — no secret in the file.

nodes.label: Ontology Annotations Contract
nodes.rationale: Column-to-role contract for every kaggle_mh resource; roles drive generated staging, tests and review config downstream.

nodes.label: ecg_recordings Resource
nodes.rationale: Grain: one 12-lead ECG segment. Raw signals stay out of the warehouse — extraction reproduced by scripts/extract_ecg_features.py.

nodes.label: registry_annual Resource
nodes.rationale: Grain: one statistic x year x sex x ICD-10 group. A NULL value is a suppressed or not-applicable cell — never zero-fill.

nodes.label: screening_assessments Resource
nodes.rationale: Grain: one behavioural screening of one person. Cohort unrelated to treatment_episodes patients.

nodes.label: survey_responses Resource
nodes.rationale: Grain: one survey response as published upstream. Landed as-is with exact duplicates; deduplicated by the content-hash surrogate key in staging. Respondents are anonymous — never Patients.

nodes.label: treatment_episodes Resource
nodes.rationale: Grain: one treatment episode per patient. Episode-grain snapshot — scores are point-in-time, not a longitudinal series.

nodes.label: Upstream Data Manifest
nodes.rationale: Point-in-time snapshots carried in-repo so the project builds offline. Refreshing one means re-fetching, updating the sha256, and treating the diff as a data change — pf impact before merging.

nodes.label: mental_health_diagnosis_treatment.csv
nodes.rationale: Synthetic patient-level treatment monitoring, 500 episodes, no PHI.

nodes.label: psychiatric_in_patients_annual.csv
nodes.rationale: CC BY 4.0 (Irish PSI) — cite CSO Ireland, not only Kaggle. Empty VALUE cells are suppressed/not-applicable — never zero.

nodes.label: mental_health_survey.csv.gz
nodes.rationale: Population survey, 2014 OSMI-style lineage; 292,364 rows, ~290k distinct — exact duplicates removed by the staging dedupe. Gzipped 29.7 MB to 1.8 MB for in-repo carry.

nodes.label: dataset_mental_disorders.csv
nodes.rationale: 120 behavioural screenings vs expert diagnosis (Bipolar Type-1/2, Depression, Normal).

nodes.label: ecg_features.csv
nodes.rationale: Derived summary features of 2,670 12-lead ECG segments (bipolar/depression/schizophrenia). Raw .mat signals NOT carried — rebuild via scripts/extract_ecg_features.py.

nodes.label: extract_ecg_features.py
nodes.rationale: Reproduces ECG summary features from raw signals so the warehouse never has to carry them.

nodes.label: CSO Ireland PxStat HRA71
nodes.rationale: Original source of the in-patient registry: psychiatric in-patients by year, sex, ICD-10 diagnostic group, 2001-2023.

nodes.label: ADR-0001 Mental-health Ontology Extension
nodes.rationale: Accepted 2026-09-01. Adds seven classes and four relations, all bridging through the conformed Diagnosis dimension. Catalogs are backlogs with admission criteria, never bulk-onboarded.

nodes.label: Grain Law
nodes.rationale: Patient-level facts and population-level data meet only in fct_diagnosis_benchmark, only as shares, only at conformed ICD-10 group grain. Any patient-level join to benchmark or survey data is a bug.

nodes.label: Clinical Patient-grain Nature
nodes.rationale: Each row is one person's record: TreatmentEpisode, ScreeningAssessment, EcgRecording.

nodes.label: Population Benchmark Nature
nodes.rationale: Pre-aggregated registry data; a NULL value is a suppressed or not-applicable cell, never zero.

nodes.label: Population Context Nature
nodes.rationale: Survey respondents are anonymous members of the public, not Patients.

nodes.label: Diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Conformed dimension every relation bridges through — the only sanctioned bridge between clinical facts and population benchmarks.

nodes.label: TreatmentEpisode
nodes.rationale: Models an intervention with an outcome — therapy type, medication, adherence, outcome — the unit intervention research reasons about.

nodes.label: SurveyResponse
nodes.rationale: Social determinants (occupation, family history, days indoors, coping) as a class disjoint from Patient.

nodes.label: PopulationStatistic
nodes.rationale: Registry-based epidemiology kept at published grain.

nodes.label: Karolinska Institutet GPH Research Groups
nodes.rationale: The class split follows the constructs used by these research groups.

nodes.label: EPiCSS
nodes.rationale: Epidemiology of Psychiatric Conditions, Substance use and Social Environment (Gardner/Agardh): separating psychiatric case data from social-environment context motivates SurveyResponse disjoint from Patient and PopulationStatistic at published grain.

nodes.label: PRIME Health
nodes.rationale: Prevention, Intervention and Mechanisms in Public Health (Magnusson): the intervention-with-outcome unit behind TreatmentEpisode.

nodes.label: GH-Pharma
nodes.rationale: Global Health Pharmacology and Therapeutics (Aklillu): medication and therapy_type first-class so therapeutic comparisons stay expressible without remodelling.

nodes.label: EPHIR
nodes.rationale: Epidemiology and Public Health Intervention Research (Moller): case-mix-share design, never absolute counts across unlike denominators.

nodes.label: fct_diagnosis_benchmark
nodes.rationale: The only mart where clinical and population data meet, as shares at conformed ICD-10 group grain.

nodes.label: diagnosis_map.csv Seed
nodes.rationale: transform/seeds/diagnosis_map.csv — the conformed diagnosis vocabulary bridge; changing a mapping changes the benchmark.

nodes.label: conformed_icd10_group Folding
nodes.rationale: Folds the registry's legacy pre-ICD-10 classification labels into modern groups so 2001-2023 trends hold.

nodes.label: Content-hash Survey Dedupe
nodes.rationale: The surrogate_key role drives the generated staging dedupe: 292,364 rows to 290,051 distinct; raw keeps full multiplicity. Two key roles deliberate — response_id preserves upstream ordinality, content_hash defines identity.

nodes.label: Decision Log Convention
nodes.rationale: One ADR per durable decision explaining why. Never delete one; supersede it. The knowledge graph indexes these so kg_search finds them.

nodes.label: Generated AIR Register
nodes.rationale: governance/air-register.md derives from air.yaml plus a fresh coverage run and sits on the gate denylist — hand-editing would make it disagree with the declaration. Credit lines are collected from catalogues actually loaded, so a swapped catalogue takes its obligation with it.

nodes.label: DuckLake Production Target
nodes.rationale: Dev stays on local DuckDB because a developer who needs a warehouse account stops running the project; only prod points at DuckLake and nothing can move dev/ci/base, by construction. No shortcut: the target is named on every invocation because believing-you-are-on-dev-while-on-prod is worse than the typing. DATA_PATH is fixed at lake creation; file catalogs serialize DDL so threads defaults to 1. Credentials are env_var calls, never values.

nodes.label: sf_* Dialect Dispatch Macros
nodes.rationale: platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake macros dispatch per adapter so a model is written once and compiles to whatever the target understands.

nodes.label: pf align Dialect Gate
nodes.rationale: Says whether the project is actually portable or merely untested. Declaring the target does not make models run on DuckLake — this gate passing is what does. Same engine as dev, so it passes by construction: zero portability distance.

nodes.label: Elementary Build Recording
nodes.rationale: Every dbt build records run results, all test results, timings and schema snapshots into main_elementary — observability as queryable tables with history, not a log that scrolled away. The edr CLI installs isolated because it cannot share a lockfile with recce; recording itself rides inside dbt.

nodes.label: Elementary Anomaly Tests
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not generated: an anomaly threshold is a judgement about one table's behaviour, so it is declared in that model's own yml where the judgement lives.

nodes.label: dbt-expectations Package
nodes.rationale: Great Expectations vocabulary as native dbt tests, installed project-wide, usable in any model's yml.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Catalogue Publishing
nodes.rationale: The catalogue is where someone who does not read YAML finds what a table means. It points at production, never a dev DuckDB file — the connection comes from pf.runtime.targets so the deploy warehouse and the catalogued one cannot disagree. The ontology is canonical and stays in git.

nodes.label: Ingestion Order Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Database pass first — every other row describes tables. dbt ingestion alone against an empty service has nothing to attach to, which is exactly what this project did before catalog/ingestion/ existed: a vocabulary published over zero tables.

nodes.label: Owner-edits Proposal Channel
nodes.rationale: UI edits are overwritten on the next publish, on purpose — but that would silence the people who know the most, so pull diffs catalogue edits against contracts/annotations.yaml into catalog/owner-edits.yaml. Nothing is applied automatically; a line moves across by hand in a pull request so a meaning change gets normal review.

nodes.label: OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: A credential set where ingestion runs; never written into a generated file.

nodes.label: Quack Dev Serving
nodes.rationale: Every reader — MCP tools, previews, sister roll-ups, any DuckDB client — reaches data/mental_health.duckdb over DuckDB's quack protocol instead of opening the file. Runtime is pf.runtime.quack; the protocol is pinned at vendor/duckdb-quack.

nodes.label: Write Window
nodes.rationale: Writers never queue behind readers: dbt, dlt, MetricFlow, Elementary and Recce borrow the file for exactly the duration of a run and the server resumes behind them; the borrowing is automatic.

nodes.label: Quack Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Enforced, not advisory (policy.yaml dev serving section): the wire is read-only at both engine and client; localhost is not a parameter so a routable dev server cannot be configured into existence; the token lives in a 0600 gitignored state file denied to agent edits and redacted from output; serving, stopping and every borrow are recorded in the provenance ledger audited by pf provenance verify.

nodes.label: Recce Diff Review
nodes.rationale: pf impact says what could break; Recce says what did change — baseline a green build, change, rebuild, diff. recce_state.json and target-base/ are gate-denied because hand-editing a recorded diff makes the review lie.

nodes.label: Generated recce.yml
nodes.rationale: Derived from contracts/annotations.yaml — a natural_key role becomes a value-diff primary key, a money_amount a profile diff. Edit the roles, not the config; pf bootstrap regenerates it.

nodes.label: Wren MCP Serving
nodes.rationale: There is no Wren web UI: the Docker chat-first BI app is legacy/v1. Current WrenAI is a CLI plus wren serve, which serves MCP. The semantic surface is pf ui Semantics reading the same manifest — nothing is iframed because there is nothing to iframe.

nodes.label: Project-owned Eval Cases
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code; these are their tests — cases encoding this entity's business rules no toolkit could guess, for agents test_failure_triage, freshness_triage, metric_gap_proposer. The why field is mandatory or the corpus decays into assertions nobody dares change. Nothing is shared with sisters. Any prompt change must keep these green.

nodes.label: Weak Prose Matchers
nodes.rationale: Use contains_any, not exact strings: a case that pins wording fails on a harmless rewrite, and a suite that cries wolf gets switched off — which costs more than the case was worth. --samples N exposes unstable prompts: passing 4 of 5 is neither passing nor failing.

nodes.label: Pages Never Restate Business Logic
nodes.rationale: Every number traces to a metric compiled into queries/metrics/. A missing figure means a metric definition in transform/models/semantic/ then pf report build — not SQL in a page. Two pages filtering differently is how one company ends up with two revenues.

nodes.label: Ratio Re-division Rule
nodes.rationale: Ratio queries carry numerator and denominator so a page re-divides at its own grain: sum(num)/sum(den). Never avg(ratio) — wrong at every grain except the one it was computed at, the most common BI bug there is.

nodes.label: Node 20 Build Boundary
nodes.rationale: Evidence 40 does not build on Node 24 / npm 11 — verified by building a pristine evidence-dev/template that fails the same way, so it is Evidence's supported-runtime boundary, not this project. sources and dev work on newer Node; build needs 20 (.nvmrc committed).

nodes.label: Evidence Config
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build. The components plugin section is load-bearing: without it Evidence's injectComponents() discovers zero component plugins, silently injects no imports, and every generated page dies in the build with 'QueryViewer' is not defined — because the preprocessor wraps each sql fence in one. Datasource is @evidence-dev/duckdb.

nodes.label: CVD-validated Palette
nodes.rationale: Palette values validated: adjacent-pair CVD deltaE >= 8, normal-vision >= 15, contrast checked on both light and dark surfaces. Re-picking them by eye makes charts unreadable for ~8% of readers.

nodes.label: mental-health — Overview
nodes.rationale: Every number on the page is a governed metric compiled from the dbt semantic layer into queries/metrics/; a missing figure is fixed by adding a metric definition, never SQL in the page. Generated by pf report build — the page is a projection of the semantic-layer definitions. DateRange reads min()/max() from one column, so date bounds arrive as two rows in one column.

nodes.label: Adherence Rate
nodes.rationale: Mean adherence to treatment in percent across episodes, unfiltered, measured over treatment_started_at from fct_treatment_episodes. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer; the page does not restate the definition.

nodes.label: Avg Symptom Severity
nodes.rationale: Mean symptom severity (1-10) across episodes, unfiltered, measured over treatment_started_at from fct_treatment_episodes. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer; the page does not restate the definition.

nodes.label: Avg Treatment Duration (weeks)
nodes.rationale: Mean episode duration in weeks, unfiltered, measured over treatment_started_at from fct_treatment_episodes. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer; the page does not restate the definition.

nodes.label: Improved Episodes
nodes.rationale: Episodes whose recorded outcome is 'improved', unfiltered, measured over treatment_started_at from fct_treatment_episodes. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer; the page does not restate the definition.

nodes.label: Improved Outcome Rate
nodes.rationale: Share of episodes whose recorded outcome is 'improved', carried as improved_episodes / treatment_episodes so it re-divides correctly at any grain; measured over treatment_started_at from fct_treatment_episodes.

nodes.label: Registry In-patients
nodes.rationale: National psychiatric in-patient count restricted to unit = 'number', sex = 'both sexes', conformed_icd10_group <> 'all disorders'; suppressed cells excluded by NULL semantics; measured over year_date from fct_registry_annual.

nodes.label: Survey Responses
nodes.rationale: Distinct population survey responses with upstream duplication removed, unfiltered, measured over surveyed_at from fct_survey_responses. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer; the page does not restate the definition.

nodes.label: Treatment Episodes
nodes.rationale: Count of treatment episodes — the single definition, unfiltered, measured over treatment_started_at from fct_treatment_episodes. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer; the page does not restate the definition.

nodes.label: Treatment Seekers
nodes.rationale: Distinct survey respondents who sought treatment, unfiltered, measured over surveyed_at from fct_survey_responses. Defined once in the dbt semantic layer; the page does not restate the definition.

nodes.label: Treatment-Seeking Rate
nodes.rationale: Share of distinct survey respondents who sought treatment — population context, never a clinical outcome; carried as treatment_seekers / survey_responses so it re-divides correctly at any grain; measured over surveyed_at from fct_survey_responses.

nodes.label: Ratio Metric Re-aggregation
nodes.rationale: A ratio metric is carried as its numerator and denominator columns and aggregated as sum(numerator) / sum(denominator) at whatever grain you group by. Averaging the ratio itself gives a different — and wrong — answer.

nodes.label: mental_health DuckDB Connection
nodes.rationale: DuckDB connector pointing at ../../../data/mental_health.duckdb. One warehouse file per project is what lets sister companies run in parallel; the reporting layer only ever reads.

nodes.label: mental-health Tools Config
nodes.rationale: Per-project tool config merged over groups/hospital/tools.yaml. enabled: false opts out of something the group turned on; config dicts deep-merge, so overriding one key keeps the rest. Currently empty — everything is inherited from the group.

nodes.label: mental_health dbt Project
nodes.rationale: dbt project 'mental_health', profile 'mental_health'. Staging models materialize as views in schema staging; marts as tables in schema marts. Macro paths pull in platform/dbt/macros and platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake/macros alongside local macros.

nodes.label: Root-project Macro Loading
nodes.rationale: Platform cleaning macros load as root-project macros, not as a package: pf_clean dispatches to its clean_* siblings unqualified, and dbt namespaces package macros, so a package install fails on the inner dispatch.

nodes.label: Cross-database Function Layer
nodes.rationale: dbt-snowflake macros are the cross-database function layer: sf_iff(...) and its siblings compile to whatever the target adapter understands, so one model runs on DuckDB in development and Snowflake in production. pf dialect lists coverage; adding a sibling toolkit (dbt-bigquery) means adding its macros directory.

nodes.label: Elementary Observability Models
nodes.rationale: Run results, test history and schema snapshots written by the package's on-run-end hooks on every dbt build. The dedicated elementary schema keeps them out of the marts. Managed by pf tool elementary.

nodes.label: dim_diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Conformed diagnosis dimension — source vocabularies mapped to the registry's ICD-10 diagnostic groups. The only sanctioned bridge between patient-level facts and population benchmarks. Grain: one diagnosis code; icd10_group is NULL for the 'normal' control label.

nodes.label: dim_patients
nodes.rationale: Patients derived from treatment episodes. Grain: one patient.

nodes.label: fct_treatment_episodes
nodes.rationale: Treatment episode fact enriched with the conformed diagnosis. Grain: one treatment episode; outcome constrained to improved / deteriorated / no change.

nodes.label: fct_screening_assessments
nodes.rationale: Behavioural screening vs expert diagnosis. Static cohort — no time axis, not projected into the semantic layer. Grain: one screening assessment.

nodes.label: fct_ecg_recordings
nodes.rationale: ECG segment features by disorder cohort. Static cohort — no time axis, not projected into the semantic layer. Grain: one ECG recording.

nodes.label: fct_registry_annual
nodes.rationale: National psychiatric in-patient statistics at published grain (one statistic x year x sex x ICD-10 group). NULL value means suppressed/not-applicable — never zero, no coalesce. conformed_icd10_group folds legacy classification labels into modern groups.

nodes.label: fct_survey_responses
nodes.rationale: Population survey at distinct-response grain — the content-hash surrogate key drives the role-generated dedupe in staging; the raw table keeps the upstream multiplicity for audit. Respondents are anonymous — never joined to patient-grain data.

nodes.label: fct_diagnosis_benchmark
nodes.rationale: Case-mix comparison — this entity's episode mix vs the national in-patient mix, as shares at conformed ICD-10 group grain. The only mart where clinical and population data meet.

nodes.label: Registry NULL Suppression Semantics
nodes.rationale: A registry NULL is a suppressed or not-applicable cell, never zero: the mart applies no coalesce, the semantic layer's sum ignores NULLs by design, and the metric excludes suppressed cells by NULL semantics. A published 0 is a real zero; NULL is absence of publication.

nodes.label: Treatment Episodes
nodes.rationale: Count of treatment episodes. The single definition. Simple metric over measure episode_count.

nodes.label: Adherence Rate
nodes.rationale: Mean adherence to treatment, in percent, across episodes. Simple metric over measure avg_adherence_pct.

nodes.label: Improved Episodes
nodes.rationale: Episodes whose recorded outcome is 'improved'. Simple metric over measure improved_count.

nodes.label: Improved Outcome Rate
nodes.rationale: Share of episodes whose recorded outcome is 'improved'. Ratio metric: numerator improved_episodes, denominator treatment_episodes.

nodes.label: Avg Symptom Severity
nodes.rationale: Mean symptom severity (1-10) across episodes. Simple metric over measure avg_symptom_severity.

nodes.label: Avg Treatment Duration (weeks)
nodes.rationale: Mean episode duration in weeks. Simple metric over measure avg_treatment_duration_weeks.

nodes.label: Survey Responses
nodes.rationale: Distinct population survey responses (upstream duplication removed). Simple metric over measure response_count.

nodes.label: Treatment Seekers
nodes.rationale: Distinct survey respondents who sought treatment. Simple metric over measure treatment_seeking_count.

nodes.label: Treatment-Seeking Rate
nodes.rationale: Share of distinct survey respondents who sought treatment. Population context — never a clinical outcome. Ratio metric: numerator treatment_seekers, denominator survey_responses.

nodes.label: Registry In-patients
nodes.rationale: National psychiatric in-patient count — both sexes, count unit only, suppressed cells excluded by NULL semantics. Simple metric over measure inpatient_value, filtered to statistic__unit = 'number', statistic__sex = 'both sexes', statistic__conformed_icd10_group <> 'all disorders' so the all-disorders rollup is excluded.

nodes.label: episodes Semantic Model
nodes.rationale: Treatment episodes semantic model over ref('fct_treatment_episodes'); agg_time_dimension treatment_started_at derives from the event_time role. Entities episode (primary), patient and diagnosis (foreign). Measures: episode_count, improved_count, avg_adherence_pct, avg_symptom_severity, avg_treatment_duration_weeks.

nodes.label: survey Semantic Model
nodes.rationale: Distinct population survey responses over ref('fct_survey_responses'); agg_time_dimension surveyed_at. Context, never clinical truth. Measures: response_count, treatment_seeking_count.

nodes.label: registry Semantic Model
nodes.rationale: National in-patient statistics over ref('fct_registry_annual'); agg_time_dimension year_date at year granularity. NULL values are suppressed cells; sum ignores them by design. Measure: inpatient_value.

nodes.label: stg_kaggle_mh__ecg_recordings
nodes.rationale: Concept EcgRecording; grain: one 12-lead ECG segment. Raw signals stay out of the warehouse; features reproduced by scripts/extract_ecg_features.py. Kaggle buraktaci, 2670 recordings: bipolar, depression, schizophrenia.

nodes.label: stg_kaggle_mh__registry_annual
nodes.rationale: Concept PopulationStatistic; grain: one statistic x year x sex x ICD-10 group. CSO Ireland HRA71 via Kaggle, 2001-2023. NULL is a suppressed or not-applicable cell - never zero-fill.

nodes.label: stg_kaggle_mh__screening_assessments
nodes.rationale: Concept ScreeningAssessment; grain: one behavioural screening of one person. Behavioural screening vs expert diagnosis; cohort unrelated to treatment_episodes patients.

nodes.label: stg_kaggle_mh__survey_responses
nodes.rationale: Concept SurveyResponse; grain: one survey response as published upstream. Respondents are anonymous public, never Patients. Upstream heavily duplicated (292364 rows, ~580 distinct); deduplicated by content_hash in the mart.

nodes.label: stg_kaggle_mh__treatment_episodes
nodes.rationale: Concept TreatmentEpisode; grain: one treatment episode per patient. Synthetic outpatient monitoring; episode-grain snapshot - scores are point-in-time, not longitudinal.

nodes.label: kaggle_mh dbt source
nodes.rationale: Raw data landed by dlt. Schema owned by the source.

nodes.label: metricflow_time_spine
nodes.rationale: Daily time spine required by MetricFlow; standard granularity column date_day; materialized table.

nodes.label: dbt_date 0.21.0 (pinned)
nodes.rationale: Present only in the lock, not packages.yml - transitive dependency.

nodes.label: mental_health dbt profile
nodes.rationale: dev/ci/base targets are a local DuckDB file via PF_DUCKDB_PATH; prod is ducklake:DUCKLAKE_METADATA with ducklake+httpfs extensions and DUCKLAKE_THREADS default 1. env_var indirection keeps credentials out of the committed file.

nodes.label: elementary edr profile (mental-health, derived)
nodes.rationale: DERIVED from the project profile by pf tool elementary - one output per target, schema suffixed _elementary the way dbt composes custom schemas. Regenerated by pf bootstrap; retarget the project, not this block.

nodes.label: Generated expectations (role-derived tests)
nodes.rationale: Every GENERATED-marker sql here derives from the ontology: contracts/annotations.yaml maps columns to roles and pf bootstrap translates roles into dbt-expectations tests. Edit the roles, not the files - regeneration discards edits. Sharper one-table expectations go in that model's own yml.

nodes.label: hospital_shared dbt project
nodes.rationale: Macro-paths-only shared dbt project: the hospital group's conformed-dimension/macro package shared by sister projects.

nodes.label: hospital: elementary tool enabled
nodes.rationale: Group-level enablement: every hospital sister inherits; a project tools.yaml can override, including off. Enabled-but-not-installed is skipped with a note - enabling is a project decision, installing a laptop fact.

nodes.label: jaffle group
nodes.rationale: One sister (jaffle-shop); ontology classes in scope: Customer, Order, Payment, Refund, Product, Location. Sisters share ontology, conformed dimensions and group metrics but have separate warehouses and run in parallel.

nodes.label: Rollup READ_ONLY ATTACH pattern
nodes.rationale: Cross-entity questions are answered only in the group-rollup project, which attaches sister databases READ_ONLY. Never read a sister project's files from another project.

nodes.label: DuckLake production warehouse
nodes.rationale: Prod runs on DuckLake; one set of models serves dev and prod. DATA_PATH is fixed when the lake is created - moving it is a data migration. A .ducklake file catalog resolves concurrent DDL by failing one side, so threads default to 1. No OpenMetadata connector yet, so the target is uncatalogued. Deliberately no shortcut: DBT_TARGET=prod is named on every invocation because believing you are on dev while on prod is the failure mode.

nodes.label: Development stays on DuckDB
nodes.rationale: A developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project. Every target but prod is a local DuckDB file - laptop, offline, no credentials, seconds. base exists so Recce has a second state to diff against. Nothing in this capability can move dev, ci or base, by construction.

nodes.label: sf_* macro dialect dispatch
nodes.rationale: Macros in platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake dispatch per adapter, so a model is written once and compiles to whatever the target understands.

nodes.label: Credentials via environment
nodes.rationale: DUCKLAKE_METADATA required; DUCKLAKE_SCHEMA and DUCKLAKE_THREADS optional. Read from the environment at run time and never written to a file - profiles.yml holds env_var calls, not values, because it is committed. pf doctor reports what is missing.

nodes.label: Dev database served over quack
nodes.rationale: Development builds into one DuckDB file; served, every reader - MCP tools, previews, sister roll-ups, any DuckDB client - reaches it over DuckDB's quack protocol instead of opening the file. Generated by pf bootstrap from pf.scaffold.generator; runtime is pf.runtime.quack; guardrails enforced, not advisory.

nodes.label: Write-window borrowing
nodes.rationale: Writers never queue behind readers: dbt, dlt, MetricFlow, Elementary and Recce borrow the file for exactly the duration of a run (pf.runtime.quack.write_window) and the server resumes behind them.

nodes.label: jaffle-shop Evidence report config
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf report build. Both plugin sections are load-bearing: without components, Evidence injectComponents() discovers zero component plugins and every generated page dies with QueryViewer not defined, because the preprocessor wraps each sql fence in one.

nodes.label: CVD-validated chart palette
nodes.rationale: Palette values are validated: adjacent-pair CVD deltaE >= 8, normal-vision >= 15, contrast checked on both surfaces. Re-picking them by eye makes charts unreadable for ~8% of readers.

nodes.label: jaffle_shop dbt profile
nodes.rationale: dev/ci/base local DuckDB via PF_DUCKDB_PATH; prod ducklake:DUCKLAKE_METADATA with ducklake+httpfs; same generated shape as sister projects.

nodes.label: elementary edr profile (jaffle-shop, derived)
nodes.rationale: Derived from the project profile by pf tool elementary; regenerated by pf bootstrap.

nodes.label: Policy and Evidence Register (policy.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Closes the gap intent -> constraint -> artifact -> evidence. Rules had lived in three disconnected places - prose in a skill, an if-statement in validate.py, a dbt test - with nothing linking the reason to the check to the proof. Every policy names the artifact that enforces it and the evidence that proves it ran; pf policy status walks the chain and unenforced policies are the interesting output.

nodes.label: Traceability chain: intent -> constraint -> artifact -> evidence
nodes.rationale: OpenTopology's contribution is not entity-relationship modelling; it is this chain.
nodes.norm_label: traceability chain: intent -> constraint -> artifact -> evidence

nodes.label: Evidence kinds register
nodes.rationale: The evidence kinds the chain may reference, each marked durable or derived. An evidence entry naming something not listed is itself a finding - how the chain stays honest.

nodes.label: Policy: money-requires-currency
nodes.rationale: A monetary amount without its currency is not a number, it is a bug waiting for a second entity to be onboarded.

nodes.label: Policy: entity-requires-identity
nodes.rationale: A class with no identity property cannot participate in a derived join, so every BI and MDL projection of it is a guess.

nodes.label: Policy: link-must-be-in-topology
nodes.rationale: A foreign key pointing at a class the topology does not relate to is an undeclared join - how two teams compute different revenue from the same warehouse.

nodes.label: Policy: pii-not-in-consumption
nodes.rationale: PII may land in raw and staging but must not reach a mart or exposure without a masking policy or an explicit recorded waiver.

nodes.label: Policy: mart-declares-grain
nodes.rationale: Grain is the one fact a downstream consumer cannot infer and cannot survive guessing; an undeclared grain is how a join silently fans out.

nodes.label: Policy: metric-owns-aggregation
nodes.rationale: Aggregation policy belongs to exactly one metric definition; a mart column named revenue is a second definition that will drift from the first.

nodes.label: Policy: change-declares-blast-radius
nodes.rationale: A model or column change must report what it breaks before it lands, including the human who owns each affected exposure.

nodes.label: Policy: change-verified-against-baseline
nodes.rationale: Blast radius is a prediction from lineage; a mart change must also be compared against a built baseline - otherwise safe means nothing references it, not nothing changed.

nodes.label: Policy: review-artifacts-exclude-pii
nodes.rationale: A value-level diff writes the rows it compared into durable shared review state; diffing a PII-role column persists real addresses into a committed artefact.

nodes.label: Policy: builds-record-observability
nodes.rationale: Every build records run and test results into the warehouse with history, for every test framework at once - new, recurring or flaky is a query, not an archaeology dig.

nodes.label: Policy: quality-floor-derived-from-ontology
nodes.rationale: The quality floor is derived from ontology roles, so coverage is a function of annotation rather than memory and a wrong test is a wrong role rather than a stale file.

nodes.label: Policy: secrets-never-in-context
nodes.rationale: A credential placed in a prompt, model file or committed artefact is durably persisted and replayed into every later session.

nodes.label: Policy: agent-authority-is-least-privilege
nodes.rationale: Least privilege that lives in a prompt is a request; in a denylist it is a control.

nodes.label: Policy: tool-contribution-may-only-tighten
nodes.rationale: Tool.gate_sections rejects a contribution to any loosening section at construction, so an unsafe tool fails at import rather than silently permitting more.

nodes.label: Policy: agent-decisions-are-recorded
nodes.rationale: Every tool call is written down before and after it happens, and the gate verdict is recorded for allows as well as denies.

nodes.label: Policy: evidence-chain-is-tamper-evident
nodes.rationale: A log an agent can edit is not evidence: each record carries the hash of the one before, and the head is countersigned by an external timestamp authority.

nodes.label: Policy: sister-projects-are-isolated
nodes.rationale: Business logic does not transfer between entities; an assumption carried across sisters is a bug by construction. A project session may not read or write another project, nor write shared infra.

nodes.label: Policy: agent-authority-is-revocable
nodes.rationale: A control that cannot be switched off mid-incident is found out about afterwards. Revocation is checked before intent is written; an unreadable revocation file fails closed.

nodes.label: Policy: high-impact-actions-need-a-human
nodes.rationale: Approvals are append-only and bound to the action they approve; an actor approving their own action is a finding, not an approval.

nodes.label: Policy: model-routing-is-declared
nodes.rationale: Which model answers which step is a declared table, not whatever the caller passed; an unregistered step is recorded as such.

nodes.label: Policy: upstream-licences-are-reviewed
nodes.rationale: Every vendored upstream carries a licence review written down per upstream and surfaced in the listing - a constraint is a fact in the registry, not something someone once checked.

nodes.label: Policy: dev-serving-wire-is-read-only
nodes.rationale: The server holds the database read-only so the engine refuses writes at the catalog; the client refuses non-read statements before the network hop using DuckDB's own parser. Writers borrow the file through the write window and never meet the wire.

nodes.label: Policy: dev-server-binds-localhost-only
nodes.rationale: The host is not a parameter of the serving path, so a routable dev server cannot be configured into existence - only programmed, which is a review event rather than config drift.

nodes.label: Policy: quack-token-never-leaves-the-machine
nodes.rationale: The serving token is generated fresh per server, lives in a 0600 gitignored state file, is denied to agent edits by the gate, and is redacted from CLI output by default.

nodes.label: Policy: warehouse-custody-is-recorded
nodes.rationale: Serving, stopping and borrowing are full chained provenance actions - who held the warehouse when is a query over records; a revoked ledger refuses the custody change.

nodes.label: Policy: control-baseline-is-declared
nodes.rationale: Each entity declares in air.yaml which controls it commits to; those are derived from the repository on every run and block the merge when they fail. Deliberately maps to no AIR control - that would be the category error the catalogue exists to stop.

nodes.label: dltHub AI Workbench (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Toolkit/skill layout and the annotate-then-generate ingest flow the ontology layer is built on. Proprietary dltHub License scoped to dltHub Services; our dlt toolkits are independent rewrites against dlt Core's public API, the submodule pinned for reference and drift detection only - counsel before shipping externally.

nodes.label: dbt Agent Skills (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: dbt Labs' account of how an agent drives dbt, rewritten for dbt Core + dbt-duckdb. Origin of the ratio-metric rule (carry numerator and denominator, never average a ratio), now enforced in the report audit. Apache-2.0.

nodes.label: DuckDB Quack (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: The client-server protocol pf quack serve puts in front of each project's dev DuckDB file. Pin is the reference source for wire behaviour - what quack_serve, quack_query and the client ATTACH can and cannot carry; the experimental client ATTACH cannot carry schema DDL, hence quack_query passthrough plus write windows. MIT.

nodes.label: DuckDB Skills (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: DuckDB's own guidance on driving DuckDB from an agent; our ports are read-only and truncated by policy (schema plus <=20 rows). Session state moved into the project so a sister's ATTACH cannot leak. MIT.

nodes.label: Dagster Skills (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Asset-first orchestration idioms; @dbt_assets with a custom translator is what makes lineage cross the dlt/dbt boundary instead of collapsing into one opaque node. Apache-2.0.

nodes.label: Loop Engineering (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: The governance shape for scheduled agent work: durable state, path gate, token budget, circuit breaker, autonomy ladder. Upstream's gate is advisory; ours is a PreToolUse hook, so the denylist is structural. Direct ancestor of the vendor-drift loop: report upstream movement, never apply it. MIT.

nodes.label: Evidence BI (dbt semantic layer edition) (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: BI as a projection of the semantic layer, not a second place metrics live. Every query compiles from a metric definition; hand-written page queries are flagged as second definitions. No LICENSE upstream - treated as reference only, nothing copied.
nodes.norm_label: evidence bi (dbt semantic layer edition) (vendored upstream)

nodes.label: Microsoft Ontology Playground (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Working reference for business ontology shape - classes with identity, datatype and object properties - plus RDF/XML round-trip fidelity. Ours matched its Customer/Order/Payment core rather than inventing a vocabulary. MIT.

nodes.label: OpenTopology (otop-core) (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: The traceability chain intent -> constraint -> artifact -> evidence. Our policy layer is emitted as an otop 0.2 manifest validated against the vendored schema; relationship vocabulary (governed_by, implemented_by, verified_by) taken verbatim. Apache-2.0.

nodes.label: WrenAI (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: MDL as the interchange format BI and text-to-SQL consume. Field names and the cardinality enum come from the vendored schema, not memory - layoutVersion was once guessed wrong, which is why the schema is vendored. Apache-2.0 core, CC-BY-4.0 docs.

nodes.label: AWS Context Ontology Accelerator (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Scan -> Model -> Serve induction with a steward in the middle: induction proposes, a person decides. Scan reads statistics rather than names; every axiom carries observed evidence. Apache-2.0.

nodes.label: Recce (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: The empirical half of impact analysis: the graph answers what could break, Recce answers what did change by diffing the built warehouse against a baseline. Declined --cloud (data residency is not an agent decision) and top_k_diff (DeepDiff ignore_order makes a category rename invisible - verified against a real rename; a keyed query_diff surfaces it instead). Reference implementation of the pf.tools contract. Apache-2.0.

nodes.label: Recce Claude Plugin (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Upstream's own account of how an agent drives Recce, ported to our toolkit format. Kept its stopping rule: a diff you cannot explain is a finding, not noise. Declined its hooks/permissions - a second hook system is how a gate gets two answers. MIT.

nodes.label: Recce PR-Update (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Composite action keeping a PR branch merged with its base - the precondition for trusting any CI diff. Generated with autoMerge false: an agent reports, a human merges. MIT.

nodes.label: Forge (wss3-forge) (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: The control plane's component layer and design tokens; ships its own Claude Code skill pack read verbatim at authoring time. Motion declined on data tables - animated rows cost reading time. MIT.

nodes.label: Next.js shadcn Admin Dashboard (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Adopted for layout and theming decisions only - sidebar-plus-topbar shell, grouped navigation. The Next.js app itself declined: every screen reads local FastAPI on localhost, and a login form over no authentication would imply a boundary that is not there. MIT.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Standards (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Entity JSON Schemas our catalogue payloads validate against in the test suite, so an upstream field becoming required breaks the build at the pin bump instead of against a live catalogue. Apache-2.0.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: The catalogue for people who do not read YAML; worth integrating for the dbt connector, which produces column-level lineage from manifest.json and catalog.json. Cloned shallow - full history exhausted the disk; pf vendor sync cannot count commits between pins for this upstream. Ingestion runs as a Dagster asset downstream of the marts, not on OpenMetadata's own Airflow. Apache-2.0.

nodes.label: ASQAV Compliance Scanner (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: Static second opinion on agent governance: reads agent source for five controls (audit trail, policy enforcement, revocation, human oversight, error handling) mapped to EU AI Act, DORA, ISO 42001. Score deliberately not a merge gate - it is regex over source. Elastic-2.0: must not be exposed as a compliance-scanning feature to tenants; runtime SDK declined because it ships actions to a hosted service.

nodes.label: Public Sector AI Playbook (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: The governance artefacts a regulated deployment must produce - model card, bias audit, risk register - mapped to the UK AI Playbook 2025 and EU AI Act. Carried rather than copied: templates belong to a deployment, and this platform is multi-tenant. CC BY 4.0 - attribution (Linda Oraegbunam) travels with each derived artefact.

nodes.label: FINOS AI Governance Framework (vendored upstream)
nodes.rationale: The risk taxonomy and control catalogue - 23 risks and 23 controls with stable AIR-* ids, each cross-walked to EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST, OWASP and more; six risks are specifically agentic. Read as data at runtime so an upstream rename is a build failure, not a rotting mapping. Pinned remote is a byte-identical fork so upstream changes land as reviewed merges. Pluggable CatalogueSource - nothing in the parser, coverage, gate or CLI names FINOS. CC BY 4.0; pf air refuses to write a register without the credit line.

nodes.label: Committer
nodes.rationale: Commit segregation by a locally served model (local weights, no tokens, no code leaving the machine) so the session implementing logic never spends attention on git splits. The model proposes groups of files and a message each as JSON only; everything around the proposal is deterministic and not the model's to decide. A plan that fails validation is printed and dropped; a hallucinated path is an error message, not a staged change.

nodes.label: Division of Labor
nodes.rationale: The model's authority is confined to judgment (grouping and wording, JSON only — it runs no command and touches no file); git performs survey and apply, validate_plan enforces the wall, provenance records. Survey lists untracked changes individually and keeps submodule-internal churn invisible.

nodes.label: Commit Plan Validation Wall
nodes.rationale: Deterministic wall between the model's opinion and the index: every change assigned exactly once; invented paths refused; vendor/** and .gitmodules refused because a pin bump is a human decision; gate-denied paths refused. Failing plans are printed and dropped rather than partially applied.

nodes.label: Plan Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: The saved plan carries a fingerprint of the tree it described; any edit, commit or new file invalidates it, so --apply can never commit a split that was reviewed against a different tree (it re-plans if the tree moved).

nodes.label: Local Backend Fallback
nodes.rationale: A local server that is down is an everyday state, not an error: the call falls through to headless claude -p --model haiku when that CLI is installed, and only fails when neither answers. Whichever backend answered is the name in the trailer. Trap: a stale ANTHROPIC_API_KEY shadows a claude.ai login and the CLI 401s — the error surfaces the CLI's own words so this diagnoses itself.

nodes.label: Style Guide Seam
nodes.rationale: Twelve log subjects teach the model less than a curated page: if docs/COMMIT-STYLE.md exists (location overridable via PF_COMMIT_STYLE_FILE), its first ~2,500 characters are injected into the commit-plan prompt as authoritative house conventions for grouping and message style. Absent, empty, or unreadable means no section, never an error. Integration point for externally curated knowledge (NotebookLM included, export-based since it has no API and sits behind Google sign-in). The guide informs the model's judgment only; the validation wall, gate and provenance are unchanged by anything the file says.

nodes.label: Session-End Automation
nodes.rationale: .claude/settings.json carries a Stop hook running pf git-doctor --from-hook --apply then pf commit --from-hook --auto. Both are no-ops unless PF_AUTO_COMMIT=1, so unarmed they stay deliberate commands. The doctor runs first on purpose: a drifted pin or stale plan would otherwise pollute the commit survey it feeds.

nodes.label: Git Doctor
nodes.rationale: Extends the committer's division of labor from pending work to wrong states: submodule checkouts off their recorded pin, nested submodules initialized inside vendored checkouts, stale commit plans, conflicts, gate-denied paths git tracks anyway. Deterministic scanners find findings; the local model's entire authority is choosing a remedy per finding from a closed menu — it composes no command, ever.

nodes.label: Closed Remedy Menu
nodes.rationale: The model chooses only from an enumerated menu per finding kind. Permanent prohibitions no finding can unlock: pin bumps, history rewrites (reset --hard, rebase, force-push, amend), gate bypasses (--no-verify), edits under vendor/** or .gitmodules, anything in provenance/** or .git/, and merge resolution — the only answer for those is leave. An off-menu resolution is rejected before anything runs.

nodes.label: Import-Cycle Guard
nodes.rationale: The circular-import invariant is held twice at different hardnesses: a pytest wall that fails the suite (and the merge, since pytest platform/tests gates it) on any real cross-module cycle, and the doctor's graph-backed eye. Deliberately no hand-written PR workflow: .github/workflows/** is gate-denied to agents and generated per project from capability ci_jobs — the wall rides the existing platform test job, the same enforcement with none of the drift.

nodes.label: Doctor's Graph-Backed Eye
nodes.rationale: When graphify-out/graph.json exists, pf git-doctor reports import-cycle findings from the knowledge graph's directed imports edges (capped at 10, calls recursion ignored). It is leave-only: breaking a cycle is authorship, so the model names the knot and hands it to a human.

nodes.label: pf commit
nodes.rationale: The seam: pf commit proposes and saves the plan; --apply makes exactly the saved plan's commits (re-plans if the tree moved); --auto plans and applies in one shot for hooks and scripts.

nodes.label: pf.gitdoctor.RULEBOOK
nodes.rationale: The detailed rule is written down, not implied: pf git-doctor --rules prints the rulebook, the exact text the model receives. It enumerates the menu per finding kind and the permanent prohibitions.

nodes.label: mlx_lm.server
nodes.rationale: Default backend (any OpenAI-compatible server works — LM Studio :1234, Ollama :11434/v1), serving Qwen with thinking disabled. Measured on this task, a reasoning-enabled Qwen spends its entire token budget thinking and returns a message with no content at all (finish_reason='length'), so the switch is not an optimisation.

nodes.label: claude -p headless CLI
nodes.rationale: Fallback backend: headless claude -p --model haiku, forced via PF_COMMIT_BACKEND=claude or reached when the local server is down.

nodes.rationale: platform/src/pf/ontology/policy.yaml — where the committer's and doctor's named policies live, resolving under pf air coverage.

nodes.label: platform/tests/test_import_cycle_guard.py
nodes.rationale: The wall: walks the real module-level imports of platform/src/pf and fails the suite (and the merge) on any cross-module cycle. Function-scope imports and the parent-package re-export idiom are exempt — they are the sanctioned ways to break a cycle, not instances of one.

nodes.label: Stop Hook
nodes.rationale: Carried by .claude/settings.json: runs pf git-doctor --from-hook --apply, then pf commit --from-hook --auto at session end; a no-op unless PF_AUTO_COMMIT=1.

nodes.label: Commit-Split-By Trailer
nodes.rationale: Attribution in the commit message itself; whichever backend answered is the name in the trailer.

nodes.label: Provenance Ledger
nodes.rationale: One action per commit (sha in the execution record); each doctor remedy is also a provenance action. Its kill switch is honoured by construction — a revoked ledger refuses the action record, and with it the commit.

nodes.label: Pre-Commit Impact Gate
nodes.rationale: Inherited rather than implemented by the committer: the pre-commit hook still blocks a breaking change on every commit the committer makes.

nodes.label: NotebookLM
nodes.rationale: Has no API and sits behind Google sign-in, so the flow is export-based: produce the git-conventions guide in the notebook, export it as Markdown, save it as docs/COMMIT-STYLE.md; the next pf commit reads it automatically.

nodes.label: ci_jobs Capability
nodes.rationale: .github/workflows/** is gate-denied to agents and generated per project from capability ci_jobs; the pytest wall rides the existing platform test job — the same enforcement with none of the drift of a hand-written PR workflow.

nodes.label: commit-plans-are-validated-not-trusted
nodes.rationale: Named policy: the deterministic wall between the model's opinion and the index.

nodes.label: llm-commits-are-recorded-and-attributed
nodes.rationale: Named policy: provenance action per commit, model named in the message.

nodes.label: git-repair-is-a-closed-menu
nodes.rationale: Named policy: an off-menu doctor resolution is rejected before anything runs.

nodes.label: Git Doctor Finding Kinds
nodes.rationale: Submodule checkouts off their recorded pin, nested submodules initialized inside vendored checkouts, stale commit plans, conflicts, gate-denied paths git tracks anyway, and (graph-backed) import-cycle.

nodes.label: leave Remedy
nodes.rationale: Hands the finding to a human with a stated reason; the only answer for the permanent prohibitions, and the default for findings the model omits.
